title: After The General's first Love Returns
author: 宇宙第一红
synopsis:
It took Bai Qingning three years to marry her husband, and she realized that she had never been in his heart.

After her husband's beloved Zhao Hongzhu returned, he ignored her and even killed her. He sought a position for a newcomer, but his relatives watched coldly. His loyal servants were displaced and separated, and when he was about to die, he even brought her mute slave to die with him.

With one more eye open, Bai Qingning returned to the year Zhao Hongzhu had just returned.

She used every possible means, bit by bit, to drag all the scumbags and bitches into the endless abyss, and then she relaxed and separated, picked up her mute slave and took good care of him.

And the slave? He was a lowly creature who had fallen into a ditch, a slave who had never seen light, and she was his moonlight. A moonlight he did not dare to look at with his eyes, fearing that the moonlight would see the greed he tried to hide, so he lowered his head and looked at the moon's shadow in the cup. But he had a secret. Maybe one day he can look directly at the moon.

chapters.title: One
chapters.content:
The twelfth lunar month brought bitter winter cold, with the north wind howling fiercely.



At the foot of the Qin family mountain in the outskirts of the capital, a famished wildcat took advantage of the night, darting across the desolate courtyard. Stepping over broken tiles to the sounds of someone's sick coughing from within, it slipped into the back kitchen and quietly scratched at the drafty sandalwood door with its claws.



The sick coughing inside paused for a moment, followed by the sound of fabric rustling and the bed frame creaking—sounds not entirely clear amid the wind and snow. Yet the person in the back kitchen set down the medicinal soup they were brewing and quickly rose to walk toward the adjacent room.



The wildcat had just entered through the door and immediately dove under a broken cabinet. As it did so, it locked eyes with that person for a brief moment.



This was a terrifying-looking person, dressed in a short hemp garment, their face covered in scars that made them appear fierce and frightening. Their eyes were especially sharp and cold, like those of an extremely vicious beast from the wilderness.



The wildcat knew this person was called Mute Slave. Ever since they had arrived, Mute Slave often hunted in the mountains. The wild chickens and rabbits in the hills had nearly been caught to extinction by him, and even wild boars had been killed by his hand.



The wildcat curled up in fear, trying to bare its teeth, but Wuyan paid it no mind. Instead, he strode out quickly and entered the main room at a swift pace.



When the door to the main room opened, the wildcat heard a trembling voice—a woman's voice that fell lighter than the snow outside. She asked: "A'Nu, has the General come to fetch me?"



Mute Slave, who had just entered, paused mid-step, then walked in with his usual measured gait, standing silently in the room for a moment before making a few hand gestures.



When the wildcat emerged with half a wild chicken leg in its mouth, it glimpsed through the door crack the appearance of the woman inside.



She was a woman lying in bed, beset by chronic illness, yet her sickness could not conceal her delicate beauty. Every gesture carried an innate nobility—truly her brows and eyes were like green lotus, her fragrant neck like congealed frost and snow.



"The General hasn't come." Bai Qingning lifted her face, her eyes filled with despair. She looked at the silent Mute Slave, her upright spine gradually drooping as if about to be crushed by the weight of her illness, tears brimming in her eyes.



Mute Slave continued making hand gestures, but she no longer looked. She lowered her head, gazing at her own wrist, and after a long while, actually began to laugh softly.



"Don't lie to me anymore," she said. "I know the General won't come."



Mute Slave's movements froze.



At the same time, a tear slid down from the corner of Bai Qingning's eye and fell to the ground, splashing up a droplet of water.



As that tear fell, even the surrounding north wind seemed to quiet.



Between the color of snow and the color of moonlight, that was the third kind of exquisite beauty.



Bai Qingning seemed utterly exhausted. She closed her eyes and fell back into unconsciousness, leaving only Mute Slave standing alone at the door.



At that moment, under the dark moon and fierce wind, with only a single candlelight illuminating the room, the man standing at the door was like a lurking beast. He stood respectfully with his hands folded, his scarred face hidden in the dim light, only his eyes fixed steadily on the person sleeping on the bed.



As if drawn by some fatal allure, Mute Slave had somehow already moved to the bedside. His hand hovered beside Bai Qingning's moist eye corner, as if to wipe away her tears.



The moonlight from outside the window fell upon his hand and her face, as if pouring out a Milky Way between them, briefly giving Mute Slave an opportunity to touch her. But Mute Slave suddenly snapped awake as if scorched by fire, hastily stood up, stepped back two paces, and stood off to the side.



The moonlight illuminated Mute Slave's fierce face, also reflecting his deep, heavy eyes.



After standing for a moment, he slowly crouched down, took out a white embroidered handkerchief from his pocket, wiped up that single tear from the ground, then folded the handkerchief and gently placed it against his chest.

Just then, sounds came from outside the door. Mute Slave quickly stood up, glanced at the person still unconscious on the bed, then strode quickly toward the door.



—--



Bai Qingning was awakened by a commotion.



Her health was poor, and she felt heavy with illness all day long, like cotton soaked through with water. When she heard the commotion outside the door, she thought it was a dream at first, but as the noise grew louder and louder, she realized it was real.



It must be the General who had come. The General had said that after some time passed, he would definitely come to take her back.



Bai Qingning rose from the bed with joy, dragging her ailing body toward the door.



But when she reached the door, she heard a haughty scolding: "Where did this dog slave come from, daring to block the General's residence's path and obstruct the General's wife's business? Come, beat him!"



The General's wife?



Bai Qingning pushed at the wooden door in bewilderment, thinking—she was the General's wife, when had she ever instructed anyone to do anything?



Her fingertips, delicate as scallion shoots, pushed the wooden door open a crack. The north wind and heavy snow swept in together, blowing up Bai Qingning's dark hair behind her. Through the crack in the door, she saw the steward matron from the Qin residence who served at the old madam's side.



The last time Bai Qingning had seen her was three months ago, when Bai Qingning left the Qin residence.



At that time, her husband Qin Shanyue had just returned victorious from battle. She had waited in anticipation for so long, only to see her husband bring back another woman. Yet she couldn't even be angry or jealous.



Because that woman was called Zhao Hongzhu, the General's originally betrothed wife.



And also because her marriage was something Zhao Hongzhu had "given" to her, so she had no right to criticize Zhao Hongzhu.



Three years ago, Zhao Hongzhu, the daughter of Prime Minister Zhao's family, and General Qin Shanyue of the Qin family had been deeply in love, stronger than gold. Everyone said they were a perfectly matched couple. Qin Shanyue had proposed marriage to the Zhao family, but the Zhao family suddenly became implicated in a major treason case and was punished by the Emperor. From then on, the Zhao family members either died or were injured. They only had time to hastily send the women of the household to the northern desert under the excuse of illness to escape disaster. The marriage between Zhao Hongzhu and Qin Shanyue became like a bubble in water, quietly dissolving into nothing.



It so happened that the General's mother became gravely ill, fearing she wouldn't live to see her son marry. The General couldn't wait any longer, and the Bai family wanted to curry favor with the Qin family, so they actively approached the Qin family, willing to marry Bai Qingning to them.



Bai Qingning was inferior to Zhao Hongzhu in every way. Her birth was inferior—she was born of a concubine while Zhao Hongzhu was legitimate. She wasn't as beautiful as Zhao Hongzhu, her talents weren't as brilliant as Zhao Hongzhu's, and she was cautious and timid, far from Zhao Hongzhu's intelligence and magnanimity. Moreover, she had been actively offered up by the Bai family when the Qin family couldn't find anyone for a rush wedding to bring joy. The three letters and six etiquettes were all conducted in great haste. Outsiders all mocked her for her lack of self-respect, so her value kept dropping again and again. After arriving at the Qin household, she wasn't liked anywhere, so she could only yield in everything and humble herself.



Fortunately, later she worked hard to win over the General. After their marriage, they treated each other with mutual respect, and the General gradually forgot about Zhao Hongzhu and came to love her. Only then did she gradually become happy.



The General had said that having her was a blessing, and the General promised her they would be a couple for life, just the two of them.



But later, there was a military conflict in the northern desert, and the Emperor sent the General to suppress it. When the General returned this time, he overturned the case against the Zhao family and brought back Zhao Hongzhu, who had been recuperating in the northern desert.



After Zhao Hongzhu returned, the General became distracted and absent-minded. He hadn't even visited her room once. At a banquet, she even caught the General having a secret meeting with Zhao Hongzhu. After she discovered them, the General stopped coming to see her altogether.

Later, she sought help from her natal family, but the Bai family only wanted to curry favor with the General. They even demanded that she voluntarily request a divorce. However, she later accidentally fell into water and nearly died, leaving her bedridden with severe illness, so the Bai family stopped mentioning the matter.



After that, the General told her that the Qin family had many affairs recently and she wasn't recovering well, so he had her go to the Qin family's ancestral home to recuperate. He said the ancestral home was quiet and peaceful, and once she recovered, he would bring her back.



The Qin family ancestral home was where she lived now, but this ancestral home had long fallen into disrepair and had no proper living quarters. She had originally brought six maids with her, but later they all found various reasons to return to the Qin residence. Some said they were going back to fetch things, others to inquire about matters for her, but after leaving, for some reason, none of them ever returned.



Only Mute Slave remained, whom she had picked up by the roadside two and a half months ago. He stayed with her and took care of her.



She had thought the General would come to take her back, but when she saw the steward matron's entourage, she felt something wasn't right.



The door crack was blown open by the wind, and the wooden board struck Bai Qingning's shoulder with a "bang," surely leaving a bruise. But Bai Qingning had no time to worry about the stinging pain. She supported herself against the door in bewilderment, looking at the people in the courtyard.



Behind the steward matron were household guards from the Qin residence, holding torches and clubs in their hands, constantly charging inward. Mute Slave blocked the entrance, bare-handed, holding people back.



This was the first time Bai Qingning had seen Mute Slave fight. The howling wind couldn't cover the sound of his fists. Wooden clubs and torches were smashed apart by his fists. Mute Slave was like a fierce tiger entering a flock of sheep, pouncing to kill.



He was sharper than the north wind.



Someone shouted "bring out the blades," and Bai Qingning snapped back to her senses as if awakening. She screamed "Stop!" and tried to rush out the door, but stumbled as she lifted her foot and fell directly to her knees on the ground.



Her blue-green skirt spread across the ground like a fallen lotus flower. Snowflakes landed in her dark hair, gravel scraped her palms, but Bai Qingning couldn't care about any of it. Coughing in the north wind, she shouted: "How dare you! How dare you beat my servant and trespass in my residence! When the General finds out, he'll punish you all and have you thrown out of the household!"



She had thought that after she shouted, these people would restrain themselves or be afraid, but after her words fell, she heard the matron let out a mocking "Ha!"



"You still think you're the General's wife?" The matron raised her face, mockingly raising her voice to shout: "The General has already used his military merits to request an imperial decree of marriage from the Emperor. When Miss Zhao marries over, she will be the proper General's wife. You, a daughter born of a concubine, ignorant of propriety, rude and overbearing, relying on a stolen marriage to enjoy three years of wealth and glory—that's already an enormous grace! You really think you're worthy of the position of General's wife!"



Hearing the matron's words, Bai Qingning felt as if a bucket of cold water had been poured over her. She went numb, almost turning into an ice sculpture in this snowy night.



It wasn't until Mute Slave let out a muffled groan and stood before her covered in blood that Bai Qingning awoke as if from a dream.



"Impossible." Her tears rolled down like pearls: "The General still has a wife, how could the Emperor grant a marriage decree? I haven't committed any of the seven grounds for divorce, and the General hasn't divorced me. The General said he would come take me back."



"Precisely because you haven't committed any of the seven grounds for divorce and refuse to voluntarily request divorce, that's why I made this trip. You think I came to take you back? Ha, I came to send you to your death." The matron's lips, painted crimson with rouge, curved into a grin as she smiled viciously at Bai Qingning: "Only when you're dead can the General properly marry a new wife."

Bai Qingning's whole body trembled. She raised her head and looked at the matron in disbelief.



To marry another woman, the General actually wanted her dead.



"Impossible! I'm the Second Miss of the Bai family, you dare touch me! I want to see the General!" Bai Qingning struggled to get up from the ground, but she had just stood up when Mute Slave scooped her up with one hand, dragging her back into the room and slamming the wooden door shut.



"Ha, it was the General himself who sent this old slave here." Through the wooden door, Bai Qingning heard the matron shouting from the other side: "This trip, Miss Zhao gave this old slave a hundred taels of gold! This servant says, General's wife, you'd better wake up. The General has long since discussed with the Bai family about abandoning you. The General gave the Bai family enormous wealth, so naturally the Bai family doesn't want a concubine-born daughter like you. If the master hadn't nodded in approval, how would this servant dare to come? You're the one refusing a toast only to drink a forfeit. If you had voluntarily requested divorce earlier, why would you need to come to this end!"



The matron's voice was more chilling than the north wind outside. Bai Qingning was supported by Mute Slave's body, but she seemed like someone who had lost her soul, staring blankly as Mute Slave pushed the wooden bed over to block the door.



The people outside tried to break in, and Mute Slave used his own body to block them. The wounds on his body burst open, and the bloody scent splashed onto Bai Qingning's face, bringing her back to her senses.



"Mute Slave."



Mute Slave raised his sharp eyes and saw that jade-like person standing there, lips pale, saying lifelessly: "You should go. It's my life they want."



Mute Slave was pushing against the door and couldn't lift his hands. He couldn't make hand signs, so he could only look at her with furrowed brows.



Bai Qingning guessed that Mute Slave probably wanted to say: You saved my life, so I cannot leave.



Tears swirled in her eyes. In this moment, Bai Qingning hated Qin Shanyue and Zhao Hongzhu to her very bones.



This marriage had never been her wish—it was clearly fate playing tricks—yet everyone blamed her for it all, as if it was because of her that this outcome came to be. And they all took it for granted that she should step aside, that she should be grateful to hand over everything she had.



But what had she ever done wrong?



After arriving at the Qin household, she had diligently taken care of everyone, yet every single person looked down on her.



Even in death, only a mute slave accompanied her, and in the end, this mute slave would die because of her too.



At this moment, the smell of burning fire suddenly came from outside the door. Bai Qingning heard someone outside shouting "burn them to death." In a daze, Bai Qingning saw a beam overhead, long fallen into disrepair and now wrapped in flames, crashing down heavily toward her!



Bai Qingning retreated in fear, but there was no way to dodge. She only saw a figure lunge over, blocking her front, holding her as they both fell to the ground together.



This was the first time Bai Qingning had been so close to Mute Slave. She could hear his violent heartbeat, could smell the bloody scent on his body, could clearly see every scar on his face, and could look into the depths of his eyes.



Bai Qingning had thought his eyes should be fierce, cold and sharp. But unexpectedly, when their eyes met, those eyes were extraordinarily gentle, as if they held an entire galaxy of stars, reflecting Bai Qingning's face.



She saw his lips move, then he reached out his hand, tentatively touching the area below her eyelid. His warm fingers, bearing thin calluses, wiped across the tears on her cheek. But as he wiped away her tears, blood from his hand dripped down—no matter how he wiped, he couldn't wipe them clean.



Then, the burning beam overhead fell, and everything归于沉寂 returned to silence.



That night's fire lit up half the sky. That night's snow blanketed the entire mountain.



And only that night's north wind knew that what he wanted to say wasn't "you saved me, I cannot leave." From beginning to end, what he wanted to say was only two words.



Don't cry.



—--



In a confused daze, Bai Qingning had a dream, as if sinking and floating in a sea of sand, unable to catch a single breath.



Her whole body ached, her head was dizzy, and people around her were making noise. Everything from the past flashed through her mind like a scroll of paintings, until at a certain moment, someone beside her shook her awake forcefully.



"Madam!" Someone shouted urgently in her ear: "Please stop sleeping, something terrible has happened—the General has brought a woman back home!"

chapters.title: Two
chapters.content:
When Bai Qingning was shaken awake, she was still in a daze. Her eyes were unfocused as she looked around at her surroundings.



Before her eyes was a canopy embroidered with silver thread cicadas. She lay on a gold-inlaid jade bed fit for a noble lady. Outside the rosewood carved window, bright sunshine streamed in. It was currently the golden autumn of the ninth month. Outside the window, the cicadas had finished their song, leaving only the rustling autumn wind. Tree leaves were falling, making the chattering of the maid beside her seem even more clamorous.



"Madam! Please say something!" The maid was so anxious that even the hairpin flowers on her head were shaking. Speaking at lightning speed, she said: "Earlier, the household guards waiting at the city gate all sent word back. The matrons and maids outside all know now. I heard them say that woman is the eldest miss of the Zhao family. She rode on the same horse as the General, entering through the North Harmony Gate all the way in, making quite a spectacle! And the General didn't even return to our home—he went directly with the young miss to the old Zhao family residence!"



He was clearly the Qin family's General, yet the first thing he did upon returning to the capital was to ostentatiously bring another woman to someone else's residence—simply trampling Madam's dignity into the ground!



But no matter what the maid said, their mistress had no reaction whatsoever. For a moment, the maid thought their mistress had been struck so hard that she couldn't even speak.



The maid hesitantly wanted to console her with "all men in the world are fickle, three wives and four concubines is normal," but felt that would too greatly diminish their mistress's prestige. What sense was there in surrendering before the battle even began? Just as she was pondering whether to say it or not, she suddenly heard Madam call out in a trembling voice: "Qiuyue."



Bai Qingning's fingers tightly clutched the bed quilt embroidered with luxuriant flower clusters, her throat choking up.



This was Qiuyue—in her past life, her only truly devoted maid who had grown up with her. Later, because she was accused of stealing Zhao Hongzhu's belongings, she was beaten to death with rods. Bai Qingning hadn't even seen her corpse, not knowing to which mass grave it had been thrown.



The maid quickly raised her head: "This servant is here, Madam."



"What is today's date?" Bai Qingning asked in a trembling voice.



"In reply to Madam, it is the second day of the ninth month in the forty-sixth year of Yuanjia." The maid named Qiuyue nervously twisted her sleeves: "Madam, Madam, are you feeling confused, experiencing headaches and ringing in your ears, unable to remember things clearly?"



In earlier years, Qiuyue had heard of women who went mad after being abandoned. Their mistress loved the General so much—could she have also gone mad?



Sure enough, the next second, Qiuyue saw Bai Qingning abruptly rise from the bed. Without even fixing her hair and makeup, she lifted her feet and walked straight toward the door.



Qiuyue was so shocked she called out "Madam" repeatedly, but Bai Qingning paid no attention. Barefoot, holding up her skirt hem, she rushed out the door like a gust of wind.



Her pale tender feet hurriedly crossed the threshold, lightly landing under the corridor eaves. The autumn wind brushed past the upturned eaves, making the white jade wind chimes hanging outside the carved rosewood window frame ring, and also blowing through her hair that was like embroidered satin.



Bai Qingning gazed at this scenery from the past. In a trance, she didn't know whether she had been reborn or was having a dream of the afterlife. In any case, she had returned.



Returned to when Qin Shanyue had just brought Zhao Hongzhu back.



This was precisely her most difficult time. In her past life, it was at this very moment that she had blindly staked everything she had on a man, ultimately perishing in flames.



Love and hate waxed and waned against each other. Right now, she wished she could stab Qin Shanyue full of holes like a sieve!

—--

When Qiuyue ran up behind Bai Qingning and looked up, she was startled. Their mistress's face was already covered in tears, staring at the small autumn chrysanthemums in the courtyard with a look as if she wanted to chew those chrysanthemums to pieces!

"Madam?" Qiuyue almost wanted to run out to fetch a doctor, but then she saw their mistress stand up abruptly with a "whoosh." Her slender pale wrist resolutely wiped across her cheek, forcefully wiping away the tears as she commanded with determination: "Come dress and fix my hair, quickly!"



She had remembered—in her past life at this time, in another half month, she would rescue Mute Slave.



If she went earlier in this life, perhaps Mute Slave wouldn't get injured, and she could save him completely unharmed.



Mute Slave was the only person who stayed with her until the end in her past life. She absolutely could not let Mute Slave get hurt again.



As for Qin Shanyue, she would deal with him after she had saved Mute Slave!



Even as she spoke, Bai Qingning swiftly returned to her room, took out all the banknotes she had on hand, stuffed them all into a sachet, then turned to get her clothes.



Qiuyue thought Bai Qingning was going to the Bai family home to see the General, so she hurriedly cleansed her face. She had wanted to give Bai Qingning a dignified updo, but Bai Qingning couldn't wait. She did it herself, simply putting her hair up in a bun, pinning it with a silver hairpin, and headed straight for the door. Even her clothing was just a blue silk gauze robe embroidered with silver thread that she grabbed at random. Qiuyue was so anxious she stamped her feet, even calling out the name from before her marriage: "Second Miss, at least put on some lip rouge!"



When Bai Qingning heard "lip rouge," her vision blurred for a moment.



In her past life at this time, she had prepared her hair and makeup early, waiting from morning until afternoon. She hadn't even dared drink a sip of water, afraid of smudging her lip rouge or damaging her appearance, lest Qin Shanyue see her looking less than perfect. She had stubbornly waited at the door until late afternoon.



But Qin Shanyue hadn't looked at her at all. That day, Qin Shanyue's eyes were filled only with another woman.



The Bai Qingning of her past life didn't understand why, even after she had conceded to such an extent, those people still wanted to utterly destroy her. But the Bai Qingning of this life understood. From the very beginning, they had only treated her as a substitute, a cheap object that could be used in an emergency. But when the noble original returned, she was supposed to step aside, to be sealed away in the deepest recesses, never to see the sun again.



She was like a mistake—everyone wanted to erase her existence, leaving not even a trace behind, as if without her, these people would return to a time of peaceful years and everything going as they wished.



Living a second life, Bai Qingning had figured it out.



What she couldn't obtain in her past life, she wouldn't want in this life. Whoever wanted to be the General's wife of the Qin family could do it—she would no longer yearn for it.



She would never let herself become so bedraggled again.



But she wouldn't voluntarily request divorce. She would make Qin Shanyue and Zhao Hongzhu pay the price!



The grudges of her past life, she would avenge in this life!



Her blue skirt hem swept past the garden paths and fragrant wooden corridors. Bai Qingning walked from the front hall to the main gate. The main gate was bustling with activity—a group of maids and matrons stood at the entrance according to their status and rank. Upon seeing Bai Qingning's skirt hem, they immediately hurried to bow in respect.



"Greetings, Madam."



"Greetings, Madam."



While bowing, some bolder maids secretly raised their heads to peek at Bai Qingning.



Today, Madam had surprisingly not dressed up much. She only wore a cloud-blue robe embroidered with smoky clouds, her face bare of powder and rouge, her dark hair simply pinned up. Yet her brows and eyes were refined and otherworldly. Standing there under the corridor, she appeared even more pure and cold than the moon in the sky.



The maids only glanced once and didn't dare look again.



In the past, their General's wife had always been gentle and soft with people, her brows and eyes always carrying a shallow moist glow. She was a person like pearl and jade, without sharp edges. But today, Bai Qingning's dark brows were coldly pressed down, and an aura of fierceness surrounded her. Like an unsheathed sharp sword—cold, keen, and transparent—she pierced straight into people's eyes.

Some of the maids exchanged glances with each other, all understanding what was going on.



Ever since their General's residence received the victory report that the General would be returning late last month, Madam had been waiting and watching every day. Today the General had finally returned, yet he hadn't even entered the front gate of his home. Instead, he had brought his former fiancée Zhao Hongzhu to the old Zhao family residence.



It was said that their General had been devoted to Zhao Hongzhu in earlier years. Later, because Zhao Hongzhu met with disaster and was exiled to the northern desert, he was forced to marry Madam instead. Now that Zhao Hongzhu had returned, the General had cast Madam aside.



If it were them, they would naturally also be angry and upset.



Just at this moment, the gatekeeper came running from afar, shouting loudly: "The General says he's just escorting someone to the Zhao family and will return immediately—"



The gatekeeper's words had barely fallen when he saw their General's wife, surrounded by cold air, walking toward the gate. The gatekeeper hurriedly stepped aside.



When Bai Qingning reached the gate, everyone naturally made way for her, retreating behind her.



The Qin family had few descendants. In this generation, there was only one male heir, Qin Shanyue, so there was also only one wife—Bai Qingning. The old madam above was advanced in years and couldn't stand for long, so she hadn't come out to greet him. Thus the entire residence was filled with servants, with only Bai Qingning as the mistress. Naturally, she should be at the front.



When Bai Qingning had just reached the gate of the General's residence, she could see from afar other people standing on both sides of the road, mostly passersby or military officers.



They had all come to witness General Qin's prestige, but they didn't know that General Qin would not be coming back now. In fact, General Qin had practically forgotten where his own home was, only caring about going to the Zhao family to comfort his beloved.



As for returning immediately--



In her past life, Bai Qingning had waited a full two hours before he arrived, and he had even brought Zhao Hongzhu back with him. It was said that the Zhao ancestral home had been sealed, and Zhao Hongzhu had nowhere to stay, so she could only seek shelter at the Qin residence.



Bai Qingning let out a cold laugh. Naturally, she wouldn't wait again. She turned and said to those maids and matrons: "Alright, everyone disperse."



Then, under everyone's astonished gazes, Bai Qingning lifted her legs and walked out of the General's residence gate, heading outside.



"Madam, Madam! Where are you going? The General hasn't returned yet!" Outside the General's residence, Bai Qingning had already walked ten meters away when Qiuyue caught up with the other maids, just in time to see Bai Qingning walking resolutely outward.



"Are you going to the Bai family home?" Qiuyue nervously twisted her handkerchief: "The General will be angry! If you rashly go back like this—"



"I'm not going to the Bai residence, and don't call me Madam anymore from now on." Bai Qingning sent all the other maids away, only bringing Qiuyue with her. As she walked, she said: "Starting today, continue calling me Second Miss."



"Second Miss, where are we going?" Qiuyue was nearly in tears: "What exactly are you trying to do? Even if you're having a quarrel with the General, you can't run away from the residence!"



Bai Qingning reached her hand toward the silver in her sleeve pocket, took a deep breath, and said: "I'm going to Gongzi Yuan."



Qiuyue nearly fainted on the spot.



Gongzi Yuan? That was the most famous male courtesan house in all of the capital!



Was that a place Madam could go?



It's over, completely over.



Madam has gone mad! She's even going to Gongzi Yuan to consort with men!



The General finds women, Madam finds men—this, this!



Can this marriage even continue!

—--

On Qilin Street under the jurisdiction of the capital, sparrows flew over green tiles and white eaves. Bai Qingning, bringing along her maid who had nearly fainted three times along the way, passed through several streets and alleys and arrived at the entrance of a Gongzi Yuan.

That Gongzi Yuan was extremely luxurious, specially opened for women of prominent family backgrounds. The Yuanjia population was sparse and encouraged childbearing, so customs were open. Women could remarry twice or thrice, and if the woman's family was powerful, after losing her husband she could directly take male lovers without remarrying. Even after marriage, some would keep male lovers, so Gongzi Yuan was quite popular.



In her past life, it was at the entrance of this very Gongzi Yuan that Bai Qingning had found Mute Slave. At that time, Mute Slave had been thrown out and lay on the ground like a dead person. Bai Qingning had heard people say that Mute Slave had refused to submit to the end, and a client had ruined his face. His voice had been destroyed, and he'd been beaten half to death before being thrown out. Bai Qingning couldn't bear it at the time and picked him up.



When they arrived, inside Gongzi Yuan was filled with decadent music.



Qiuyue had steeled herself to follow Bai Qingning inside. As soon as the two entered, they were nearly lost in this sea of male beauty.



Balconies and pavilions, winding corridors and screens—upon entering Gongzi Yuan, there were twelve small compartments. In each compartment stood a man of decent appearance playing the zither, painting, brewing tea, or composing poetry. The female guests didn't linger in the main hall; almost all were in the elegant private rooms on the second floor.



As soon as Bai Qingning entered, a man with fox-like eyes walked over with a smile, asking in a soft voice: "You look unfamiliar, Miss. Is this your first time here? Why not go upstairs and sit? I'll play a tune for you?"



His manner was refined and courteous, not at all dissolute. Combined with his attractive appearance, he seemed quite appealing.



Bai Qingning was a sheltered young lady who hadn't seen much of the world. She should have been too embarrassed to lift her head, but she had died once before. As long as she didn't die, she didn't care, so she appeared exceptionally uninhibited. Her delicate small chin lifted as she said resolutely: "I want to buy a slave, buy one who just arrived. Take me to choose."



The man drew out a long "Ohh": "Understood. Miss wants to keep an outside residence? Come, this way please."



Bai Qingning lifted her feet and followed.



Behind her, Qiuyue's entire body was trembling.



Help, someone help!



A green hat is about to land on the General's head!



—--



The man led Bai Qingning through several beaded curtain corridors to a room. Inside were over a dozen men for Bai Qingning to inspect. With one glance, Bai Qingning knew none of them were right. She hesitated for a moment, then slipped this man twenty taels in banknotes.



"I'm looking for someone, this tall, very strong—"



She gestured for a while. The man seemed to know who she meant, saying quietly: "So Miss came for him. Tsk, what bad timing. A few days ago, his face was ruined."



Bai Qingning's heart tightened.



As he spoke, the man turned and led Bai Qingning deeper inside, saying as they walked: "Miss, don't be frightened. The scene isn't very pleasant."



They passed through several more rooms and finally arrived at a small, dark room that was shadowed and damp. Inside, there was the sound of coughing. As the man lifted the tattered cloth curtain for Bai Qingning, he said: "Hey, you in there, stop lying around. A customer has come to look at you."



Bai Qingning's heart was anxious. She lifted her feet and walked inside.



As soon as she entered, she smelled a foul, rank odor, like bedding that hadn't been changed in who knows how long, damp and infested with insects. The smell was so strong she could barely breathe. There were no candles lit in the room either—it was pitch dark, and she couldn't see anything.



She didn't have time to speak before she felt a gust of wind rush at her. The whole world spun around her, and she was directly pinned to the ground.

An iron hand gripped her throat tightly. A man had pinned her to the ground.



Up close, Bai Qingning finally saw those familiar eyes.



They were a pair of beautiful phoenix eyes, but there was no gentleness in them—only heavy wariness and hatred. His face had wounds where flesh had been sliced open and rolled back. Some wounds had festered with pus. Fresh blood dripped from his face and splashed onto Bai Qingning's face.



Familiar blood, familiar angle. Bai Qingning's nose tingled, tears nearly falling.



"If you're afraid, get lost." Bai Qingning heard him speak.



"If you dare buy me, I'll strangle you to death."



How wonderful, Bai Qingning thought. You can still speak.



"A'Nu, don't be afraid," Bai Qingning said.



The room that day was as damp as usual. Outside, another foolish customer had come. Shen Shizou's whole body burned with fever, but he forced himself to make threats. Outside, someone lifted the curtain to watch his humiliation. Through the lifted curtain, a bit of light shone in, illuminating the face of the woman lying on the ground.



It was a face of absolute beauty. Ten thousand shades of gorgeous red could not compare to the cinnabar mark between her brows. There was no disdain or mockery on that face. Those eyes held tears, and that gaze passed through icebergs and snow, through blazing beams and a time of complete disarray, falling gently onto his face.



Shen Shizou heard her say: "I will take you out of here."



—--



But when Bai Qingning went to buy him, there was a small hitch. The proprietor saw that Bai Qingning wanted to buy him, so he raised Shen Shizou's price. Bai Qingning hadn't brought enough money.



Bai Qingning could only spend money to first hire a doctor for Shen Shizou, buy medicine, and reserve an elegant room for him to stay in.



The young men of Gongzi Yuan who wanted to live in good places needed patrons to spend money to buy them lodging. If no one supported them, the young men could only live in the worst places. Only if someone supported him could Shen Shizou live in a good place and eat good food.



Bai Qingning personally selected an elegant room for Shen Shizou and bandaged his wounds with her own hands.



Being so close, Shen Shizou dodged her hands several times. His gaze was cold and hard, completely unyielding. He refused to let Bai Qingning touch him, but Bai Qingning didn't mind at all.



"Don't worry. I've paid to reserve you for a month. Besides me, no one will be able to touch you, and no one will be able to bully you. You must take good care of yourself." When Bai Qingning was leaving, she solemnly grasped Shen Shizou's sleeve and said: "I will definitely save enough money to take you away. My family has money. Wait for me to bring it."



Behind her, Qiuyue had already gone weak all over, leaning against the wall, unable to stand.



This servant understands now.



Not only does Madam want to keep a man, Madam also wants to steal the General's money to keep a man!



Madam is too audacious!



—--



Bai Qingning had come to Gongzi Yuan at noon. By the time she had arranged everything, it was already afternoon. She had haggled with the proprietor here, finally settling on a price of five hundred taels of patterned silver.



This price wasn't cheap—it was enough to redeem some of the more famous courtesans who didn't sell their bodies. But the proprietor had a shrewd eye. Seeing Bai Qingning's attire, he stubbornly refused to budge. Mute Slave's indenture contract was in the proprietor's hands, so Bai Qingning had no choice.



Bai Qingning wasn't someone who knew how to haggle. Such matters were always handled by maids. But that useless foolish maid of hers was still dizzy on the side. Just seeing the young men here had made her unable to breathe. Bai Qingning didn't feel comfortable leaving the matter of buying someone to others, so she had to negotiate herself.



"Next month, I'll bring money to redeem him." Bai Qingning repeatedly instructed: "You're not allowed to mistreat him, not allowed to make him serve clients. Otherwise, I'll smash your establishment."

The proprietor nodded and bowed all the way, saying "yes." After Bai Qingning left, the proprietor looked up at the second floor with a smirk, shouting toward a corner on the second floor: "You little bastard, it turns out you have enormous good fortune. Looking at that madam's bearing, she should be from a wealthy family. Who knows what she saw in you? Boy, you'd better hold on tight. Otherwise, with how you look now, if you make me lose money, I'll beat you to death and throw you out the door to let wild dogs devour you."



The figure on the second floor stood behind a pillar, not answering a word. He stood there as silent as a sculpture, until a figure emerged from below the second floor.



It was a slender, graceful figure. He could only see a bit of her brows, eyes, and nose. As her skirt hem swayed, she was like a lotus flower walking through the mortal world. Ten thousand splendors couldn't touch even a corner of her. Though she clearly stood there, she seemed utterly incompatible with this world.



Shen Shizou looked down at her with lowered eyes.



This woman wanted to keep him as an outside lover, but he was already like this—his appearance completely ruined. Did she truly not care at all?



She said she would come back in a month to take him away, but would she really return?



Taking such an ugly outside lover as him—what pleasure could there be in the bedchamber?



Was she toying with him, or was it momentary interest, or was she pitying him?



As he thought this, Bai Qingning, who had walked downstairs, suddenly raised her head and looked toward that section of eaves.



She could only see blue bricks and green tiles, and a corner of clothing, but Bai Qingning knew that Mute Slave was there.



Because Mute Slave always watched her like this from places she couldn't see.



Bai Qingning smiled brilliantly upward.



Wait a little longer for me. I will take you out.



Shen Shizou stood there, his form unmoving, but his fingers had already clenched into fists.



At that moment, one of them was in the wooden building, one was under the eaves. Neither had completely seen the other's face, but they both knew the other was watching them.



Just at this moment, a horse came galloping from the alley entrance.



On the horse sat a man wearing armor and wielding a heavy blade, controlling the horse with one hand. He had an arrogant appearance, his entire body sharp and imposing, his presence overwhelming. Between his brows, sharpness was condensed.



It was precisely Qin Shanyue, who had hastily rushed back after settling Zhao Hongzhu.



At that moment, the September wind of the capital blew upon all of them at once, simultaneously lifting the blue-green skirt hem and the man's hair ribbon. The horse's hooves trampled the wind as it came. Fallen leaves from the treetops drifted past the three of them. All things in the world became mere backdrop.



The many protagonists from the tale finally made their grand entrance at this moment, then passed by each other unknowingly, rushing forth to the next page of the story.

chapters.title: Three
chapters.content:
When Qin Shanyue rode his fine horse urgently back to the Qin residence, there was not a single person at the entrance of the General's residence—only two guards watching the gate. The common people who had previously lined the streets in welcome had also dispersed. For a moment, it seemed exceptionally desolate.



Qin Shanyue's brows furrowed slightly.



Where was his wife?



The horse's hooves stopped at the entrance of the General's residence. The gatekeeper hurriedly opened the door, leading Qin Shanyue inside. After Qin Shanyue dismounted, he took the horse for him, his manner respectful.



But Qin Shanyue's chest felt increasingly uncomfortable.



In the past, whenever he returned from campaign or from suppressing bandits, everyone in the household would line up to welcome him. No matter how late, Bai Qingning would wait for him, then escort him all the way to the inner residence, help him wash and change clothes. Hot soup and water were always prepared, every detail attended to.



But today, though these people were respectful enough, they weren't enthusiastic enough. It made him feel disappointed everywhere he looked, dissatisfied with everything. For a moment, he didn't even know where he should go.



"Where is Madam?" Qin Shanyue blurted out this question.



A young servant beside him respectfully answered: "In reply to the General, Madam—Madam left the residence earlier and hasn't returned yet."



Qin Shanyue's footsteps paused. A flash of surprise crossed his ink-dark eyes.



He had been on campaign for nearly half a year. Today was his first day back. Why had his wife left the residence?



His wife had always cherished him dearly. How could she be so neglectful of him?



"Where did she go?" Qin Shanyue asked coldly.



The young servant carefully watched Qin Shanyue's expression and answered softly: "Madam was originally waiting at home for the General, but when she heard that the General had brought Miss Zhao... Miss Zhao to the old Zhao family residence, Madam went out alone. She even sent away the maids following her. This humble one doesn't know where Madam went."



Qin Shanyue's advancing footsteps paused. All the questions about why no one was at the entrance to greet him now had answers.



So Bai Qingning was throwing a tantrum at him.



Because he had brought Zhao Hongzhu back, Bai Qingning was jealous and deliberately showed him a cold face.



No, he had to explain to Bai Qingning immediately.



Qin Shanyue's brows furrowed deeply.



"General, should this humble one send people to search?" Seeing Qin Shanyue's expression, the young servant felt that Qin Shanyue's mood seemed somewhat better at this moment, so he asked in a low voice again.



"Go quickly," Qin Shanyue said in a low voice. "Check the Bai family home. Perhaps Madam has returned to the Bai family."



His wife was usually dignified and proper, but in reality, she was most clingy. Whenever she suffered a grievance, she loved to throw tantrums and run home to her natal family.



"Yes." The young servant respectfully led the horse away.



After the young servant left, Qin Shanyue paused in place for a few seconds, then turned around somewhat stiffly and followed the path to the front hall to see the Old Madam.



In earlier years, the Qin family had also been prosperous with many descendants, but later almost all died on the battlefield. In this generation, only Qin Shanyue remained as the sole heir. The entire family were loyal martyrs. Old Madam Qin had imperial honors bestowed upon her and held a lofty position. But as she aged and her health declined, she gradually retired to the courtyard. Every time Qin Shanyue returned from a long journey, he would come to pay his respects to the Old Madam.



When Qin Shanyue returned, the Old Madam was sitting in the front hall. Two clever young maids were massaging Old Madam Qin's legs. After being announced, the young maids rose and withdrew. Qin Shanyue then entered the door, bringing in a gust of cold wind.



"Your son pays respects to Mother." After bowing, Qin Shanyue exchanged a few heartfelt words with the Old Madam.



After speaking for a moment, Old Madam Qin suddenly looked at Qin Shanyue, then said: "I heard you brought Zhao Hongzhu back."



Qin Shanyue's lips pressed slightly tighter. His face, handsome as mountain jade, turned slightly cold. After a long pause, he gave a low "Mm," then added: "The matter of the Zhao family was a wrongful case back then. Preparations are already underway to overturn the verdict. Before long, Zhao Hongzhu's father and brothers will have their names cleared."

Old Madam Qin wore a deep blue-green satin jacket and a headdress inlaid with jade and gold—priceless in its nobility. Sitting upright in the seat of honor, she slowly let out a "hmph" and said: "Back then, it was Zhao Hongzhu I wanted. That Bai Qingning is inferior to Zhao Hongzhu in every way. When you married her back, I was never at ease. Now that Zhao Hongzhu has returned, you should marry her. Give her the position of equal wife."



But Qin Shanyue shook his head slightly, saying: "I don't plan to marry Zhao Hongzhu. I promised Qingning that in this life, she would be my only one."



Old Madam Qin's face darkened. The jade coral prayer beads in her hand fell heavily to the ground: "Shanyue, that Bai Qingning is petty and small-minded. In the end, she still doesn't match you. If I hadn't been gravely ill before and nearly died, how would I have hastily arranged your marriage and had you marry such a—"



Just at this moment, a maid suddenly came to report from outside.



"Madam, Miss Zhao requests an audience."



"Invite her in." Old Madam Qin even stood up.



The Zhao and Qin families were old acquaintances. In earlier years, Zhao Hongzhu had even been raised under Old Madam Qin's care. To Old Madam Qin, she was no different from the apple of her eye.



But Qin Shanyue furrowed his brows.



When he returned this time, he had specifically settled Zhao Hongzhu in an outer residence, complete with maids and servants. Yet he had barely arrived home before Zhao Hongzhu followed. To visit Old Madam Qin directly without sending a visiting card first was highly improper.



As he was thinking this, a beauty in brilliant red had already walked in from outside.



Completely unlike Bai Qingning's cool and dignified manner, Zhao Hongzhu was bright and flamboyant. When she looked at people and smiled, her whole person seemed to glow—like a mass of blazing fire. One glance was enough to know she was a vibrant and lively good girl.



Zhao Hongzhu had once been the most dazzling flower in the capital.



"Azhu." As soon as Old Madam Qin saw Zhao Hongzhu, her eyes reddened. She grasped Zhao Hongzhu's hand and wouldn't let go, chattering on and asking how Zhao Hongzhu had been all these years. Zhao Hongzhu responded softly, bringing up the hardships in the northern desert. Even Old Madam Qin shed tears listening.



"You'll stay at the Qin residence from now on." In just a few sentences, Old Madam Qin's heart had tilted toward Zhao Hongzhu. She personally instructed the head maid beside her to prepare the Nuanxiang Pavilion behind the main hall. The Nuanxiang Pavilion was where Old Madam Qin's youngest daughter used to live. Giving it to Zhao Hongzhu, a woman with no blood relation, was somewhat unreasonable.



But aside from the Nuanxiang Pavilion, the other places in the residence were all in the rear courtyards. Once she lived in the rear courtyards, Zhao Hongzhu would be considered Qin Shanyue's woman. Better the Nuanxiang Pavilion than that.



Qin Shanyue valued filial piety highly. From the moment Old Madam Qin saw Zhao Hongzhu, he hadn't spoken. Only after Old Madam Qin had cried herself weary and was helped back to her sleeping quarters to rest—after Zhao Hongzhu and Qin Shanyue walked side by side out of the front hall, dismissed the servants, and stood under the corridor—did Qin Shanyue finally speak with furrowed brows and a somewhat cold tone: "Hongzhu, you've overstepped in this matter. You living in the Qin family now—it's neither proper nor justified. How will you be able to marry in the future?"



A trace of self-mocking smile appeared on Zhao Hongzhu's face: "Brother Qin, after what happened to my family, who would still want me? In these years in the northern desert, I've suffered all the cold indifference of human relationships. Only Brother Qin was willing to help me. I've long decided that I will never marry in this lifetime."



"Today, it's not that I insisted on coming to the door to be annoying. I just kept the Old Madam in my heart and wanted to come speak with her. I just didn't expect the Old Madam would insist on keeping me here. I also know that my status is now lowly and it's not good for me to stay here long. Brother Qin, rest assured, I'll go bid farewell to the Old Madam in a moment. I absolutely won't put Brother Qin in a difficult position."

Qin Shanyue's brows furrowed even tighter, and his heart felt somewhat guilty.



That marriage arrangement back then—ultimately, it was the Qin family who, seeing the Zhao family suddenly embroiled in disaster, feared being implicated and hastily broke off the engagement. He felt guilty toward Zhao Hongzhu, which was why he had been working all these years to help overturn the Zhao family's case.



But no matter what, in the end, he owed Zhao Hongzhu a debt.



"There's no need." Qin Shanyue's voice rang out low and deep: "You can stay at the Qin residence for the next few days. Tomorrow I'll go to court and personally present the injustice the Zhao family suffered back then, and search for your scattered relatives. Once everything is properly handled, you can leave then."



Zhao Hongzhu didn't bow in gratitude and shed tears like an ordinary woman would. She only raised her head and gave Qin Shanyue a smile.



She was naturally bright and beautiful. With this smile, she was more brilliant than all the flowers in the courtyard.



Qin Shanyue was dazed for a moment.



In earlier years, Zhao Hongzhu had been like this. No matter the circumstances, Zhao Hongzhu could hold up that beautiful face and walk forward step by step. She was resilient, she was decisive, she had the tenacity that all the sheltered ladies in the world lacked. When facing difficulties, she never cried or whimpered. She was always the most intelligent, the calmest one. Everyone praised her.



"Among all the blossoms that have fallen, she alone shines bright—Zhao Hongzhu claims all the charm."



Qin Shanyue had once loved such a girl.



But quickly, Bai Qingning's gentle face floated up in Qin Shanyue's mind. The pure lotus fragrance diluted the memories of the past. Qin Shanyue stepped back half a step. On that consistently cold and sharp face, several traces of awkwardness actually appeared. Retreating, he said: "You—you should go rest first. I still have matters to attend to."



Zhao Hongzhu stood in place, the smile on her face unchanged, just watching as Qin Shanyue left.



Only after Qin Shanyue's figure finally disappeared did Zhao Hongzhu's constantly raised head slowly lower.



Three years apart, and the youth who had once run several streets to buy back a hairpin flower because of one word from her, who had climbed the wall and said he would definitely marry her—he already had another sweetheart.



She still remembered the sunset glow over the wall that day, but now the courtyard was overgrown with wild grass, and the General had a beauty by his side.



How could the phrase "things have changed, people are different" possibly explain it all?



Everyone in the world was moving forward. Only she alone was still sinking and floating in that calamity from three years ago, still without a place to return to.



The Zhao family was long gone. Only she remained alive in this world. She was just a weak woman without official position or merit to support her. What methods could she have? Could she really just wait like that in that small courtyard?



Even if vindication came, her father and brothers were already dead. She could never become the eldest miss of the Zhao family again. Vindication couldn't give her justice. What she wanted was blood debt repaid in blood.



Those who had harmed the Zhao family back then all had to die, and her only reliance was the Qin family.



The Qin family had connections reaching to the heavens. She could only grip tightly onto Qin Shanyue, this blade, to carve out a path from the encirclement of wolves.



She had to hold onto Qin Shanyue.



Using every possible method.



—--



Qin Shanyue left from Old Madam Qin's quarters, passing through several corridors and courtyards. On the road, he encountered a young servant bringing news, saying: "Madam has already returned."



Qin Shanyue's heart warmed somewhat, and his footsteps quickened.



He walked for a quarter of an hour and finally arrived at Lotus Courtyard.



Bai Qingning loved lotus flowers, so Qin Shanyue had built a Lotus Courtyard for her. He had invited skilled craftsmen to dig ponds and divert living water. Every summer, lotus flowers bloomed everywhere here. Bai Qingning most loved to sit in the pavilion and play the zither.

"By the lotus, a person like the moon—pale wrists like congealed frost and snow."



Thinking of Bai Qingning's face, the corners of Qin Shanyue's lips curved into a relaxed, reminiscent smile, and his steps entering Lotus Courtyard became lighter.



He strode quickly inside, but noticed that Lotus Courtyard was completely empty. The maids who usually stood under the corridors awaiting orders and the young servants who swept and sprinkled water were all gone. Qin Shanyue walked alone into the side room and actually heard faint clattering sounds coming from inside.



Qin Shanyue quickened his pace, reached out his hand, and pushed open the carved rosewood door.



Inside the room, Bai Qingning was taking inventory with Qiuyue of Bai Qingning's dowry and the assets she had accumulated over the years at the Qin family. Sandalwood boxes were piled all over the floor, and the room was filled with gold, silver, jewelry, and hairpins gleaming brilliantly.



Bai Qingning was not favored in the Bai family. She was a concubine-born daughter, born of a concubine mother. Above her was a legitimate elder brother, below her a legitimate younger sister and a concubine-born younger brother. The legitimate brother had already entered the court as an official, the legitimate sister remained unmarried and had been seeking a husband in recent years, and the concubine-born brother was still studying.



In her past life, her mother had died early, and she was also raised by the main wife. She had been taught to put the Bai family first in everything—her husband's family was her heaven, and the Bai family would always be her support.



She had always thought the Bai family had affection for her. Even though she was a concubine-born daughter, she was raised and loved at the main wife's knee. But only after dying once did she realize that the Bai family merely treated her as a marriage alliance tool. To curry favor with Qin Shanyue, the Bai family was even willing to let her die.



People always have to suffer great calamities before they can see through certain people.



Bai Qingning's last bit of affection for the Bai family had already dissipated. She now only wanted to count clearly how much dowry the Bai family had given her and whether it was enough for her to buy someone.



When the Bai family married her into the General's residence that year, they knew they were reaching above their station, so they gave her a lot of dowry to maintain appearances. If converted entirely to silver, it would be around four thousand taels.



Don't underestimate these four thousand taels—for ordinary common folk, ten taels of silver was enough to live on for a year.



The Bai family back then had not yet made their fortune. The whole family were scholars, with all show but little substance. She was also a concubine-born daughter, so being able to produce these four thousand taels of silver was already quite good.



In these years at the Qin family, managing the household, she had also saved up several hundred taels.



This silver was enough for her to redeem Mute Slave. Besides that, she also needed to find herself a way out.



The Bai family couldn't possibly be her support. Ordinary people also couldn't afford to provoke the Qin residence's power. She still wanted to take revenge on Qin Shanyue and Zhao Hongzhu, so she had to prepare travel permits and new identity documents in advance, to facilitate future escape and avoid being resented by these two families.



Bai Qingning's mind was rattling away like an abacus when she suddenly heard the light sound of a wooden door. She raised her head and saw a tall, upright figure standing at the door.



The newcomer was extremely tall, almost blocking all the light from the doorway. He wore armor, a black long blade hung at his waist, and the scent of blood still clung to him. His brows and eyes were cold and sharp. When looking at people, he naturally carried an aura of cold, stern威pressure.



With one glance, Bai Qingning's heart suddenly turned cold.



After two lifetimes, she had finally seen this husband again.



—--



"What are you doing?" Qin Shanyue's low voice came from the doorway, startling Qiuyue, who was concentrating on counting money. With an "Ah!" she stood up. The moment she saw Qin Shanyue, Qiuyue nearly fainted from fright on the spot.



Oh heavens, she and Madam were stealing the General's money to play with men and were discovered by the General!

chapters.title: Four
chapters.content:
"Sorting through some old things." Bai Qingning gathered her skirt and rose, but she didn't joyfully and lightly rush over to him as Qin Shanyue had expected. Instead, she stood distantly among a pile of boxes. First, she had Qiuyue move the items out. Only after Qiuyue left did she step forward, bowing to Qin Shanyue from afar: "This concubine respectfully welcomes the General."



As she bowed, her pale hands swayed, the jade bracelet on her wrist gently swinging. Her jade head slightly lowered, her movements dignified and elegant, but no joy could be heard in that tone—cold as snow in the twelfth month.



"Aning." Qin Shanyue knew Bai Qingning must still be upset, so he softened his tone by three parts: "It's my fault for returning late."



Bai Qingning didn't speak. She only summoned Qiuyue to serve tea.



In her past life, when Qin Shanyue returned, he had also spoken to her so gently. With just a few words, he had dismantled her defenses and suspicions, making her willingly swallow down all that bitterness and sourness.



Common people all said that Qin Shanyue was a general who battled on the field, a killing god who slaughtered cities and seized territories. But stripped of that bloody armor, Qin Shanyue was actually a steady and quiet person. He wasn't very good at sweet words of love, only at making resounding promises.



"I know you must have heard some gossip and rumors. Aning, I did indeed bring Zhao Hongzhu back from the northern desert, but it has nothing to do with personal feelings. The Zhao family's treason case back then was a wrongful conviction. I've obtained evidence. Bringing Zhao Hongzhu back this time is also to help overturn the Zhao family's case."



"Brother Zhao and I grew up together since childhood. We two are brothers bound by life and death. He died suffering false accusation and humiliation. Now that I have evidence, I cannot fail to help him this once. Aning, please bear with this a little. Wait for me. Once I arrange everything properly, I will definitely make good arrangements for Zhao Hongzhu and find her a good husband. Will you trust me?"



Bai Qingning sat upright in her chair, holding a cup of Spring Longjing tea from after the rain. She smelled the tea's fragrance, then raised her eyes to look at Qin Shanyue.



The same words as in her past life, but entering her ears now brought entirely different thoughts.



In her past life, hearing these words, like a prisoner receiving a pardon, she had thrown herself into Qin Shanyue's embrace and wouldn't let go, crying her heart out, unable to care about anything else. But hearing them now, she only felt mockery.



Just a few baseless words, yet they had been enough to fool her completely.



"As long as the General has his own plans, that's good." Bai Qingning took a sip of tea, her voice falling coldly: "Qingning will follow the General's instructions completely."



Qin Shanyue's heart caught. His sharp phoenix eyes lifted, as if he hadn't expected Bai Qingning to be so cold and indifferent. It left him rather at a loss as to how to proceed. He and Bai Qingning had been married for three years, and it had always been Bai Qingning who rushed toward him.



Just as Qin Shanyue was hesitating about whether to say more, a young servant suddenly came from outside to report that the Emperor had summoned him to the palace.



By normal reasoning, Qin Shanyue should have entered the palace the next day, but the Emperor's decree came urgently. Qin Shanyue had no time to speak further with Bai Qingning. He only hastily offered a few words of comfort before leaving.



After Qin Shanyue left, Qiuyue tremblingly entered the room.



All the maids in Lotus Courtyard had been sent away, leaving only Qiuyue. The surroundings were completely quiet. As soon as Qiuyue entered, she saw Bai Qingning sitting upright in her chair, lost in thought. Her fingertips, delicate as scallion shoots, gripped the gold-traced white moon porcelain cup. Her fingertips were scalded red, yet she seemed not to feel the pain.



"Madam." Qiuyue didn't dare call her "Second Miss" inside Lotus Courtyard. Fortunately, Bai Qingning didn't care about this, so she continued: "Just now, a matron from the Old Madam's courtyard came to ask whether Madam can manage the victory banquet in a few days. If not, she'll send over two capable women to serve."

Bai Qingning's drifting thoughts were pulled back. With a sweep of her eyes, she saw the tea leaves floating in the cup. The tender green buds floated in the water, gradually sinking to the bottom along with Qiuyue's words.



Qin Shanyue had been away from the capital for a long time. Returning victorious from battle, the Emperor would naturally bestow rewards. Right now, he was the hottest figure in the capital. Naturally, a grand victory banquet should be held, made lively and bustling, to properly show off.



"The General's victory banquet will invite many people. The guest list has already been drafted and is waiting for Madam's review. The servants for procurement have also all been dispatched. It's just that the specific arrangements still require Madam's word."



As Qiuyue said these things, she looked at Bai Qingning with particular worry, afraid that Bai Qingning would just throw up her hands and not care about anything—from today on, Madam had been acting strangely and inexplicably. Watching her made Qiuyue's heart equally chaotic.



"Mm." Bai Qingning took the drafted list, casually crossed out a few names, saying "no need to invite these people," then handed the name cards back to Qiuyue.



Looking at the people who had been crossed out, Qiuyue wanted to ask "Madam, won't you ask the General?" but then remembered that bright green hat on the General's head and swallowed those words back down.



"Go reply to the Old Madam that I have enough people here. No need to trouble the Old Madam." Bai Qingning rose, walking toward the courtyard as she said: "Summon all those matrons below. I have instructions to give."



Qiuyue bowed and withdrew, leaving Bai Qingning alone sitting in the hall.



In Bai Qingning's mind, she began recalling the banquet from her past life.



In her past life's victory banquet, it wasn't Bai Qingning who single-handedly organized it. Although she managed the household affairs, there was still the Old Madam above her. Old Madam Qin had never liked her, disdaining her low birth and petty ways of doing things. Therefore, whenever there was a grand banquet, she never entrusted the banquet matters entirely to her. She would always insert two women to obstruct her, constantly sending people over to ask questions, as if coming to help her but actually nitpicking everywhere, always wanting Bai Qingning to do things their way.



And in her past life, Bai Qingning had indeed been distracted by the matters of Zhao Hongzhu and Qin Shanyue, her mind unsettled. She simply couldn't arrange things properly and just let those two matrons arrange everything. As a result, on the day of the victory banquet, when Bai Qingning arrived at the venue, she saw Zhao Hongzhu standing in the host's position greeting guests, directing those two women, smiling sweetly as she welcomed and sent off guests.



That was a place only the mistress of the house could stand. Yet all the Qin family members looked as if it was perfectly natural.



At that time, standing in the courtyard, Bai Qingning felt as if she was being lashed by the gazes of all the guests.



She was clearly the mistress of the Qin family, yet at her own family's banquet, she couldn't find a place to stand. When she arrived, Zhao Hongzhu even bowed to her, saying "the Old Madam said Madam was seriously ill and asked me to lend a hand." Those words made everyone want to laugh.



Lend a hand—in what capacity was she lending a hand? By what right did she stand in the mistress's position? Zhao Hongzhu couldn't wait to announce to everyone that she was the mistress of the Qin family, that she had returned, and Bai Qingning had to step aside.



At that time, with so many people and prying eyes, Bai Qingning had forcibly managed to say a few polite words, then withdrew early. The banquet wasn't even over yet. With a knot of anger stuck in her chest, feeling terribly uncomfortable, she looked for the General at the banquet. But she hadn't expected to catch the General and Zhao Hongzhu having a secret meeting in a room, engaging in illicit affairs. She and the General made quite an ugly scene at the time. In her rage, she fell ill that very night, spending several days in a daze. After that came Qiuyue's incident. She returned home to seek help from the Bai family, but instead the Bai family told her to voluntarily request divorce. She accidentally fell into water and nearly died.

Thinking about it, her contest with Zhao Hongzhu had been lost from the very day of the victory banquet in her past life.



Starting over again, Bai Qingning would tolerate no one. Old Madam Qin wanted to insert people—she gave not an ounce of face and directly blocked it. And as for Qin Shanyue and Zhao Hongzhu's secret meeting... in this life, she would see how this Zhao Hongzhu could still maintain her footing in the Qin family.



Several thoughts flashed through her mind, and Qiuyue had already brought several matrons over.



In the residence, there were six notable steward matrons in total—two managed accounts, two managed the kitchen, and two managed daily procurement. After Bai Qingning took charge of household affairs, she had always used these six. They were quite handy to employ. After individually instructing and warning them about the banquet procedures, Bai Qingning dismissed them.



The matrons' front feet had barely left before Bai Qingning called Qiuyue over.



"Find some time," Bai Qingning instructed. "Go to that Gongzi Yuan and see how he's doing now, whether anyone's giving him trouble."



Qiuyue's legs went weak, and she nearly fainted again.



The General was still in the residence—how could their mistress keep thinking about that young male courtesan!



"Madam, what if the General discovers this?" Qiuyue lowered her voice, earnestly advising: "We should go see him less often."



"Just be careful," Bai Qingning said, completely unconcerned about any general or not. "Just go."



Qiuyue left Lotus Courtyard in a daze.



It's over—their mistress has had her soul stolen by a male fox spirit from Gongzi Yuan!



When Qiuyue left Lotus Courtyard, she replied to the maid from the Old Madam who had been waiting outside. The maid then went back to report to the Old Madam. Learning that Bai Qingning had actually refused her arrangement to insert people into the banquet affairs, the Old Madam was so angry she smashed a teacup and cursed for a long time.



Some clever maids, thinking to curry favor with Bai Qingning, secretly passed these words to the maids in Bai Qingning's courtyard. Those maids then came to tell Bai Qingning. In just a moment, Bai Qingning knew about it.



The Old Madam was getting on in years after all, not long from departing westward on a crane. Last time, they had specifically invited an imperial physician from the palace, who only said she could last at most until the end of this year. Qin Shanyue had no other concubines, so in the entire vast General's residence, there was only Bai Qingning as mistress. Quite a few people had restless thoughts, wanting to sell information to Bai Qingning to gain favor with her in the future.



"I understand." Bai Qingning casually acknowledged with a sentence. She hadn't wanted to meddle much in the Old Madam's affairs, but just as the maid was about to withdraw, she called out "Wait."



"In the coming days, find two capable ones." Bai Qingning's gaze swept over this maid twice. She remembered this maid was called Chunri. She had a clean background and had served her for many years, quite loyal. Only then did she add: "Gather more news from the front courtyard and Nuanxiang Pavilion. Also, tomorrow I need to make a trip to the Bai family. Go deliver a message to the Bai family today."



Qiuyue was too foolish and her courage too small. She had to find some other helpers.



Chunri, receiving Bai Qingning's instructions, knew she was about to be entrusted with important tasks. Excited for a moment, she clenched her fists tightly. She first responded with acknowledgment, then secretly glanced at Madam. Seeing Bai Qingning's frosty expression, she swallowed her words back down and hurriedly bowed and withdrew.



Only after everyone had left did Bai Qingning slowly sit back in her chair. She turned over all the schemes and plots in her belly, desperately thinking about what she should do.



The Qin family, the Bai family, Zhao Hongzhu, Mute Slave, Qiuyue.



In the past, she had valued harmony above all else everywhere, disliking scheming against people. But now, she had to fight for herself.

In this life, she must turn everything upside down, or else she would have lived this life in vain.



—--



When Qiuyue left the residence gate, the sun was already setting in the west. Before arriving at Gongzi Yuan, she even changed her attire a bit, putting on a bamboo hat for herself. Outside, she gave herself a pep talk, then snuck into Gongzi Yuan like a thief.



The proprietor led Qiuyue to Shen Shizou's room with a smile all the way.



Shen Shizou was a golden canary reserved with heavy gold, not to receive guests, so he was kept in the deepest part of the second floor. When Qiuyue entered, Shen Shizou was changing his bandages.



He had already changed into a set of ink-wash robes, wearing a black feather crown. Although his face was still bandaged, just looking at his build and bone structure, he was clearly a dragon among men. Growing into such an appearance, no wonder he could bewitch Madam so completely.



—--



When the wooden door of the room was pushed open and the proprietor withdrew with an ingratiating smile, Shen Shizou stood up with his spine tensed.



His gaze fixed on the doorway. With just one glance, he knew the person entering was not that lotus-like woman.



Who is this?



Why... was she unwilling to come herself?



After the other party entered, they looked at each other for a moment, neither speaking first.



After more than ten breaths had passed, Qiuyue felt they couldn't continue waiting like this.



Since Madam insisted on having this young courtesan, she as a maid naturally had to help Madam. Madam couldn't spare the time now, so it naturally fell to her to instruct this young courtesan, just like how those experienced matrons in the past instructed Madam on how to serve the General.



So, Qiuyue mustered all the courage of her life, yanked off her bamboo hat, puffed out her chest, and said loudly: "You, since you're already our Madam's person, from today onwards you must learn how to serve our Madam. Now, I will teach you how to please Madam."



Madam, today Qiuyue will definitely not fail your teachings!



—--



When Shen Shizou heard these words, he pressed his lips tightly together and didn't speak.



Sure enough, they wanted to do those filthy things with him.



Shen Shizou should have disliked this, but somehow, remembering the tenderness in Bai Qingning's eyes and brows when she spoke to him, he surprisingly didn't feel... repulsed.



—--



While Bai Qingning was unaware, her maid who fainted every three steps had finally grown up like a branch after rain.



She just grew a bit crooked, that's all.

chapters.title: Five
chapters.content:
Autumn, the hour of midnight.



Cool moonlight spilled onto the streets. Qin Shanyue sat in the carriage, his sword-like brows tightly furrowed, his face full of exhaustion.



Today when he had his audience with the Emperor, he had brought up the Zhao family matter. After discussing it with him for a while, the Emperor gave him shocking news.



The Zhao family indeed had not participated in treason back then, but there truly were people in the court who had committed treason. The Emperor had already handed this matter to the Embroidered Uniform Guard to investigate secretly. Recently, they had just found some leads. Before the matter was fully resolved, the Emperor couldn't overturn the Zhao family's case, lest they alert the enemy.



In other words, Zhao Hongzhu would have to stay at the Qin residence for some more days.



And bringing Zhao Hongzhu back had drawn some attention. To prevent those in the shadows from knowing he was already aware of the treason matter, he needed a proper excuse to settle Zhao Hongzhu.



This proper excuse was that he still had lingering feelings for Zhao Hongzhu and wanted to use his military merits as a reason to keep Zhao Hongzhu, making those people think he brought her back because he loved her, not because he wanted to overturn her case.



This meant he had to give Zhao Hongzhu a status. It couldn't be as a concubine. If he were to give Zhao Hongzhu status, it could only be as an equal wife.



But how could he face Bai Qingning like this?



One thought after another flashed through his mind. The carriage had arrived at the back gate at this time. Qin Shanyue first went to the study. After organizing all the evidence clearly, he had wanted to return to Lotus Courtyard but was told by the maids there that Bai Qingning had already retired for the night.



Guilt rising in Qin Shanyue's heart, he didn't go to Lotus Courtyard to disturb her. Instead, he made do alone in the study for the night.



Qingning had always been gentle and compliant. After he explained the matter of Zhao Hongzhu to Bai Qingning in detail, surely Qingning would be able to tolerate it.



Qin Shanyue slept through the night with such thoughts. The next day when he went to find Bai Qingning, he was told again that Bai Qingning had already returned to her natal family today.



Qin Shanyue pinched the bridge of his nose, thinking that Qingning was still angry with him.



But he no longer had the energy to coax her. He had many things to do today. Since returning to the capital, he had yet to visit the other generals. A pile of military matters awaited his attention.
