"Very well." Qin Shanyue could only say to the young servant: "When Madam returns, have her come see me."



The young servant acknowledged and left. At this time, Bai Qingning had already boarded a carriage and returned to the Bai family.



Bai Qingning's father had been just a minor official in the Ministry of Revenue a few years ago. Now he had risen to Vice Minister of Revenue, all relying on Qin Shanyue's power and influence. Now that Qin Shanyue had returned to the capital in great victory, even before the Qin family could strut about, Father Bai was already looking down his nose at people, frequently using Qin Shanyue's name to conduct business outside.



Even Bai Qingning's legitimate elder brother had entered the Ministry of Justice through Qin Shanyue's arrangements.



The Bai family had previously relied on Qin Shanyue everywhere. No wonder later, when Bai Qingning discovered Qin Shanyue and Zhao Hongzhu's secret meeting and fell out with Qin Shanyue, they urgently and frantically pressured Bai Qingning to step aside.



In their eyes, Bai Qingning was merely a vine they used to climb up and curry favor with the Qin family. Now this section of vine was being disobedient, actually daring to challenge Qin Shanyue, daring to fall out with Qin Shanyue over some trivial matters. Those who benefited naturally were the first to refuse, even more extreme in their attitude than Qin Shanyue.



When Bai Qingning arrived at the Bai family, it was mid-morning.



The Bai family residence was an old estate located near Kangping Street in the middle section of the inner city. The plaque above was made of cumin-scented pine wood, exuding an aged fragrance settled by years. The floor tiles were white jade stone, the gaps between tiles clean and orderly. The roof had green tiles and red eaves. Against the wall grew large patches of purple wisteria. When the breeze blew, the entire courtyard was filled with floral fragrance.

Bai Qingning had sent word ahead of time, so an old matron had been waiting at the side gate early on. Seeing her arrive, she bowed all the way and led her through the gate, chattering along the way: "Madam has been worrying about you terribly. Knowing you were coming back, she had this old slave wait here early."



The old matron in front chattered on as she led her into Madam Bai's Bamboo Courtyard. Only the female family members were home.



Father Bai and her legitimate elder brother weren't on rest days—they were both busy outside. Her concubine-born younger brother was studying away from home. Her legitimate younger sister was learning etiquette from a matron. Upon seeing Bai Qingning, she acted coquettish, wanting to talk with Bai Qingning as an excuse to escape learning etiquette.



Bai Qingning gifted her legitimate younger sister a white jade hairpin. This hairpin was from the Qin family's storehouse. The Qin family only had her and the Old Madam as female masters. The Old Madam had no one to exchange gifts with, so she could dispose of the storehouse items as she pleased. Although the Qin family looked down on her, the Qin family's standards were established—they never treated her shabbily.



This single white jade hairpin could sell for at least a hundred taels of silver outside—an extremely precious item, rarely seen in the Bai family. Her legitimate younger sister normally couldn't even see such things. Now, having received this hairpin, she happily left the room.



After she left, Madam Bai sent the servants away before speaking intimately with Bai Qingning.



"I heard early on that Qin Shanyue brought back that Miss Zhao. As soon as I heard, I knew you must be unhappy about it. But what can you do about being unhappy? You still have to accept your fate." Madam Bai was a gentle beauty who spoke in a measured manner, each sentence sincere: "Men are like this. Earlier you said Qin Shanyue was willing to be with you for life—I knew it was impossible. Don't worry about how many women he has. Hurrying to bear a child is the real priority."



When Madam Bai said these things, Bai Qingning never opened her mouth. Only after Madam Bai finished did Bai Qingning smile at her.



"Mother is right." Bai Qingning lowered her brows and eyes, speaking slowly: "I came this time to tell Mother something. Tomorrow is my husband's victory banquet. If Elder Brother has no time, have Fourth Brother make the trip and show his face. If he can get to know a couple of powerful people, that would be good too."



Seeing Bai Qingning in such an obedient posture and willing to help her natal family, Madam Bai's tone softened by three parts. She stared at Bai Qingning's face for a moment. Seeing Bai Qingning truly had no intention of feeling wronged or angry, she moved closer and said to Bai Qingning: "Mother is telling you this secretly. Keep it in your heart but don't let it show. Mother heard your father say that recently the Emperor has intentions to overturn the Zhao family's case. That Miss Zhao is currently a soft persimmon anyone can pinch, but in the future she will definitely have great fortune. The imperial family owes the Zhao family and will definitely compensate them."



"The General originally had a marriage contract with Miss Zhao. This time, Miss Zhao was brought back by the General. If in the future the Emperor intends to grant a marriage decree, you won't be able to avoid it either. Better to establish a good relationship with that Miss Zhao from the very beginning, lest things become awkward later."



"If you can get along well with that Miss Zhao, perhaps in the future she might even give you some assistance. Just endure for now—you'll have good days ahead."



These words—Bai Qingning hadn't heard them in her past life.



In her past life, when she came to the Bai family, it was already after the banquet. At that time, she had lost everything at the Qin family and was in a daze. After returning, she only wanted to complain and have the Bai family stand up for her.



Thinking about it now, the Bai family must have seen that she was obsessed then, single-mindedly opposing Zhao Hongzhu, and had lost favor at the Qin family. They simply gave up on her directly, so they didn't mention these things.

But in this life, she displayed a calm and carefree manner, so the Bai family was actually willing to tell her some truths.



So at that time, the Bai family already knew that Zhao Hongzhu would definitely rise to great heights, which was why they repeatedly urged concessions.



From beginning to end, she was the only one kept in the dark.



"Daughter understands." Bai Qingning smiled even more gently: "Daughter will do everything according to Mother's words."



Madam Bai was even more satisfied. She thought for a moment, then added: "Your fourth brother is still studying. It's not much use for him to meet those people too early. Better to have your elder brother go instead. And bring your younger sister along too. Your third sister has also reached the age to marry—she should meet some people."



Bai Qingning smiled and lowered her eyes.



She had known it—Madam Bai would never bring that concubine-born son out.



Only that pair of legitimate son and daughter were her foundation.



However, this suited her intentions perfectly.



Since Madam Bai thought Zhao Hongzhu was so wonderfully good, then let her taste this sweet fruit that was Zhao Hongzhu herself.



—--



Bai Qingning stayed at the Bai family until afternoon before leaving. When she returned to the Qin residence, Chunri had already been waiting at the entrance of Lotus Courtyard for a long time. Bai Qingning's front foot had barely entered when Chunri knelt in the side room on her back foot, presenting a golden hairpin with both hands.



"Are you certain it was Matron Liu who had someone plant it?" In the side room, Bai Qingning looked at the crabapple golden hairpin placed on the table, asking in a gentle tone: "Did anyone else see it?"



Matron Liu—she was an old acquaintance. In her past life, it was she who had led people to burn Bai Qingning to death.



"No one else, only this servant saw it." Chunri also knew the matter was serious. Kneeling on the ground, she carefully weighed each word: "Madam previously instructed this servant to inquire about Nuanxiang Pavilion's affairs, so this servant paid attention and had a young sister keep watch. She saw Matron Liu enter Nuanxiang Pavilion and speak with Zhao Hongzhu for a while. After coming out, Matron Liu found an excuse and had a maid make a trip to our Lotus Courtyard. This servant felt something was wrong and came to consult Madam."



After Chunri came to consult, Bai Qingning told Chunri not to make a fuss but to quietly search the courtyard, focusing on Qiuyue's area. Sure enough, they found a crabapple golden hairpin in Qiuyue's cabinet.



The golden hairpin was exceptionally exquisite. One glance showed it was painstakingly crafted by skilled artisans—quite valuable. Sold outside, it could fetch a hundred taels of silver.



Bai Qingning reached out and stroked the golden hairpin, recalling events from her past life.



At that time, she had still been wallowing in self-pity, in poor spirits, completely unaware of these undercurrents. One day when she woke up, her Qiuyue had already been dragged to kneel in the courtyard. Those people only said that Qiuyue had stolen Miss Zhao's belongings—caught red-handed with the evidence. Old Madam Qin had Qiuyue beaten to death alive.



After beating Qiuyue to death, Old Madam Qin still wasn't satisfied. She also punished Bai Qingning with confinement, using the crime of lax management as the reason, trampling Bai Qingning's dignity into the ground before everyone.



From that point on, Bai Qingning completely lost power in the Qin family.



And her foolish Qiuyue, even before dying, had knelt before her crying, saying "it has nothing to do with Madam."



"I understand." Bai Qingning put away the hairpin and turned to reward Chunri with a jade bracelet: "Well done. You may go."



After Chunri kowtowed and withdrew, Bai Qingning sat alone by the bed for a while, then smiled faintly.



Matron Liu. Miss Zhao.



Miss Zhao had already made her move against her. If she didn't return the favor, that would be too discourteous.

—--



When Qin Shanyue finished all his affairs and returned to the residence, it was already very late. As usual, he headed first to Lotus Courtyard, but before arriving, he ran into a maid running out from Nuanxiang Pavilion.



The maid said urgently "Our young miss is so ill she's dying," so Qin Shanyue hurried to see Zhao Hongzhu. Sure enough, in Nuanxiang Pavilion he saw Zhao Hongzhu collapsed on the bed, face pale. Half-conscious, she was still calling Qin Shanyue's courtesy name.



"Zijin, Zijin."



Qin Shanyue's courtesy name was Zijin.



Speaking of which, in earlier years, Qin Shanyue and Zhao Hongzhu had been classmates. The imperial family ran a school specifically for the children of civil and military officials, without gender separation. They only set up a wooden screen in the middle of the classroom to separate the students on both sides. At that time, Zhao Hongzhu had learned Qin Shanyue's courtesy name.



For a woman to call a man by his courtesy name was really too intimate, so Zhao Hongzhu never called him by his name. Only on the day they pledged their love did Zhao Hongzhu call his courtesy name. From then on, she would always call him that in private.



Later, after he married, Bai Qingning only called him "husband," occasionally acting coquettish and calling him "General." She had never called him by his courtesy name.



Qin Shanyue hadn't heard Zhao Hongzhu call these two words in many years. Hearing it suddenly, he only felt a strange sensation rise from his waist, shooting straight up to his scalp. He stood rigidly by the bedside, unable to move. But Zhao Hongzhu on the bed reached out her hand and grasped his palm.



While Qin Shanyue stood stiff, Zhao Hongzhu slowly nestled closer, placing her head in his palm, then closed her eyes and fell into a deep sleep.



The sleeping Zhao Hongzhu's face bore fear and unease, tears soaking the corners of her eyes. Seeing this made Qin Shanyue's heart ache sharply.



"Your young miss—what illness has she contracted?" Qin Shanyue asked in a hoarse voice.



"Miss was previously frightened. When we went to the northern desert, we encountered bandits on the road. Miss nearly got killed. Since then, she cries in terror every night, unable to sleep." The maid knelt on the ground kowtowing, crying and pleading as she knocked her head: "General, the three years of bitter cold in the northern desert—Miss only endured them relying on you. Miss cannot be without you. Please have mercy and come see our miss more often each day."



Qin Shanyue's chest felt as if it were soaked in bitter water. He couldn't say a single word.



Those memories from the past suddenly came alive. The former Zhao Hongzhu with her flower-like smile, riding horses through Chang'an, overlapped with the current Zhao Hongzhu with her deathly pale face on the bed, making Qin Shanyue feel only a dull aching pain.

chapters.title: Six
chapters.content:
If it weren't for him betraying Zhao Hongzhu, how could Zhao Hongzhu be in such a state?



These three years in the northern desert—who knows how much suffering that once delicate and beautiful girl endured.



Qin Shanyue felt an impulse spreading through his heart. Unable to control himself, he grasped Zhao Hongzhu's ice-cold fingers in return, gripping them tightly, as if wanting to pull back all the lost time as well, hold it to his heart, and never let go again.



That night, Qin Shanyue stayed in Nuanxiang Pavilion until midnight, only coming out when dawn broke.



During that half night, Qin Shanyue's heart wall—solid as the Great Wall of the northern desert—was forcibly breached by Zhao Hongzhu's tears. The deep affection of former days drilled in through this opening and re-entrenched itself in Qin Shanyue's heart. As the cold autumn night wind blew on his body, his palm seemed to still retain Zhao Hongzhu's warmth.



When he came out, he once again passed by Lotus Courtyard. But this time, Qin Shanyue didn't know how to enter.



He recalled Zhao Hongzhu's deathly pale face as she lay collapsed on the bed. He truly couldn't bring himself to say words like "will properly settle Zhao Hongzhu and find her a good family to marry into."



Where could he settle Zhao Hongzhu?



Without him, Zhao Hongzhu suffered through every night.



He owed Zhao Hongzhu a debt.



So he dared not see Bai Qingning either. He feared seeing Bai Qingning's tears.



Thus, after standing at the entrance of Lotus Courtyard for a moment, Qin Shanyue didn't even step through the door. Full of troubled thoughts, he walked away under the starlight.



At this moment, Qin Shanyue didn't yet know that Bai Qingning, whom he thought was sleeping soundly, was actually standing at the window draped in clothes, gazing at the moonlight and contemplating her hidden killing moves. Nor did he know that Zhao Hongzhu, whom he thought was suffering nightly anguish, also rose from bed after he left, wiped away her tears, and gazed in the direction of his departure, counting up her own vulnerabilities.



Both women looked at the same man, but both were thinking about how to destroy the other. The white moonlight carried poison, the cinnabar mole concealed a blade, while Qin Shanyue was still thinking about how to maintain balance.



—--



The day of the victory banquet arrived quickly.



The banquet time was set for noon, with guests arriving two quarters of an hour early. But Bai Qingning had been busy since early morning.



She needed to inspect the food and water, then check the seating arrangements. After arranging everything properly, she calculated the time and went to the front hall to welcome guests.



She had prepared quite a few "gifts" for Zhao Hongzhu today.



At the victory banquet, male and female guests weren't seated separately. Everyone gathered in one large front hall, with men and women simply sitting in separate areas. She welcomed the female guests—wives from various families sitting to one side, their conversation quite lively.



Bai Qingning had previously been of a leisurely and elegant temperament. With Qin Shanyue often away, she rarely socialized, so outsiders didn't know her well. They only knew she was a cool beauty, but hadn't expected her to be so gentle and proper, doing things at an unhurried pace. Every troublesome matter at the banquet, large or small, was arranged, making people extraordinarily comfortable.



After three rounds of wine, the conversation boxes opened, and people began subtly probing Bai Qingning about Zhao Hongzhu's current situation.



"Don't laugh at me, Madam Qin, but Hongzhu and I were close friends in earlier years. Later we lost contact, and I've been thinking about her all this time."



Bai Qingning followed the voice and looked toward the girl who spoke.



She wore green clothes and looked quite lively and cute, but Bai Qingning knew this girl had a major grudge against Zhao Hongzhu.



In her past life, this girl hadn't come. In this life, she had been specifically invited by Bai Qingning with a personal invitation. She thought Bai Qingning didn't know about her matters, but in reality, Bai Qingning had long since sent people to investigate everything clearly.

In earlier years, Zhao Hongzhu had been considered a favored daughter of heaven in the capital—infinitely glorious, with schemes and methods. Whoever provoked her would be repaid tenfold in kind. The girl before her eyes was one who had once provoked Zhao Hongzhu—her name was Qian Biyu.



It was said that at an imperial banquet, Zhao Hongzhu had schemed to push Qian Biyu into a lake. Qian Biyu's clothes became completely soaked before all the powerful nobles of the court. Although Yuanjia customs were open, Qian Biyu was still an unmarried girl at that time. Summer clothes were all made of silk, thin as a single layer. Once soaked through, it was no different from being half-naked. Qian Biyu lost tremendous face. The marriage that had been under discussion was also delayed. For a long time afterward, she couldn't find a suitable husband. Watching herself grow older and older, she could only grit her teeth last year and choose a poor scholar, finally marrying this winter.



Now, Zhao Hongzhu had been brought back from the northern desert by Qin Shanyue and was living in the Qin residence without title or status. Qian Biyu naturally wanted to come step on her, but before stepping, she needed to first probe what Zhao Hongzhu's current situation was.



At this time, most people in the capital didn't know the Zhao family's case was about to be overturned, nor did they know about the many complex entanglements behind Zhao Hongzhu. They only knew that the Zhao family had fallen on hard times, and General Qin, remembering old affections, had brought her back from the northern desert. But after bringing her back, they didn't know how she would be dealt with—would she be taken as a concubine, or kept as an outside mistress? So naturally they had to ask, and conveniently probe what attitude this General's wife Bai Qingning had.



"Sister Zhao was raised under the Old Madam's care since childhood," Bai Qingning pretended not to see the mockery and probing in these people's eyes, only saying with a smile: "She's no different from half a daughter to the Old Madam. My husband says he will find Sister Zhao a good marriage match in the future."



Bai Qingning spoke candidly, so those who were speculating whether Qin Shanyue and Zhao Hongzhu had a private affair felt embarrassed to speak up, and could only suppress their curiosity and stop asking.



While they were talking, a commotion sounded from outside—the Old Madam had personally brought Zhao Hongzhu.



Old Madam Qin had imperial honors bestowed upon her and held unique prestige in the entire rear courtyard. All the female family members had to pay their respects. Old Madam Qin treated these outsiders indifferently, but kept Zhao Hongzhu's hand in hers the entire time, truly treating her like her own daughter in word and deed.



Everyone in the room had different thoughts, pairs of eyes constantly sweeping over Zhao Hongzhu and Bai Qingning's faces, but one wore a gentle smile while the other had warm brows and eyes—no one could detect any outward emotions.



Bai Qingning had died once—she truly didn't care about these people's gazes. But Zhao Hongzhu was calculating other matters.



At this banquet, Bai Qingning controlled the entire venue throughout. Zhao Hongzhu didn't even have a chance to speak with a few people—she couldn't connect with a single old friend, and could only dutifully stay by Old Madam Qin's side the entire time, making Zhao Hongzhu feel somewhat constrained.



When Old Madam Qin grew tired, Zhao Hongzhu used "escorting Old Madam Qin back to her room" as an excuse and went down together with Old Madam Qin.



But after Zhao Hongzhu escorted Old Madam Qin back, she turned around from the Old Madam's courtyard and returned, silently walking from the guest banquet front hall to the side room behind Qin Shanyue's guest reception courtyard, asking as she walked: "How are the arrangements?"



The maid following behind Zhao Hongzhu replied quietly: "General Qin is already in the room."



Zhao Hongzhu slowly responded with a "Mm."



These days, she had been working hard to repair her relationship with Qin Shanyue, but she had underestimated Bai Qingning's weight in Qin Shanyue's heart. Qin Shanyue clearly had developed feelings for her again, yet he kept bitterly enduring, refusing to relent.



She could only force Qin Shanyue this once, using her own chastity to force him.



So Zhao Hongzhu drugged Qin Shanyue. She did it cleanly and efficiently, having a maid tamper with Qin Shanyue's cup at the men's seating area. When the matter came to light later, she could push all the blame onto the maid, only saying that the maid had long plotted against Qin Shanyue, wanting to use her body to gain the position of concubine. And she was merely an innocent victim who accidentally entered the side room and had her body taken by Qin Shanyue.



She knew this was despicable, but she had only this one path to walk. Qin Shanyue rigidly guarded that line—even having developed feelings, he refused to touch her. As time went on, her status in the Qin family would only become more and more awkward. If she couldn't ascend to the clouds, she could only drag Qin Shanyue down into the mud.



Zhao Hongzhu took a deep breath and resolutely stepped into the side room. The maid sensibly withdrew some distance.



Upon entering the side room, Zhao Hongzhu smelled thick alcohol fumes mixed with a man's scent.



This was a side room with its back to the light. Rays fell on the carved wooden window, illuminating the floor in neat lines and frames. A figure lay prostrate on the bed, hidden behind layered curtains. The form couldn't be seen clearly—only suppressed groaning sounds could be heard.



It must be Qin Shanyue.



Zhao Hongzhu took a deep breath and began gradually loosening her clothes and untying her sash.



She knew Qin Shanyue was by nature steady and good at endurance, so she had given him three times the normal dosage. The medicine woman who sold her the drug had said that no matter who it was, even a general who had fought on battlefields, would lose control because of it. Afterward he might lose his memory, and when it happened, he might even force himself on her—she would need to endure the pain.



Zhao Hongzhu thought—what she feared least was pain. No matter what kind of pain, she could endure it.



Moreover, Qin Shanyue's pain—she was willing to receive it. The more she hurt today, the better her days would be in the future.



Her last gauze garment fell to the floor. Zhao Hongzhu, her pale tender toes bare, stepped into the bed curtains step by step.



The bed curtains were layered upon layers, the interior pitch dark. Zhao Hongzhu couldn't see anything clearly. She mustered her courage and touched the other person's hand.



That burning hot male body shuddered, then like a fierce tiger pouncing on prey, directly lunged onto Zhao Hongzhu. Zhao Hongzhu's thin spine crashed heavily into the bedding. The man's body pressed down fiercely.



When the moment arrived, some unease and panic surged into her mind. No woman wouldn't be afraid.



But this was the path she had chosen.



Zhao Hongzhu closed her eyes, lying prostrate on the bed, gritting her teeth and enduring.



Only when her flower bud was broken did Zhao Hongzhu shed tears.



She had also once imagined a wedding night with a hall full of guests, a thousand red candles reflecting faces, red silk parading the streets with firecrackers bursting, laughing and chatting cheerfully while exchanging wine cups. But who would have thought--



The maid outside the door, hearing those sounds, couldn't help but blush and walk farther away. The maid's face was red, but her heart was exceptionally joyful.



After today, their young miss would be General Qin's woman.



Then, those people outside who curry favor with the powerful wouldn't bully their young miss anymore.



The maid kept watch on the left side of the side room, but didn't notice that on a small path to the right side of the side room, someone was walking over gracefully.



—--



Qian Biyu walked alone through the General's residence courtyard.



The General's residence was very large—the most expansive estate on all of Qilin Street. The grounds were quite vast, with flower bushes all around. Beneath her feet was expensive Dali black stone. She walked along the cracks in the ground, thinking she didn't know how much longer it would take to walk back. She really couldn't recognize the way.



The Qin residence had been an imperial meritorious noble's princely mansion in earlier years, later bestowed upon the Qin family. But the Qin family only produced military talent—three branches, all twenty-four sons died on the battlefield, leaving only the current Qin Shanyue. So most of the courtyards were uninhabited, with very few maids and servants. Qian Biyu walked alone along the small path for a long time but didn't see a single person to ask for directions.



Qian Biyu could only curse her bad luck under her breath.



When she attended the banquet today, she had accidentally been bumped by a maid who knocked over a wine cup, the wine soiling her gauze skirt. Fortunately, Madam Qin was well-prepared and had already set aside new skirts, and arranged for a maid to take her to change.



She could only withdraw first to change clothes. But after changing and coming out, she found the maid had disappeared. She could only resignedly walk through the courtyard. Fortunately, there was only one path, so she kept following this path.



Walking along, when Qian Biyu passed by a side room, she heard strange sounds. At first she didn't realize what it was, but when she became aware, her face immediately flushed with embarrassment.



This! In broad daylight, someone was actually engaging in lustful acts here!



Qian Biyu turned to leave immediately. She had to get far away from here—her reputation as a young lady couldn't be ruined by this!



But when Qian Biyu walked to the side room entrance, she suddenly saw a familiar figure. The person was guarding at the side room door with a cautious and careful expression.



She recognized this maid!



This was Zhao Hongzhu's personal maid, as close as sisters with Zhao Hongzhu. If she was guarding the door here, could the person inside be--



—--



When she guessed who was inside, Qian Biyu's fingertips turned pale from gripping, not from tension, but from excitement.



If she had to pick the person she hated most in her life, that person would definitely be Zhao Hongzhu. Because of Zhao Hongzhu, she had once become the laughingstock of the entire capital. Also because of Zhao Hongzhu, her previously arranged ideal husband flew away. All the good families with power and influence in the capital didn't want her, and she looked down on the bad families. So she was forced to languish in her boudoir for three years. Finally, when she was almost at the age where she'd be fined according to the standing law, she gritted her teeth and chose a poor scholar.



A marriage far beneath her station—the lowest of the low.



And now, the culprit who had harmed her in the past was in such a predicament!



She needed to think of a pretext to attract enough people and catch the people inside in the act of adultery right in bed.



Qian Biyu's fingertips gripped the fan in her hand so tightly they turned white. She endured for a moment on the spot, then thought of an excellent plan.

chapters.title: Seven
chapters.content:
In the Qin family's main hall, Qin Shanyue sat drinking wine with several high officials from the court.



This victory banquet had invited many people—basically all bringing their families. There were also many spirited young gentlemen who didn't understand court affairs, only harboring hearts full of romance. Naturally, they couldn't sit still in the front hall. After eating, they all made excuses to wander randomly through the courtyard—right next to the courtyard was where the women were seated. In such circumstances, young men and women encountering each other wasn't considered improper. If they met someone they admired, they could even boldly step forward and invite them to view flowers together.



Never mind what major national affairs those adults were discussing—in these youths' hearts, there was only room for a single hairpin flower.



With those troublesome children gone, after drinking for a while, the several high officials drank their way into the study. Outside stood Qin Shanyue's trusted guards on watch. Inside the room, the conversation shifted from romance and poetry to court affairs.



Every matter in the court had blood, tears, and dust wedged between each word. Speaking of them was easy, but those sinking and floating within knew how dangerous it was. Everyone sitting in the study wore serious expressions. Even the faint wine smell on their sleeves was nearly dispersed by the study's cold atmosphere.



"Although the Emperor is suppressing it without speaking, we privately already have some leads." Qin Shanyue sat behind the desk, several letters laid out before him. He casually passed them out, saying: "Those involved in the treason back then—it should be Prince Duan."



Prince Duan—the current Emperor's own younger brother.



Back then, Prince Duan and the Emperor were blood brothers. Later they had a falling out over the same woman. Simply put, Prince Duan's legitimate wife, properly married through matchmakers, was abducted into the palace by the Emperor, given a new name and made an imperial concubine. Later this imperial concubine either ran away or died—in any case, the imperial city was thrown into chaos. Prince Duan and the Emperor even drew swords on each other. Their brotherly affection became more fragmented and colder than the fine snow outside.



Back then, this ridiculous affair was talked about throughout the entire capital. Later, Prince Duan went to the frontier, killed his way to fame and merit, then was enfeoffed outside. He should have been able to live out his years peacefully there, but after the Emperor grew old, his paranoia arose. He always felt Prince Duan would rebel, so he ordered Prince Duan recalled and detained in the capital, kept under his watchful eye, using the excuse that Prince Duan's health was poor and he was returning to the capital to recuperate.



As he was being kept, the Zhao family treason matter arose.



Everyone in the capital who knew some inside information thought in their hearts that one of these imperial brothers would die sooner or later. Either the one above would kill Prince Duan before dying, unable to rest easy, or the one below would accumulate enough power and stab the one above.



Therefore, both sides couldn't bear to hear the word "treason." The more they feared something, the more they had to investigate it. When things got intense, it was said that on every court official's rooftop, two Embroidered Uniform Guards would crouch all night. Whoever dared mention these matters would be directly thrown in prison, taken for a trip to the Northern Suppression Bureau. Even if innocent, half their life would be gone.



"Now, to overturn the Zhao family's case, we must expose Prince Duan. But to expose Prince Duan, I'm afraid the entire court will be thrown into chaos."



"Since the Emperor has already sent the Embroidered Uniform Guard to investigate, he has already decided to eliminate the problem root and branch. Right now the Emperor's dragon body is unwell, and the Crown Prince's wings aren't yet fully grown. The Emperor is probably trying to clear the path for the Crown Prince."



One of the gentlemen sitting below was the Vice Minister of War. In earlier years, he had been personally promoted by Old Master Zhao and remembered his teacher's grace. Over these years, he had been secretly investigating Old Master Zhao's treason case with Qin Shanyue. Seeing there was now a direction but being forcibly stuck, he couldn't help feeling irritated. His speech became somewhat unguarded. Relying on the fact that outsiders couldn't hear, he bluntly revealed those secret matters: "This humble official has been making inquiries everywhere these past days and heard a secret rumor. It's said that when Prince Duan entered the capital in recent years, he's been constantly inquiring about a missing child."

Pausing for a moment, the Vice Minister of War lowered his voice and said: "I heard from that informant that the lost one is the son of that imperial concubine from back then. Only, I don't know whether he's Prince Duan's or—"



That imperial concubine from back then had truly bewitched both the Emperor and Prince Duan. It was said that for a period of time, the Emperor lavished endless favor on her, while Prince Duan secretly had illicit relations with the imperial concubine. The front foot would barely leave before the back foot climbed into bed. A eunuch once said he personally saw a pair of men's jade boots hidden under the imperial concubine's bed. In the end, no one knew whose child was in that belly. Some also secretly spread that the imperial concubine's disappearance back then was the Empress Dowager's doing because she couldn't stand to watch anymore.



In any case, there were all kinds of stories, but the result was only one—the Emperor and Prince Duan, blood brothers, hated each other to the bone. The Empress Dowager had turned against both sons. The three most noble people in the imperial city had reached the point of crossing swords, with their subordinates fighting to the death for them.



Qin Shanyue's reach extended to the frontier. He didn't know much about the dark private matters of the court. Hearing this now, he only felt it was absurd.



Elder brother seizing younger brother's wife—how could anyone do such a thing?



Just as he was about to say "Then investigate that missing child's matter as well," he heard the Vice Minister of War say again: "That child was lost from a young age. There's nothing special about him, except there's a butterfly-shaped birthmark on his back, said to be identical to the one on the imperial concubine's body."



Qin Shanyue pinched the bridge of his nose and asked: "How old now?"



"It's said he's twenty-one now, should have received his cap ceremony, but growing up outside, who knows what he looks like." The Vice Minister of War shook his head. Just as he said this, a commotion suddenly came from outside, along with maids' shouts.



"What's the matter?" Qin Shanyue immediately led the various officials out from the study. The matters they were discussing were too secret—they had to be extremely careful.



"In reply to the General, they say a side room outside has caught fire." The trusted guard at the door clasped his fists: "This subordinate didn't dare leave his post without permission, so I've been standing guard the whole time."



"Go take a look first." Qin Shanyue casually gave an order, then first led the officials back to the banquet. His front foot had barely arrived at the banquet and settled the officials when his back foot went to where the fire was.



Today's grand banquet had many people coming and going. He feared that with things happening so suddenly, Bai Qingning couldn't manage alone.



But when he arrived, he unexpectedly discovered many people gathered around that side room. Not only was Bai Qingning there, but some prominent ladies from the capital were also present, along with some unmarried young ladies, all curiously crowding around the entrance. That side room had already been half-consumed by flames, yet the doors and windows were still tightly shut. A maid stood at the door, blocking everyone from entering.



"My young miss is resting." The maid kept repeating those same lines: "No one can go in."



"Resting? Is resting more important than life?" Qian Biyu stood in the crowd. Her face bore a concerned expression, but in her eyes pressed a jumping evil fire: "The fire has already grown so large. Instead of saving your mistress, you're here blocking us. Are you trying to kill your mistress?"



The maid was Zhao Hongzhu's personal maid, so naturally she recognized Qian Biyu. Her face had turned completely red, yet she couldn't refute a single word.



Qian Biyu felt wonderfully light and airy, her whole body comfortable to death.



At that time, outside the window she had seen a bundle of dry firewood and a fire starter—it was like divine inspiration. She had directly set fire behind the building. At first the fire wasn't large and not many people saw it, so she added a bit more. Just then, people came here to view flowers. Very soon she attracted a large group. After the crowd arrived, she mixed into the crowd and led them to this place.

She was afraid the two people inside would escape, so her actions were especially swift. Perhaps Heaven was helping her—her plan was proceeding incredibly smoothly.



"Enough." Bai Qingning at the side spoke up: "First extinguish the fire in the side room, then find two sturdy matrons to go in and search for people. Whether they find anyone or not, those who enter will be rewarded."



Seeing the mistress had spoken, the rest naturally didn't dare say more. Zhao Hongzhu's maid, seeing she couldn't hide it anymore, turned pale and walked before Bai Qingning, saying in a low voice: "Please, Madam, step aside with me."



Bai Qingning walked aside with the maid and heard the maid plead: "I beg Madam to show mercy and disperse the crowd. Our young miss was burned by the fire... when she comes out shortly, I'm afraid she won't be properly clothed, which would be improper and make people laugh at her."



Those pouring water to fight the fire were all Qin family people. Even if they saw something, they could suppress the news. But the noble ladies outside were different—others couldn't seal their mouths.



Bai Qingning put on an appearance as if this was natural and turned to disperse the crowd, but her speed in speaking and acting was too slow. Before the surrounding people had time to step away, the fire-fighting matrons had already rushed inside.



These two matrons were rough-work matrons, sturdy with big courage. In earlier years, one was a butcher's daughter who had slaughtered pigs since childhood. The other had married a constable and had heard countless murder cases. Both had bold personalities and were somewhat reckless. They weren't afraid of fire. As soon as the mistress gave orders, they charged in headfirst. But after charging in just a few steps, the butcher's daughter matron turned back, slapping her thigh and shouting: "Heaven have mercy! Two people inside, clothes all stripped off! Rolling around on the bed embracing each other!"



With this one shout, the young ladies who had been gathered around the building all exploded. Each one covered their face with round fans or handkerchiefs, but their eyes held unusual light, all staring fixedly at the side room.



"Two people?" Bai Qingning widened her eyes in surprise, looking toward the maid and asking: "How can there be two people? Who's inside!"



The maid's face turned redder than the rouge on the young ladies' lips. She bit her lips tightly but couldn't refute a single word.



Beside her, Qian Biyu finally found a chance to speak. Her round fan covered her face, hiding her lips curled up high, but couldn't hide the malice surging in her eyes. Her chin lifted, the hairpin on her head swaying slightly: "Speak up quickly! Who's inside? Could it be some shameful scoundrel? You maid pushing and blocking—are you helping your mistress in an illicit affair?"



The maid naturally also recognized Qian Biyu. She knew this person had a grudge with her young miss back then, so she naturally also knew that as long as Qian Biyu was here today, this matter could never end well. The maid was forced into helplessness, looking at Qian Biyu as if she wanted to swallow Qian Biyu alive.



But Qian Biyu continued fanning the flames from the side: "In broad daylight, under clear heaven, whose young lady is this, whose daughter? To openly conspire and have illicit relations with a man, doing such base things—simply losing all face."



Qian Biyu's words were harsh, but they aroused everyone's curiosity.



Those who came here today were all guests of the Qin residence, almost all from the same circle. Everyone had seen everyone else, had some connection. So who exactly was the woman in this room right now?



Just at this moment, the two matrons had already dragged out a woman. She was wrapped in clothes and bedding, in a terrible state, hair disheveled, exposing large areas of skin. The matrons clearly didn't have time to dress her. When this woman was dragged out, the crowd immediately erupted.



"Isn't that Miss Zhao?"



"Heavens! How could Miss Zhao be here!"



"Who is the man inside?"



"Miss Zhao actually did such things with someone."



"If you ask me, after three years of exile in the northern desert, Zhao Hongzhu probably long ago wasn't pure anymore. It's not surprising she'd do such things."



"I heard people say that place in the northern desert is very chaotic. Barbarian tribes constantly plunder and invade the borders, and there are many wandering bandits. Who knows what Zhao Hongzhu might have encountered."



The Zhao Hongzhu who was dragged out had already fainted. But even in her faint, her brows were tightly furrowed. Clearly she had just suffered great pain, and being smoked by fire, it was normal for her to pass out.



When dragged out, those two matrons found this matter dirty to touch. They crudely threw the person on the ground, then under Bai Qingning's instruction, entered the side room again to find the remaining man.



And Zhao Hongzhu, this young lady whose body was barely covered, was just thrown on the ground like this, lashed by everyone's gazes, commented on with the most vicious words.



Seeing this group speak more and more unpleasantly, the maid couldn't bear it anymore. She quickly rushed forward to shield Zhao Hongzhu, then blocked in front of Zhao Hongzhu, shouting loudly to everyone: "Our young miss hasn't done such filthy things! Don't speak nonsense!"



"Hasn't done it? Today's matter is laid out before everyone's eyes. You still have the face to say she hasn't done it?" As soon as Qian Biyu saw Zhao Hongzhu's face, she seemed to see herself being fished out of the lake back then. Qian Biyu excitedly clenched her fists, shouting loudly: "Your young miss is already in such a state, yet you still dare speak such lies, turning black into white!"



"A woman like Zhao Hongzhu who can be had by anyone—speaking of it truly makes one sick. Who knows who the person inside is? Acting so secretly, it might even be someone's husband!"



After Qian Biyu shouted this, the eyes of all the young ladies present sharpened considerably.



They were all maidens waiting to be married. Their sisters at home also had betrothed husbands. If anyone's fiancé or husband did such a thing, it would truly be sickening to death.



"It's not, it's not someone else's husband!" The maid was pushed to desperation and also began speaking without restraint, stamping her feet and shouting: "Our young miss has never had contact with other people's husbands. The person inside also isn't someone with a fiancée. The person inside, the person inside is—"



"It's the General!" The maid finally couldn't bear it anymore, shouting in an unprecedented, going-all-out voice: "It's the General! My young miss and the General have always admired each other! The General has never forgotten my young miss all these years, and my young miss has always been keeping herself for the General! The two of them have always been thinking of each other. My young miss has never been that kind of fickle woman!"



When Zhao Hongzhu's maid roared out these words, the young ladies who had originally been tense and glaring immediately dropped their full guard. Only when they raised their eyes again to look at that refined and gentle lady at the front of the crowd, their gazes inevitably carried some sympathy.



This maid swore that Zhao Hongzhu and Qin Shanyue mutually delighted in each other, that neither had forgotten the other for many years. Then, where did that place Bai Qingning, who was already the General's wife?



Sure enough, when everyone looked toward Bai Qingning, this lady was already covering her face, stepping back several steps with an expression of disbelief. Her feet stumbled, nearly falling. That pitiful appearance made the surrounding young ladies inevitably feel sympathy.

chapters.title: Eight
chapters.content:
They were all women, all noble ladies from wealthy families. From childhood they had all heard endless teachings from their family elders. They had to be mistresses of the household, manage domestic affairs, bear children to continue the family line, support their natal families. When their husbands took concubines they had to endure it. When wronged they had to endure it. When pressured by mothers-in-law above, they still had to endure it. Everything had to be endured.



Today it was Bai Qingning standing here being laughed at by everyone. But wouldn't it be them tomorrow?



If they had truly come at first just to watch the excitement, now seeing Bai Qingning looking so desolate and sad, they only felt they could relate.



"How could it be the General?" At this time, Bai Qingning was also being supported by someone. She turned back, her face as bright and pure as the moon over mountains now filled with grief. Tears swirled in her eyes, slowly falling down her cheeks. She looked like a white lotus swaying in the rain, as if about to be crushed by wind and rain, bending at the waist, clothes soaked through—so sorrowful that anyone who saw would want to step forward and wipe away a tear for her.



"It's impossible, my General couldn't possibly." Bai Qingning cried more and more fiercely, tears rolling down from her eye sockets. Her nose tip and eyes all turned red, looking heartbreaking: "The General said he would find a good family to marry Zhao Hongzhu to. How could he possibly have illicit relations with Zhao Hongzhu?"



Hearing this, the surrounding people felt unbearable pity. Then Qian Biyu spoke up: "Some people enjoy the benefits of others while also ruining their marriages. If you're going to marry, why set up a chastity arch? Concubine is concubine, aunt is aunt. What does this count as now? Putting on airs, using the identity of 'old flame' and 'honored guest' to live in someone's house, even making them serve you well—how shameless!"



"Exactly! It would be better to honestly be an outside mistress! Now without title or status, entangling with someone's husband in their house, stealing right under their nose—truly inauspicious to death!"



"General Qin has been wise all his life—how could he do such things? Zhao Hongzhu was considered a well-bred lady in earlier years. She's truly disgraced her father and brothers."



"The pitiful one is still Madam Qin! To discover her husband having illicit relations with someone else in such circumstances—imagine how humiliated she must be."



Amid the voices of condemnation, even Zhao Hongzhu's most protective maid lowered her head in shame.



In such matters, truly their young miss was in the wrong. They weren't qualified to speak.



And Bai Qingning covered her face with a handkerchief, quietly putting on an appearance of heartbreak, hiding in the crowd watching the show.



The side room was still that side room, the maid still that maid, but the situation had already changed—a hundred turns and twists.



In her past life, when she accidentally discovered such things, she had cried inconsolably, cursing Qin Shanyue again and again, cursing Zhao Hongzhu.



At that time, Qin Shanyue lay motionless on the bed, while Zhao Hongzhu knelt before her, begging her to fulfill them. She couldn't calm down and continued cursing. That maid, protecting her mistress, jumped out. The person knelt on the ground, but her head was raised, saying with righteous indignation: "Our young miss and the General admired and relied on each other in earlier years. If it weren't for Madam inserting herself, they would have had children together long ago! Why must Madam press so hard today?"



Even after two lifetimes, Bai Qingning remembered that scene.



The man she deeply loved lay indulgently on the bed, still unconscious. Zhao Hongzhu knelt on the ground pleading. And another maid dredged up all those past events, throwing them in her face sentence by sentence.



She was the one betrayed, she was the most innocent one, yet everyone bullied her. Because she was also a loser. Whether in the circumstances at that time or the results afterward, she hadn't won a single thing.



Losers were meant to be stepped on, bullied, skinned and boned, then cursed with "delusional fantasies." It didn't matter whether you were the innocent one—once the victory was decided, you deserved to die.



But now it was different.



She only needed to stand here. The rest would naturally be handled by others. In her past life, these people took it for granted to oppress her because she didn't know how to borrow势力 (power/influence), because she was at a disadvantage, because bullying her meant no one would stand up for her.



But now, her势头 (momentum/power) was established. Zhao Hongzhu had been completely trampled down by her. Today's humiliation would accompany Zhao Hongzhu forever. As long as Zhao Hongzhu lived for one more day, others would never forget this matter.



In this lifetime, Zhao Hongzhu would never again be like her past life—receiving an imperial marriage decree from the Emperor and marrying into the Qin residence openly and honorably.



Bai Qingning's thoughts had just turned here when footsteps suddenly came from the distance, mixed with some male voices. The unmarried female family members present all withdrew, but didn't go far, only standing at a distance watching.



After male guests arrived, the maid on the ground finally couldn't bear it anymore. She kowtowed to Bai Qingning begging for mercy: "Madam, I beg you, please take my young miss away."



After such a good show had occurred, without Bai Qingning speaking, the surrounding maids and matrons all dared not move. They just watched their mistress and servant like watching a monkey show. Before there were only female guests, which was still acceptable. Now that male guests had come, if they didn't take away their young miss, Zhao Hongzhu would truly be finished.



So the maid knelt on the ground and began kowtowing.



Bai Qingning was born with an indifferent and gentle temperament. She didn't love arguing right and wrong with people or competing for superiority. But after dying once, she understood—if she didn't争 (compete), didn't抢 (grab), didn't辩 (argue), then people would come take advantage of her. Once she truly stood up and retaliated tenfold, a hundredfold, those people instead began not daring to provoke her and even had to kneel down begging her.



Speaking of it all, it was nothing more than these four characters: bullying the weak and fearing the strong.



"Take her away." Bai Qingning waved her hand, and two matrons stepped forward to lift Zhao Hongzhu.



Zhao Hongzhu was unconscious like rotten mud. When lifted up, the clothes on her body that hadn't been properly arranged slid down, exposing large areas of skin.



The maid hurriedly shielded her again.



Delayed for this short while, the male guests from afar had already nearly walked over. Someone looked from afar at that group of male guests and couldn't help crying out in surprise: "Isn't that the General?"



The crowd immediately erupted again like a pot boiling over, looking toward that direction. They discovered that today's show at the Qin family was truly one wave after another, ups and downs—they couldn't even finish a complete sentence. As long as they watched two glances less or heard two sentences less, the situation would gallop like an unbridled wild horse. How could a single phrase "unexpected" explain it clearly?



"Why is the General here?" Qian Biyu was the first to speak. When she saw Qin Shanyue, her fingernails nearly dug into her own flesh. Her voice rose to an almost piercing pitch: "Then who is that man inside?"



The crowd immediately fell into chaos. Even more shocked than Qian Biyu was Zhao Hongzhu's maid. The maid's originally flushed face turned white with a "swoosh." She looked at Qin Shanyue walking over in disbelief, her lips trembling. For a long while she couldn't speak a single word.

Who was the man inside?



Their young miss had clearly drugged General Qin!



So who did Zhao Hongzhu actually sleep with?



Just as everyone was in complete confusion, Bai Qingning spoke. She first had people send away the unconscious Zhao Hongzhu and her maid together, then asked the ladies present to all leave.



Since Madam Qin had spoken, what came next was clearly family disgrace. Bai Qingning wanted to cover it up, and others couldn't very well stubbornly pry, so they had to leave.



Qian Biyu deliberately hung back a step, pretending to walk slowly, even purposely dropping her handkerchief, finally dawdling until the man inside was dragged out.



The two matrons dragging this man out were exhausted. A man's body was heavy, not light and petite like a woman's. The matrons were panting heavily with difficulty as they dragged out a man whose upper body was naked and lower body was carelessly wrapped in white undergarments. This man's back was covered in scratches from fingernails, making the unmarried girl Qian Biyu's face flush red with embarrassment.



And in the next instant, the man was thrown on the ground, allowing Qian Biyu to see his face clearly!



It was a face of gentlemanly propriety, gentle and refined as jade, only with his face flushed red from drunkenness and his hair in disarray. But even with just this hasty glance, it was enough for Qian Biyu to see clearly who this was!



The eldest legitimate son of the Bai family, Bai Yunhe, who held the official position of Minister of Justice. He was the object of affection for countless young ladies in the capital. Although the Bai family's rise to power was recent and their foundation thin, Bai Yunhe had good looks and an unlimited future. He was also quite self-disciplined—there wasn't even a single concubine or secondary consort in his household. It was said that Bai Yunhe's family values were strict, and he absolutely would not take concubines until he had a legitimate son.



Just the fact that his rear courtyard was peaceful made countless women's hearts flutter. In earlier years, Bai Yunhe had many noble ladies secretly sending him admiring glances. But later, Bai Yunhe gained the favor of the Minister of Justice, who personally taught him, and so naturally became engaged to the Minister of Justice's second legitimate daughter. They were to be married next year.



Half of what Bai Yunhe had achieved today was due to the support and cultivation of the Minister of Justice. Following the path ahead, Bai Yunhe would become the Minister of Justice.



But now, he had actually rolled into bed with Zhao Hongzhu! Could the Minister of Justice tolerate this?



If it had been another woman, perhaps they could think up some excuse and suppress it. But this was Zhao Hongzhu! The Zhao Hongzhu who was entangled unclearly with Qin Shanyue!



Qian Biyu's mind spun rapidly in circles. Thinking it through, she suddenly realized that this Bai Yunhe was also Bai Qingning's eldest legitimate brother!



Circles of developments and strings of interpersonal relationships flashed through her mind, even more tangled than the balls of silk thread she wound when doing embroidery, all mixed up together in chaos. She couldn't figure it out.



Qian Biyu wasn't particularly clever, but she knew this matter was of great importance. So she pressed this matter firmly into her belly, deciding that before things became clear, she wouldn't speak of it—in any case, Zhao Hongzhu was already finished, and she had no grudge against Bai Yunhe. If this matter came out of her mouth, who knows what trouble it might bring. Better to let it rot in her belly.



Qian Biyu hurriedly got up, lifted her skirts, and chased after the crowd ahead.



At this point, the female guests finally exited. After the female guests left, the male guests arrived. When Qin Shanyue came over, Bai Qingning had already ordered other servants to carry Bai Yunhe away and send him to a side room nearby.

Qin Shanyue only saw a disheveled figure from behind and a room that had been burned by fire, doused with water, with smoke curling up in a particularly choking manner, as well as Bai Qingning standing alone in front of the room.



Qin Shanyue hadn't seen Bai Qingning in a long time. He felt guilty and didn't dare go to Lotus Courtyard to find Bai Qingning. The more he missed Bai Qingning in his heart, the less he dared to see her, to the point that now when he suddenly saw Bai Qingning, he had a feeling as if lifetimes had passed.



The woman standing there had her hair casually styled in a Flying Immortal Flowing Cloud bun, with only a single dark green jade hairpin as decoration. Black hair wound around the green hairpin, her features like misty mountains. A light white dress wrapped her slender shoulders, a pale blue waistband tightly and firmly cinched her waistline, drawing out a fine, startlingly beautiful line. From Qin Shanyue's direction looking over, he only felt that Bai Qingning was like the Goddess Peak standing in thin mist, every strand of hair revealing heaven's meticulous carving of beauty—pure, elegant, and yet unreachable.



Qin Shanyue's heart stirred. He quickly walked over, but heard Bai Qingning say in a cool tone: "I trouble the General to first go entertain the guests. After the banquet matters are concluded, I will tell the General what happened at the banquet."



Qin Shanyue had wanted to say "I didn't come to ask what happened, I just wanted to see you," but when these words reached his lips and he saw Bai Qingning's cold expression, he swallowed them back.



Qingning was clearly still angry with him.



Qin Shanyue could only swallow back his bellyful of longing, turn around and go back to deal with the other guests at the banquet. Because something had happened in the middle that Qin Shanyue wasn't clear about, the guests at the banquet soon dispersed in twos and threes.



Only, for some reason, when the guests walked to the door and Qin Shanyue went to see them off, those womenfolk always looked at him with a strange gaze.



When he returned to the courtyard, he discovered that the maids in the residence also seemed to be trembling with fear. The entire Qin residence was permeated with a strange atmosphere. He found it increasingly strange, so he first went to Lotus Courtyard.



He wanted to know what exactly had happened.

chapters.title: Nine
chapters.content:
When Qin Shanyue returned to Lotus Courtyard, he discovered that there were servants constantly coming and going in the courtyard. Some servants had even invited a physician, who was being led to the side room with a medicine box.

Qin Shanyue thought Bai Qingning had fallen ill, so his steps involuntarily quickened. But when he walked into Lotus Courtyard, he saw Bai Qingning sitting at the stone table in the garden, with Chunri standing beside her, serving tea.

Scalding boiling water swirled the tender green tea tips round and round against the white cup walls. Curling hot steam rose to one's fingertips. Chunri avoided the steam and just then saw Qin Shanyue walk to the stone table.

Seeing the General had arrived, Chunri quickly retreated two steps, not daring to listen to the conversation between the Madam and the General.

The events at today's banquet had already spread among the maids. The Qin family's household rules were strict, and such matters were simply unheard of to them. Every maid didn't show it on their faces, but they were all thinking about it in their hearts.

Moreover, the two people involved in the matter were now in the side room of Lotus Courtyard.

"Qingning." Qin Shanyue's brows knitted together like thick ink, his gaze constantly sweeping over the people coming and going in Lotus Courtyard, his voice continuously dropping: "What on earth happened?"

Bai Qingning liked quiet. The maids serving inside were limited in number. Other people would be stopped at the door and not allowed to enter randomly. This was the first time Lotus Courtyard was so lively. Not only were errand-running servants from the outer courtyard constantly going back and forth, but even a medicine woman had been invited from outside.

The number of people in their Qin household could be counted on one's fingers. Those who truly counted as masters, besides Old Madam Qin, were only Qin Shanyue and Bai Qingning. Now the two of them were both here, so who else could require such a commotion?

The thoughts in Qin Shanyue's heart grew heavier and heavier. He knew that in the entire Qin household, there was only that one person—Zhao Hongzhu.

Whether he wanted to mention it or not, something must have happened to Zhao Hongzhu.

"Today when I was at the banquet, I heard a maid below come report that a fire had started over at the west side room in the back. At that time, I happened to run into a circle of noble ladies. When I went to handle it, there were many people there."

Bai Qingning sat upright on the stone stool, her fingers holding up a cup of tea. The full moon fell into the teacup, rippled by her red lips. Tea fragrance spread around her, gently dispersing with her soft tone.

But what she said was not so pleasant.

"There was someone in the burning room. I called for matrons to go in and rescue them, and discovered the person inside was Zhao Hongzhu." When Bai Qingning said this, she slowly put down the teacup in her hand and lifted her eyes to look at Qin Shanyue.

She hadn't carefully looked at this person's features in two lifetimes. Now taking a careful look, she only felt it was unfamiliar.

Qin Shanyue's expression suddenly changed: "Zhao Hongzhu, what happened to her?"

Bai Qingning curved a mocking smile.

The general she had loved—the one with righteousness for family and country, a heart embracing all under heaven, whose word was worth nine tripods, upright and incorruptible, who had promised her a lifetime together—had already died in that snowfall. The person standing before her now said with his mouth that he had no romantic feelings for Zhao Hongzhu, said he would find a good family for Zhao Hongzhu to marry into, wishing he could swear oaths and stake all his bones to add weight to these vows. But as long as there was the slightest ripple, all his persistence and integrity seemed to be completely shattered, becoming completely unrecognizable.

"I don't know what happened to her either. I didn't enter the sea of fire—two matrons went in." Bai Qingning lifted her chin to the side, and two matrons came forward. They were the same two matrons who had dragged Zhao Hongzhu out earlier. Bai Qingning had rewarded them each with twenty taels of silver, which was two and a half years' income for them.

Both matrons were coarse-minded women who usually just did rough work. Once they received the silver, they were so happy their mouths couldn't close. Bai Qingning had never given them any verbal warnings, so their hearts were floating, and they spoke without thinking. Bai Qingning just lifted her chin toward them, and the two poured out everything like beans from a bamboo tube, without any embellishment or tactful phrasing.

"The side room was on fire, and us two old servants went in to rescue people. Oh my, as soon as we entered, we saw Miss Zhao rolling on the bed with a man. The two were doing that filthy business, and they didn't care even though the fire had started. We took another look—that man was drunk, and Miss Zhao was unconscious. So we two old servants hurriedly dragged Miss Zhao out."

After the matron finished speaking, she added: "Miss Zhao's body was covered with all those marks. Even the medicine woman who came to examine her kept shaking her head."

A medicine woman was a female physician who specialized in treating the madams and unmarried young ladies in households, specifically dealing with women's matters. Generally, when women in wealthy households wanted to conceive or regulate their bodies, they would invite a medicine woman. If the medicine woman shook her head after examining her, clearly Zhao Hongzhu had been tormented quite miserably.

When hearing these words, Qin Shanyue was at first bewildered. In his heart, he loved, respected, and felt regret toward Zhao Hongzhu. To Qin Shanyue, Zhao Hongzhu was the cinnabar mole on his chest, remembered by Qin Shanyue at every moment. Qin Shanyue would forever hold her up high, not letting anyone hurt her.

But now, his cinnabar mole had been violated by another person, and she had been carried out in front of everyone—her reputation was completely ruined.

This was a pain Qin Shanyue could not accept. He could accept Zhao Hongzhu hiding in the northern desert, could accept Zhao Hongzhu suffering hardships and losing wealth and glory, could even accept Zhao Hongzhu marrying someone else, but he could not accept Zhao Hongzhu being trampled like this.

His Hongzhu should have been cherished by everyone.

Thinking of what Zhao Hongzhu had suffered, Qin Shanyue hated himself to the extreme.

He had said he would protect Zhao Hongzhu! He had promised Zhao Hongzhu, promised Zhao family's deceased elder brother, but he hadn't been able to marry Zhao Hongzhu, and now he couldn't even protect Zhao Hongzhu. This person had met with trouble right under his nose!

A surge of violent anger rolled in his chest. Qin Shanyue wished he could kill everyone who knew about this matter!

After the two matrons finished speaking, they realized Qin Shanyue's expression was as cold and heavy as the moat in the twelfth lunar month. Just one look, and that bone-chilling cold rushed straight to their faces. Faintly, there was also suppressed fury, like a male lion whose territory had been plundered. Even the veins on his forehead were trembling.

The matrons were all terrified and didn't dare speak awkwardly. Just as they were feeling uneasy, they saw Bai Qingning wave her hand, and the two of them hurriedly left.

"Who was it." After the matrons had all left, Qin Shanyue squeezed out two words from between his teeth.

"The situation is still uncertain at the moment. It's not good to say the specific reason. I ask the General to please wait a bit, until—"

"Who was it!" Qin Shanyue's explosive roar suddenly rang out, almost exploding right above Bai Qingning's head.

Bai Qingning's hand holding the porcelain cup paused, then she coolly raised her head, stared fixedly at the furious Qin Shanyue, and said in a calm voice: "If the General wants to know so badly, why not go inside and take a look. It's in the east side room."

Bai Qingning's expression was indifferent, her tone also revealing distant coldness. Qin Shanyue knew that Bai Qingning was still angry with him because of those matters, but he couldn't care about Bai Qingning's dissatisfaction anymore. Zhao Hongzhu had suffered such wrong—his heart was cut to shreds. How could he care about anyone else?

Bai Qingning just watched as Qin Shanyue charged into the east side room like a raging bull. Soon, panicked voices rang out from the room, along with the screams of maids and servants, and finally the sound of fists hitting flesh.

The people inside made a commotion for about a quarter of an hour before Bai Qingning lifted her skirts and walked to the side room door.

She stepped across the deep red threshold. Before her eyes was a ground full of kneeling maids and servants. The old physician was so frightened he clutched his medicine box tightly, wanting to leave but not daring to move. He was just an ordinary sitting physician who ran a medicine shop—he had overheard the secrets of the General's household. Could he still walk out this door?

In the innermost part of the side room, Qin Shanyue was gripping Bai Yunhe's neck, forcing Bai Yunhe to kneel on the ground. Bai Yunhe only wore undergarments, and a mass of bright red blood had been coughed out at his chest—clearly he had been punched by Qin Shanyue and suffered internal injuries.

This already counted as restraint. Bai Yunhe was just a weak scholar who had properly risen through the imperial examinations, an ordinary common man. Given Qin Shanyue's strength, if one punch didn't kill him, that already counted as holding back.

"Speak! Who made you do such a thing? Did you have evil intentions toward Zhao Hongzhu and force yourself on her!" Qin Shanyue's roar shook people's ears, making them buzz. The maids kneeling on the ground pressed their heads to the floor, their entire bodies trembling.

"All of you, leave." Bai Qingning waved at those maids and servants, her water sleeves gently swaying. Those maids left as if granted amnesty.

At this moment, Bai Yunhe had already been beaten until his face was covered in blood. His hair was loose, piled messily on his shoulders, and he had lost a tooth. When he spoke, it was slurred: "I don't know. My condition wasn't right. I must have been drugged by someone. Don't pile everything on me alone! That Zhao Hongzhu—I've barely met her a few times. Why don't you go ask Zhao Hongzhu?"

Bai Yunhe was the Vice Minister of Justice. He had handled many cases and could be considered well-informed. He was also clever. He only needed to turn his mind a bit to know that this incident must have a reason.

He had probably been set up by someone.

"Outrageous! Zhao Hongzhu is innocent, romantic, frank, and straightforward—how could she possibly do such a thing? It must be you who coveted Zhao Hongzhu. You forced yourself on her and did despicable things to her!"

Qin Shanyue's roar echoed in the side room. His eyes were full of bloodshot veins, and his entire body's murderous aura pressed down on people's hearts until they felt stifled. Even the air became thinner.

"How could I possibly do despicable things with her!" Bai Yunhe was in the thick of it—his pressure was even greater than others'. But he absolutely could not yield, nor could he take responsibility for such a catastrophic disaster. So he argued strenuously, directly choosing the sharpest words to counterattack.

"She's the only daughter of the Zhao family. Right now her case is about to be overturned. The winds and clouds in the capital are stirring. Prince Duan is eyeing everything covetously! Why would I wade into these muddy waters? Everyone in the court avoids her by three measures when they see her! Do you think everyone is like you, daring to risk great impropriety by bringing her back? Everyone in the entire capital knows you have undying designs on her! Who would dare to offend you in your Qin residence?"

Bai Yunhe had even mentioned Prince Duan, so at this moment he naturally had no more reservations. He continued: "I already have a marriage engagement. My future father-in-law is my direct superior! My reputation and future prospects are bright—how could I destroy my own Great Wall for the sake of one woman?"

These words were even more frightening than those earlier mentions of the General's household secrets. They faintly hinted at Prince Duan's treason. The old physician beside them was dripping with cold sweat and about to faint. Even Qin Shanyue sobered up somewhat. The hand gripping Bai Yunhe's neck didn't loosen, but it was no longer as forceful as before.

Bai Yunhe got a moment to breathe, and his words came out hoarse and sharp: "Instead of wasting your energy interrogating me, you should go interrogate your Zhao Hongzhu. She wants to overturn the case. She wants someone to help her. I'm the Vice Minister of Justice. I hold countless secrets in my hands. If she wants to clear the Zhao family's name, starting with me is most convenient! She wants to coerce me with such filthy matters!"

Bai Yunhe's speculation was reasonable and logical. This was the most likely scenario he had deduced based on the current situation, but it pierced Qin Shanyue's heart. His eyes suddenly turned crimson. In fury, he threw Bai Yunhe to the ground and with his other hand drew the sword from his waist.

"Impossible." The heavy blade left its sheath with a resounding clang that rang in the ears. Qin Shanyue's blade swept past Bai Yunhe's ear, cutting off a strand of hair. The next second, the blade pressed down, pressing hard against Bai Yunhe's vulnerable neck. Unlike Qin Shanyue's extremely steady hand, his voice was trembling: "Hongzhu wouldn't. It must be you who violated her."

Qin Shanyue's appearance was too terrifying—a posture that wouldn't listen to anything and was determined to take Bai Yunhe's life. Bai Yunhe panicked. His eye caught the blue hem of a skirt beside him. Bai Yunhe hastily sought help: "Second Sister! Say something quickly! Your brother is absolutely not that kind of person. You know it!"

Qin Shanyue's furious mind was startled, and he suddenly looked to the side.

He had completely forgotten about Bai Qingning just now. Now he suddenly remembered—when he was going mad questioning for the sake of another woman, his wife was watching from the side.

The instant Qin Shanyue looked at Bai Qingning, she was turning around to look at the old physician still kneeling on the ground. Qin Shanyue could only see half of her delicate face and her pretty chin.

That face had no ripples—only calm. She nodded slightly and said to the old physician on the ground, "Rise and speak." The old physician tremblingly climbed up, then heard her say: "My brother says he was drugged by someone. Have you examined him? Is there truly such a matter?"

Probably seeing that the old physician was truly frightened, Bai Qingning added: "Today you can only leave by telling the truth. After today, I'll give you fifty taels of gold. You can take the silver and leave the capital. From now on, no one will hold today's matter against you."

The old physician's hands were covered in cold sweat. He clutched the medicine box in his hands, the wrinkles on his face trembling, before he gritted his teeth and opened his mouth under Bai Yunhe's nervous gaze and Qin Shanyue's murderous stare.

"This lord... was indeed drugged by someone. Top-grade aphrodisiac incense, enough to make a person sink into lust for two hours, unable to distinguish right from wrong, acting purely on instinct."

After the old physician finished speaking, Bai Yunhe was the first to struggle. He still couldn't get up, but the old physician's words corroborated his innocence. For a moment he felt both relieved and indignant. The violent anger in his chest couldn't dissipate. He simply maintained his position of being pressed to the ground, lifted his leg, and heavily kicked Qin Shanyue: "Did you hear that? I was framed by that Zhao Hongzhu of yours! The woman you think about day and night would use such disgusting methods to coerce me!"

With a clang, the heavy blade in Qin Shanyue's hand fell to the ground. His expression instantly became ferocious, frightening the old physician into scrambling backward in retreat. But Qin Shanyue couldn't care about this person anymore. He turned around and strode in large steps toward the west side room.

Over there was where Zhao Hongzhu was.

He had to ask Zhao Hongzhu personally.

chapters.title: Ten
chapters.content:
In the west side room, Zhao Hongzhu had awakened. The medicine woman had already left, and the Qin household's maids had all been dismissed. Only Zhao Hongzhu and her trusted personal maid remained in the room.



The trusted maid knelt on the ground, trembling as she recounted everything that had happened. When she finished, she directly prostrated herself on the ground, crying until she nearly fainted.



"Miss, Miss! That man wasn't the General—it was Bai Yunhe of the Bai family! What should we do?" The maid had been crying for a long time without hearing a response. When she raised her head, she saw Zhao Hongzhu sitting on the bed hugging her knees, staring blankly at her own arm in confusion.



On Zhao Hongzhu's hand was a very deep pinch mark. This had been pinched out when she was pressed against the pillow while doing that business. Actually, she hadn't resisted. She had obediently given herself completely. It was just that the person who touched her was too fierce, so various marks were left on her delicate skin.



The one on her hand was merely the lightest. The other marks on her body were too horrible to look at.



Before, she had thought these were marks left by Qin Shanyue. Even if it hurt, it was a sweet pain. But what if these were left by another person?



Wave after wave of cold chills surged up from behind her, shooting straight to Zhao Hongzhu's scalp. Goosebumps rose densely on Zhao Hongzhu's back. Her pair of bright, charming eyes stared vacantly at her fingers. Her originally rosy lips were as pale as rice paper. Her ears were filled with the maid's crying sounds, and her mind was in complete chaos.



This person wasn't Qin Shanyue—it was Bai Yunhe.



She remembered Bai Yunhe, the eldest legitimate son of the Bai family, a man with gentle features who looked quite refined and scholarly. When Bai Yunhe passed the imperial examinations and achieved success that year, she had seen him from afar, but there had been no other interaction.



Why was it Bai Yunhe?



Clearly, clearly she had arranged everything perfectly. She was foolproof. She should have been foolproof!



And who could be the person who could so silently set her up like this?



There were only so many people in the entire Qin household. Besides Old Madam Qin who wholeheartedly loved her and indulged her, and Qin Shanyue who harbored old feelings for her, there was only one other person who had both reason and possibility to make a move against her.
