"Ah, for ones of our standing, all we can do is rely on our looks to serve."

"Once you're in her residence, stop walking around with that stiff face of yours."

"Indeed—she said she'd redeem you and she did, five hundred taels of silver. She really didn't hold back."

"This female guest must really like you. You'd best serve her well."

Amid the commotion all around him, Shen Shizou kept his face taut, closed his eyes as if unable to bear hearing any more, and was led out of Gongzi Garden by Bai Qingning.

What was he to do? This woman...was going to keep him.

——

The moment Shen Shizou was taken away, the proprietor cheerfully found himself a spot to count the money. But as he counted, he began to feel a little regret—had he known this woman would be this generous, he would have asked for a higher price!

The proprietor had only just had this thought when a commotion erupted outside, as if someone was making their way toward his room. Servants were apologizing profusely, but couldn't stop the sound of that person's footsteps at all.

"Sir! This Sir! Please stop—the companion you're asking about has already been purchased by another guest. It's not that we didn't want to take you to arrange a private visit, but by that time, that guest had already taken the person away."

"Sir, oh dear! Sir, your silver won't do either—the person has truly been taken away—"

The broken, intermittent voice came to a stop just outside the door. The proprietor had just put away the silver and barely opened the door—before he could even see who had come—when he was sent sprawling to the ground by a man's kick.

The proprietor let out a yelp and knelt on the ground. Clutching his face, he looked up, and saw a fierce-looking man.

The other man wore a martial short-collar outfit, appeared to be in his forties, with a steady expression and fierce eyes. The moment he caught sight of Shen Shizou, he narrowed his eyes and stared fixedly at Shen Shizou's face, scrutinizing it carefully. Then he directly flung a portrait at the proprietor.

"Where is this person?"

The face in the portrait was unmistakably Shen Shizou's.

The proprietor tremblingly recounted how Bai Qingning had purchased the person and taken him away. The man furrowed his brows and said coldly: "Draw me this woman's appearance. If you dare conceal even half a detail, I'll send you down to meet the King of Hell."

chapters.title: Twenty
chapters.content:
At this moment, Bai Qingning, who had already left Gongzi Garden, had no idea that their whereabouts were being investigated. She had already brought Shen Shizou to the small courtyard she had newly purchased.

The courtyard was not large—it was a small estate near the foot of a mountain at the outer edges of the capital, close to the royal hunting grounds. There were some villages nearby. A quarter-hour's walk would bring you to a market, though getting into the capital proper required over an hour.

The place was not remote—there were people around, yet it also had the quiet of the forest. The grounds were not expansive, a two-courtyard compound. Along the courtyard walls grew trees of a variety called Misty Forest, evergreen through all four seasons. Their leaves were not tender green but a deep, sunken dark jade green, carrying the weight of years well-weathered. The moment you walked into the courtyard, you could smell a crisp, refreshing mountain air mingled with the deep fragrance of pine wood. It was exceptionally pleasant.

"I just purchased this courtyard. Let's call it Misty Forest Courtyard." Bai Qingning led Shen Shizou through the door and said to him: "Your household registration is in the capital, so you are counted as a resident of the capital. From now on, whether you want to buy fields and land, open a shop, go into business—whatever you wish to do—A'Nu, you may do anything you want."

When Shen Shizou heard this, he raised his eyes to look at Bai Qingning before him.

Bai Qingning stood a few feet ahead of him, her skirts swaying in the breeze. The dark green trees and her blue-green skirts reflected off each other, and Bai Qingning's silhouette stood as upright and otherworldly as the misty forest itself.

"Anything?" Shen Shizou finally spoke. His voice was deep and low, resonant and far-reaching as an evening bell.

This was the first time in their acquaintance this lifetime that Shen Shizou had spoken to her in such an unhurried, even tone.

"That's right." Bai Qingning turned her head. Her pair of eyes smiled all the more gently, and even the cool air around her seemed to dissipate somewhat. When she smiled, she was as warm and soft as the moon setting behind returning clouds.

While the two of them spoke, Qiuyue stood not far off waiting for instructions. Seeing Bai Qingning smile like this, Qiuyue wrung her handkerchief in indignation.

This servant hasn't seen Madam smile so happily in a very long time!

What strange and peculiar tricks does this fox spirit possess?!

——

Shen Shizou pressed his thin lips together tightly.

Spending so much silver to redeem him, buying him a residence—this woman—

"Why did you bring me here." Shen Shizou turned his face away, not looking at Bai Qingning. But the corners of his eyes kept drifting back to Bai Qingning's fingers.

A few slender, fair fingers peeked out from her sleeve cuff—like the bright moon in clouds, drawing his gaze straight to them.

"You and I...have a connection." Bai Qingning naturally wouldn't recount everything about her rebirth. She turned it over in her mind, and said only: "I felt you shouldn't be worn away in a place like that. I want better for you."

He suddenly raised his head and stared at Bai Qingning.

Of course! This woman was fond of him, wanted him. Even though she was already another man's wife, she had defied womanly virtue to come find him!

At this thought, Shen Shizou's eyes carried a trace of inexplicable shame. He stared hard at Bai Qingning, as if trying to see through her surface and into whatever she was concealing underneath. Unable to restrain himself, he blurted out: "Aren't you afraid I'll run away?"

She had spent such a great price to redeem him, yet hadn't left even a single servant or maid to keep watch on him. If he ran, wouldn't it all be a wasted effort?

"You may leave whenever you wish." Bai Qingning knew that Shen Shizou had been shut away in Gongzi Garden for so long that he was wary of others, so her tone was even gentler, faintly carrying a trace of tender sympathy: "You may do anything you want. I brought you out because I hope you can live well."

Shen Shizou's heart jolted.

Of—of course!

This woman had deep feelings for him—feelings that had taken root.

"You are already married." Shen Shizou's gaze swept over Bai Qingning's pinned-up hair, then jerked away as if scalded, and his voice turned suddenly cold.

Having already married, how could she—how could she keep him like this?

He had read the books of the sages and trained in martial arts for ten years. He should not be involved in such sordid affairs.

"Ah, you mean that." Bai Qingning touched her own hair bun, and the smile on her face deepened: "Don't worry about it. It will be resolved soon. Those people won't be able to hurt me this time."

Shen Shizou didn't understand what Bai Qingning meant. He looked up at her in confusion, only to see Bai Qingning gazing at him with a warm, full smile.

In the forest, the woman was clear and cool as the moon, her features radiant as blooming flowers.

A'Nu—this time, you don't need to come and be hurt for my sake anymore.

Thinking of this, Bai Qingning was reminded of the affairs back at the General's residence. She still hadn't received her letter of repudiation yet.

"I still have matters to attend to, so I won't be able to come often these next few days. I've left you some silver. I heard from the people at Gongzi Garden that you enjoy reading—I've bought some books and put them in the study. Read them when you have nothing to do. Once I've finished with my matters, I'll come see you. If you want to go out for a walk, you can follow the small path outside. There are a few taverns and teahouses nearby, and the outer city has no curfew—it's quite lively."

After saying all this to Shen Shizou, Bai Qingning turned and walked out. Shen Shizou stood with his back straight and didn't move. Only after Bai Qingning had left did he finally let his spine relax.

He couldn't describe what he felt inside—a tangled mess, like a ball of knotted thread.

This woman was generous with her spending and dressed in fine clothes, clearly from a family of considerable means. A woman like her—he should be beneath her notice. Obviously she only had a measure of interest in him, did genuinely like him, but not so deeply—she would arrange a residence and keep him, but would not give him more.

Naturally she would never live out her days with him in a proper, recognized manner.

What's more, this woman still had a husband.

Shen Shizou felt he could not continue being entangled with this woman. Although she had told him he was free to come and go, he couldn't actually just leave like that. He needed to first find a way to earn five hundred taels, return it to this woman, settle all debts clearly—and then he could leave.

But, if this woman came to want him in the meantime—

Shen Shizou closed his eyes in helpless embarrassment, unable to work out how to reckon this hopeless account. He only felt this place was a swamp of mud—he should leave, he should go—yet he was already sunk deep in it, and no matter what, couldn't move his legs.

After a long while, Shen Shizou turned and walked into the courtyard.

Passing through the Misty Forest trees, he entered the side room. The room had been swept spotlessly clean. Green moss crept up the steps; the grass and trees cast their freshness through the curtains. Inside, there was none of the suffocating mixed fragrance of face powder from Gongzi Garden—only a clear, bright scent of grass and wood.

On the table sat freshly boiled water, still steaming. The bed was clean and neat, soft and dry. After Shen Shizou washed his face and cleaned up, he leaned back on the bed and rested for a while.

He was thinking about what kind of livelihood he should find next. He absolutely could not truly rely on a woman to support him.

Following the plans he had once made, he should be sitting the imperial examinations. If not for what had happened midway—

Several thoughts swept through his mind. Before he knew it, Shen Shizou had fallen asleep leaning against the bed.

He had a dream.

In the dream, he and that woman sat together in the Misty Forest. The woman pressed him down to the ground. Her slender jade fingers descended from his forehead, tracing slowly down along his cheek, his throat, his Adam's apple, until they finally came to rest on the sash at his waist. Her fingers hooked it—and a vast expanse of skin like cool jade and morning dew was revealed.

Heavy rain beat against the begonia blossoms. The flower hearts soaked in pooling water. The trees of the Misty Forest and the deep blue sky above both swayed and shimmered. He was drunk inside the dream, unknowing of what hour or day it was.

chapters.title: Twenty one
chapters.content:
Until a certain moment, Shen Shizou let out a muffled grunt and abruptly sat up from the bed. Before his eyes was a sweep of dark blue gauze curtains. When he woke, he instinctively glanced down at his lap, and immediately froze, unable to move.
He stood there for a long while, then shut his eyes as if unable to bear it any longer.
Fortunately, there was no one else in the small courtyard. This fleeting, unseemly spring dream was witnessed by no one. As if trying to cover something up, he hurriedly changed his soiled clothes.
When he pulled off his upper garment, his sturdy back was revealed.
He was not thin or frail. His frame was upright, his shoulders broad and his waist narrow, his body draped in a layer of even, strong muscle. And on his tawny skin, there was unmistakably a red butterfly birthmark, its wings spread as if about to take flight.
He remained lost in that dream and couldn't pull himself free. He was distracted even while changing, and naturally did not know that someone from Gongzi Garden had been following the trail, gradually closing in on the outside of his courtyard.
The person outside was separated from him by only a single wall. He and another world he had never imagined were also separated by only a single wall.
——
After leaving, Bai Qingning traveled for over an hour before returning to Qilin Street.
Qilin Street was clean and tidy, with people coming and going. When she and Qiuyue returned to the Qin family residence, it was already afternoon.
Sending the mute slave to the outer city estate had taken up quite a bit of time, but with the Bai family as her banner, she had no fear of being discovered. When Bai Qingning returned to the Qin family estate with Qiuyue, she had only just entered Lotus Courtyard and hadn't yet had time to sit down, drink a cup of tea, or ask Chunri about what had happened in the residence, when someone barged into Lotus Courtyard from outside.
Leading the way was an old matron from the Old Madam's courtyard, dressed in a dark brown brocade cloud-pattern robe. As she walked, her thin lips pressed downward in a mean line, deepening two long nasolabial folds at the corners of her mouth. Upon seeing Bai Qingning, she gave a proper bow, then lifted her chin, her tone imperious: "Young Madam, the Old Madam requests that you bring your maid Qiuyue to the front hall."
Bai Qingning raised her eyes to survey this old matron. Something seemed to come to her, and her originally cool features suddenly softened. Those eyes even curved with a trace of a smile. She set down the small fan in her hand and asked as if remembering something: "Could you be—Liu Matron, who serves at the Old Madam's side?"
Liu Matron gave a respectful nod, but clearly had no intention of making small talk with Bai Qingning. She kept her face stiff and repeated herself once more: "The Old Madam requests that you bring your maid Qiuyue to the front hall."
Qiuyue was named twice in succession and stood there dazed. Her hands, clasped in front of her belly, shifted uneasily. She looked toward Bai Qingning for help.
She was nothing but a small maid. Why would the Old Madam specifically call for her?
Qiuyue mentally reviewed every misdeed she had committed in the past fifteen years, then in horror thought—could it be that she and Madam's outing to buy a companion had been discovered?
Help! Madam stole the General's money to go keep a wild man, and the Old Madam has found out!
"Alright." Yet the Bai Qingning sitting ahead seemed not to have noticed any of this at all. Meeting Qiuyue's terrified gaze, she set down the teacup in her hand, rose to her feet, and even unhurriedly shook out her sleeves, saying: "Lead the way."
Qiuyue sucked in a sharp breath.
We're done for! My Madam still hasn't figured it out!
They're both exposed!
——
During the quarter-hour walk from Lotus Courtyard to the Old Madam's front hall, Qiuyue walked in tremendous agony.
Her mind was full of visions of herself and Madam kneeling on the ground together, weeping and confessing their wrongs, after which the Old Madam would use Madam's failure to uphold wifely virtue as grounds to have them both dragged out and beaten to death.
No!
If they were going to die, then let only her die!
She would carry everything for Madam!
She would say she had fallen head over heels for that companion at first sight, and that Madam had only gone to redeem him because of her endless pleading!
Madam, let Qiuyue bear this burden for you!
Qiuyue can do it!
During that walk, Qiuyue went from initial anxiety and unease, to steadfast resolve in the middle, to a final calm readiness for death—playing out three full scenes entirely in her head, even mentally rehearsing the lines she would sob out as she threw herself forward.
By the time they arrived at the Old Madam's front hall, even the way Qiuyue lifted her feet carried the air of someone going nobly to their death.
The Old Madam's front hall occupied an enormous area. You first passed through an outer room before entering the inner room. The inner room floor was laid with glazed tiles, so clean they could mirror your reflection. The chairs were made of agarwood, giving off a deep, aged fragrance. Two rows of old matrons stood on either side. The Old Madam wore a crimson gold-inlaid crane skirt, her expression solemn as she sat in the chair. Upon seeing people arrive, she cast a cold, measured glance upward.
Bai Qingning swept her eyes around the room, and behind the Old Madam in the hall spotted a wooden folding screen. Behind it there appeared to be a silhouette—someone in a pale gold-pink skirt. Most likely Zhao Hongzhu.
Bai Qingning turned everything over in her mind, and understood at once what sort of affair this was.
The Old Madam was here to avenge Zhao Hongzhu.
This thought had barely flashed through her mind before Bai Qingning heard Liu Matron say ahead: "Old Madam, the people have been brought. Caught in the act."
When the words "caught in the act" came out, Qiuyue's scalp prickled. She instinctively looked around, half-expecting someone to bring that companion of hers forward.
Instead, Liu Matron turned a cold face toward her, and scolded harshly: "Brazen servant! You dare steal from your masters—why haven't you knelt down?"
Qiuyue stood there in a daze.
This—this was a plot she hadn't imagined at all!

chapters.title: Twenty two
chapters.content:
"This servant—this servant doesn't know." Qiuyue's heart seized, and she dropped to her knees with a thud: "This servant has never stolen anything from the masters!"

"Still daring to be stubborn!" Liu Matron raised her hand sharply, looking as though she was about to slap Qiuyue across the face.

"Liu Matron." At this moment, Bai Qingning, who had been standing to the side without having said a word, finally spoke: "This maid of mine is the senior maid who serves at my side. She follows me every day. How could she steal anything? And what exactly is she supposed to have stolen?"

Seeing Bai Qingning speak up, Liu Matron immediately added with a smile that didn't reach her eyes: "A maid came to report today that she saw Qiuyue coming out of Warm Fragrance Pavilion with Miss Zhao's gold hairpin. That gold hairpin is a family heirloom of the Old Madam Zhao, priceless in value. From the Young Madam's tone, it sounds like you don't believe your maid would steal. But if she truly did steal—what would Madam intend to do?"

"If she truly stole it, I will accept all punishment. But if she didn't steal it?" Bai Qingning's words were addressed to Liu Matron, but her gaze went straight to the Old Madam seated in the master chair at the front of the hall, because she understood better than anyone that today's scheme was well known to the Old Madam.

Seeing Bai Qingning's manner so calm and composed, even faintly pointed, the Old Madam's wrinkles tightened slightly, her brows drawing together.

She had simply never liked the cold edge about Bai Qingning. The girl wore the same neither submissive nor arrogant expression toward everyone, showing not the slightest compliance even before her own mother-in-law—so unlike how endearing Hongzhu was.

Today Zhao Hongzhu had come to find her and said that last night's affair with Qin Shanyue had been consummated. The great stone weighing on the Old Madam's heart had finally been lifted. It was just that Zhao Hongzhu had said with some hesitation that Bai Qingning had flown into a terrible rage last night, and had beaten her personal maid Lancao to death. Zhao Hongzhu was suffering greatly now.

Naturally the Old Madam had to stand up for Zhao Hongzhu, and give Bai Qingning a proper lesson. To think she would dare execute a maid with the rod inside the Qin residence—how utterly outrageous!

Thinking of the loyal, devoted Lancao who was now dead, the Old Madam's expression turned even colder.

"Since this has already been brought before the Old Madam, let both the witnesses and evidence be presented. Right and wrong can be judged by the evidence. But I will say plainly first—if this maid of mine truly did steal Miss Zhao's gold hairpin, whether she lives or dies, I will hand her over to Miss Zhao to decide. But if my maid did not steal this hairpin—if she was deliberately framed and wrongly accused—then this debt, who should I go to collect it from?"

Bai Qingning's gaze first went to the folding screen. Zhao Hongzhu behind it didn't speak, clearly determined to let others take the lead. Then her gaze swept over the Old Madam seated in the main seat.

The Old Madam sat with perfect composure. Today she was playing the role of impartial judge, and she could not show favoritism. She even spoke a few gracious words: "Qingning, don't be angry. The household staff are just trying to guard against theft from within. It was not specifically aimed at your maid. If there's been a wrongful accusation, it's simply a misunderstanding."

Bai Qingning curved the corners of her lips: "In that case, please bring forward both witnesses and evidence, so everyone may judge together."

"The witness is right here." Liu Matron pointed out a maid, who immediately knelt to the ground and recounted the events of that day.

"This servant woke early this morning and saw Sister Qiuyue coming out of Warm Fragrance Pavilion with Miss Zhao's gold hairpin in her hand. This servant thought it seemed wrong, and so reported it to Liu Matron."

"The stolen goods should be hidden in the servant's own room. As long as someone looks, they'll find it." After the maid on the ground finished speaking, Liu Matron turned and pointed at the flustered Qiuyue: "Since Madam doesn't believe she stole the hairpin, why don't we go directly to Lotus Courtyard, search her room, and catch the thief with the stolen goods. What do you say?"

"Of course." Bai Qingning turned around and smiled at Liu Matron for a moment: "Lead the way, Liu Matron."

For catching a thief with stolen goods, there was naturally no need for the Old Madam to follow. Zhao Hongzhu shouldn't be going either—she should maintain an air of having nothing to do with the whole affair, sitting above it all on her high platform, so that no unseemly matter could dirty her feet regardless of what happened.

But Zhao Hongzhu had suffered a great blow at Bai Qingning's hands yesterday. Lancao's dying screams and tears had been circling in her head ever since. She had been holding her breath, waiting for the chance to deal Bai Qingning a devastating blow. Now seeing Bai Qingning about to walk into her own doom, she felt immensely gratified—she absolutely had to watch in person.

Lancao was dead. She wanted Qiuyue dead too. She wanted Qiuyue beaten to death by the rod, dying alive and in plain sight in Lotus Courtyard, dying right before Bai Qingning's eyes. She wanted every time Bai Qingning saw the tiles of Lotus Courtyard, she would remember the image of Qiuyue's blood spreading through the cracks between the stones.

So Zhao Hongzhu personally walked out from behind the wooden screen and asked the Old Madam's permission to go along.

chapters.title: Twenty three
chapters.content:
The Old Madam had always indulged and pampered her. Upon hearing the request, she simply waved her hand and told her to go. Worried Zhao Hongzhu might suffer some grievance, she also dispatched her own personal maid to follow along, so the maid could report back easily.

So Zhao Hongzhu brought two maids and followed behind Bai Qingning and Liu Matron.

Bai Qingning noticed Zhao Hongzhu, but after yesterday, Zhao Hongzhu had come to hate her to the bone—she couldn't even bring herself to maintain even surface-level courtesy, and simply trailed at a distance behind her, staring at Bai Qingning's back with venomous eyes.

Lancao had yet to be buried. She wanted to wait until Bai Qingning's personal maid was dead before burying Lancao.

Today the Old Madam would stand up for her. When Qin Shanyue returned, he would also banish Bai Qingning to the estate. After today, Bai Qingning would have no foothold left in the Qin family. She no longer feared Bai Qingning.

Zhao Hongzhu didn't approach to provoke her. Bai Qingning didn't challenge her either, and walked at the very front. Liu Matron followed behind with several matrons trailing after Bai Qingning, keeping close watch on her the whole time, afraid Bai Qingning might pass word to someone to go check Qiuyue's room first.

But she didn't.

Bai Qingning walked straight-backed at the front, her pace composed, neither hurried nor slow. Even the hairpin ornaments in her hair swayed only slightly as she moved. It was the maid Qiuyue behind her who was pale as paper, growing more and more uneasy with every step.

Qiuyue kept feeling that today's commotion was somewhat wrong, carrying with it a sense of coming at her with great force. She clearly hadn't stolen from anyone, yet now found herself inexplicably filled with guilt and fear. The sweat in her palms had made them slick and slippery. Her eyes kept darting to Madam ahead.

But Madam hadn't looked back once.

When they returned to Lotus Courtyard, the matrons called out all the servants and maids in the courtyard, had them stand in two rows outside, and every face wore an expression of panic.

Just last night Madam had beaten two maids to death. The sight of blood all over the courtyard had left all the servants trembling in fear, unable to sleep through the night. Several maids had been startled awake. How could there be trouble again today?

It was frightening just to look at.

Once they reached Lotus Courtyard, Liu Matron didn't wait for anyone to instruct her. She directly led three stout matrons straight into Qiuyue's side room and began tearing through it.

Lotus Courtyard was large, and the rooms for the maids were many. Qiuyue was a senior maid who had been part of the dowry from her family. When Bai Qingning had first arrived as a bride, she had personally chosen for Qiuyue the best, most spacious single-occupancy room, which she had all to herself.

This singular favor meant that Qiuyue, even with no head for scheming, had never been bullied in Lotus Courtyard.

Qiuyue watched helplessly as those matrons rushed in and tore through her room. Every chest and cabinet was opened. Qiuyue's private savings, the jewelry Bai Qingning had gifted her, the story books Qiuyue had secretly bought—all of it was scattered across the floor. The sound of cabinets being thrown down rang out clearly through the wooden door.

The fear in Qiuyue's heart swelled to a level she could no longer bear. She couldn't help but edge close to Bai Qingning and lower her voice: "Madam, what are we going to do?"

Bai Qingning only turned her face slightly and gave Qiuyue a gentle smile, saying in a soft voice: "What are you panicking for? No one can wrongly accuse you of something you haven't done. This world follows the principle of cause and effect. If you don't believe it, look up at heaven—it spares no one."

Qiuyue clenched her fists tight and thought: that's right! No one can wrongly accuse her of something she hasn't done!

The sounds of rummaging continued to come from inside Qiuyue's room, but gradually grew quieter. After all, there were limits to how large the room could be. Yet the people inside stubbornly refused to come out, convinced the gold hairpin had to be here, had to be here—so they kept on searching, looking as if they intended to dig up the very earth to find it.

"Did you find it?" Bai Qingning lifted her skirts and walked to the doorway, peering inside.

It was afternoon at that moment. The cool, austere autumn light fell in through the window, casting the shadow of the window lattice over the four people inside and across the floor. Liu Matron's face was flushed blue-red from suppressed emotion, with a trace of panic still showing. She was gritting her teeth and berating the other three matrons to keep searching. The floor was littered with things that had been knocked about, looking chaotic at first glance.

But no matter how they searched, they could not find the gold hairpin that should have been in Qiuyue's room.

Sweat had broken out hotly on Liu Matron's forehead, yet her back ran cold wave after wave. Standing in that room, her mind was in complete disorder.

How could they not find it?

How could they possibly not find it?

The thing was clearly supposed to be here!

What would happen if they couldn't find it? The Old Madam would probably blame her for incompetence.

No wonder Bai Qingning had looked so unafraid in the front hall earlier, daring to argue her case so resoundingly, and so easily letting them into the courtyard.

She had seen through their plan all along!

Liu Matron gritted her teeth, knowing today had likely been wasted effort.

Fortunately she hadn't painted herself into a corner with her words—she still had room to maneuver.

When she heard Bai Qingning asking from the doorway, Liu Matron managed to lift her head and squeeze out a smile: "Madam, this old servant has searched your quarters. Your maid is indeed innocent. Her room is completely clean—nothing unseemly at all. This old woman was foolish enough to believe false reports, and has caused Madam trouble. Please rest assured, Madam—today's matter is entirely this old woman's fault. This old woman will ask the Old Madam to punish her personally, and will pay three months of wages to Miss Qiuyue as compensation for the wrong done to her."

"We're all human. It's easy to be taken in and make mistakes. I don't blame you." Bai Qingning stood at the doorway, glanced at the foolish maid Qiuyue who had let out a sigh of relief, then smiled and swept her eyes over Zhao Hongzhu standing at the back.

Zhao Hongzhu had come to watch Bai Qingning's downfall. But watching up to this point, she suddenly realized Bai Qingning had been prepared all along.

Zhao Hongzhu was momentarily stunned with fright. When she had made that move, she had done it with exceptional cleanliness and care. And yet Bai Qingning had even known about this!

No wonder she had ended up so thoroughly calculated by Bai Qingning that day!

Zhao Hongzhu momentarily lost her nerve. The defeat was already set. She didn't want to stay and watch Liu Matron apologize and humiliate herself. Just at this moment, Zhao Hongzhu saw Bai Qingning turn around and smile at her for a moment.

Zhao Hongzhu's chest suddenly tightened. Before her eyes floated the image of Lancao's face in her dying moments—mouth wide open, blood seeping from every orifice.

A bad premonition suddenly surged up into Zhao Hongzhu's heart.

chapters.title: Twenty four
chapters.content:
"But Miss Zhao's gold hairpin is so precious—its whereabouts should certainly be found. Since it wasn't found in my Lotus Courtyard, let's search through all the rooms of the maids and matrons in Warm Fragrance Pavilion as well."

After saying this to Zhao Hongzhu, Bai Qingning turned back to look at Liu Matron. Her pale blue water sleeves drifted lightly in the air, giving Liu Matron no chance to refuse. Eyes curved in a smile, she said: "There's a certain place where we might just find it."

Liu Matron's movement stiffened for a moment, and the flattering smile that had been on her face just before turned suddenly startled.

A place where they might find it? What place?

But Bai Qingning didn't answer. She simply led everyone on foot to Warm Fragrance Pavilion.

——

Liu Matron had originally been one of the Old Madam's trusted confidantes, naturally living alongside her. It was only after Zhao Hongzhu's return that she was assigned by the Old Madam to Zhao Hongzhu's service. And Liu Matron had been part of the Old Madam's bridal dowry—a woman who had weathered decades of storms at the Old Madam's side. This alone showed how deep the Old Madam's fondness for Zhao Hongzhu ran.

Zhao Hongzhu had never dared to neglect Liu Matron. After Liu Matron moved into Warm Fragrance Pavilion, she was given a private room, with two maids attending her every day. Though she was just a matron, she lived quite comfortably.

When Bai Qingning said she wanted to search Warm Fragrance Pavilion, Liu Matron's heart immediately clenched. Her instincts told her this was bad. But the words to refuse couldn't come out when they reached her lips.

Bai Qingning had blocked every avenue for her. She had come under the pretense of "finding the hairpin." Since the hairpin hadn't been found, Bai Qingning's suggestion to look in Warm Fragrance Pavilion was perfectly reasonable—Bai Qingning held all the justification.

And Bai Qingning had given her no chance to refuse. She directly led Lotus Courtyard's matrons, nearly forcing Liu Matron into Warm Fragrance Pavilion, and dispatched Lotus Courtyard's matrons to search the side rooms directly.

Zhao Hongzhu could no longer stay uninvolved. She stepped forward to stop them, saying: "Warm Fragrance Pavilion is my territory. Let me search it myself."

"Lotus Courtyard is also my territory, and it was still searched by others." Bai Qingning's tone was gentle but unyielding: "However Lotus Courtyard was searched, Warm Fragrance Pavilion must be searched the same way."

Bai Qingning and Zhao Hongzhu went head to head, eyes locked on each other with a cold, piercing chill. The servants standing behind them didn't dare make a sound.

Word had already spread today among Warm Fragrance Pavilion's maids about last night's affair between Zhao Hongzhu and the General. These two women—one was their current mistress of the household, the other a woman who had already consummated a marital relationship with the General. Neither could be offended.

The other servants didn't dare speak or step forward. But the servants of Lotus Courtyard obeyed only their own mistress. With a wave of Bai Qingning's hand, several matrons and maids walked straight toward Liu Matron's side room.

Seeing that things were going badly, Zhao Hongzhu gave the maid behind her a look. The maid quietly retreated two steps, then turned and ran toward the Old Madam's courtyard to find the Old Madam.

At this very moment, a matron from Lotus Courtyard came running out of Liu Matron's room, holding a begonia-shaped gold hairpin high in the air, and called out loudly: "Found it, Madam! This was turned up from inside Liu Matron's cabinet!"

The afternoon autumn sunlight fell on the gold hairpin, and that well-polished ornament gave off a bright, gleaming luster. When the hairpin was held up, Liu Matron's legs gave way and she collapsed straight to the ground: "This—how can this be? This old servant is wrongly accused!"

No matter how carefully she had calculated—the gold hairpin that should have appeared in Bai Qingning's courtyard had appeared in her own room!

No wonder Bai Qingning had insisted on making this trip to Warm Fragrance Pavilion. It turned out Bai Qingning had taken the hairpin and placed it in her room!

chapters.title: Twenty five
chapters.content:
In her fear and shock, Liu Matron instinctively began protesting: "It wasn't this old servant! This old servant didn't!"

"If it wasn't you, then how did this thing come to be found inside your room?" Bai Qingning took the gold hairpin, turned around, and directly signaled Lotus Courtyard's matrons to bind Liu Matron.

"Stealing a master's jewelry—by the Qin family's household rules, that calls for ten lashes and expulsion from the Qin household. But you not only stole the hairpin, you also tried to frame my maid Qiuyue for the theft. Your crime warrants death. Someone come—ten lashes, plus fifty rod strikes, administered right here in Warm Fragrance Pavilion!"

When Bai Qingning finished speaking, Liu Matron began struggling on the spot. Ten lashes plus fifty rod strikes—even a grown man couldn't survive that. These old bones of hers would certainly die!

She was too terrified to care about anything else—if she didn't act, she would die! So she struggled and cried out with red-rimmed eyes: "Even though this old servant is a servant, I was still the Old Madam's dowry maid—I am the Old Madam's person! Who gave Madam the right to punish me? If anything happens to this old servant, the Old Madam will certainly have a falling out with Madam!"

When Liu Matron shouted this, even the matrons holding her down couldn't help but relax their grip slightly. And at this very moment, Bai Qingning snatched the whip from a servant's hand and dealt Liu Matron a fierce, heavy lash!

Though Bai Qingning was a woman with no great strength, this whip was specially made. The base was iron, with a layer of tiny spiked barbs cast over it. Even a light brush against skin could scrape off a layer of flesh. With Bai Qingning wielding it like this with full force, the blow landed on Liu Matron's back with a resounding crack!

The brocade garment couldn't withstand such a strike and split apart. Blood and flesh flew up together. The people holding Liu Matron were so startled they froze in place, unable to move. As for Liu Matron, at the first lash the pain practically exploded through her scalp, draining all strength from her body. She slumped to the ground, unable to get up.

That kind of pain—like having all the skin flayed from your body. Liu Matron had never experienced anything like it in all her years of living. That single lash had nearly beaten her to death. Her chest heaved with rough, wheezing breaths. She couldn't even cry out on the first strike. It was only when the second lash came down that Liu Matron finally let out a wail.

That wail no longer sounded human—it was like a dog at the village gate being kicked to death and skinned alive, howling and howling, burrowing straight into people's ears. The sound was so harrowing that even those holding Liu Matron flinched with pale faces, startled into stumbling backward. Liu Matron rolled to the ground as a result, wanting to crawl up but unable to in the face of overwhelming pain.

Yet Bai Qingning didn't soften her hand at all. She raised the whip high and brought it down again and again on Liu Matron writhing on the ground. On that face, clear and cold as the moon, there was nothing but an expression of stern resolve.

Beaten by a whip, or burned by fire?

In her past life, two lives—hers and the mute slave's. In this life, she would first collect a bit of interest from this Liu Matron!

For that moment, the entire Warm Fragrance Pavilion echoed with nothing but Liu Matron's cries of pain.

After ten lashes, Bai Qingning flung aside the whip in her hand. The whip, stained with blood and flesh, landed on the ground with a thud.

"Bind her." Bai Qingning looked toward the nearby matrons: "Fifty rod strikes. Begin."

The two matrons nearby were so frightened they had gone numb. Cold sweat had soaked through their palms. But not daring to defy Bai Qingning, they tremblingly lifted Liu Matron and placed her over the long bench specially used for administering rod punishment.

By this point Liu Matron was already half-dead from the whipping. Knowing Bai Qingning wouldn't spare her, it roused something fierce in her instead. She lay draped over the bench and began screaming curses: "Vicious woman! You vicious woman! I was the Old Madam's dowry maid. I was the one who nursed the Great General! How dare you beat me to death—how dare you beat me!"

Bai Qingning gestured to the nearby servants. The two servants then lifted the wooden rods in their hands—iron-capped at one end, capable of shattering bones and sinew with each blow.

"Strike!" Bai Qingning furrowed her brows slightly. The two servants began, and with each blow that landed on Liu Matron, Liu Matron screamed "vicious woman" at the top of her lungs.

After only a few strikes, Liu Matron could no longer call out.

And at this moment, a commotion arose outside Warm Fragrance Pavilion. A large group of people clustered around a figure making their way over. At the very front walked someone who was sixty years of age, slightly hunched at the shoulders, expression anxious but unable to move quickly—the Old Madam.

"Stop!" When the Old Madam saw Liu Matron being held down on the bench and beaten, she was immediately overcome with fury, pointing at Bai Qingning and shouting: "Bai Qingning! How could you lay hands on Liu Matron?"

"Old Madam." Bai Qingning unhurriedly produced the gold hairpin and recounted the entire matter of the hairpin being found in Liu Matron's room. Then she softened her voice and said gently: "Catching a thief with the stolen goods in hand—that Liu Matron is the thief within the household. Your daughter-in-law knows that Liu Matron was your dowry maid and that you and Liu Matron share a deep bond. But this kind of person who bites the hand that feeds her and steals should be beaten to death. She is your maid—who knows how many valuables she has stolen from guests without you knowing. Your daughter-in-law is also beating her for the sake of our Qin family's reputation. The Qin family is an old and prominent household—how can we tolerate people like this?"

chapters.title: Twenty six
chapters.content:
With every word Bai Qingning spoke, the Old Madam's complexion darkened one shade more. Her originally pallid face had flushed to a deep crimson. Zhao Hongzhu hastily took the Old Madam's arm to support her, but didn't dare say a single word.

She too hadn't expected that Bai Qingning would be this ruthless—actually daring to back the Old Madam into a corner like this. Others might not see through it all, but Bai Qingning naturally knew all the underlying reasons. Today, Bai Qingning had surely offended the Old Madam severely!

Sure enough, the Old Madam couldn't catch her breath. She stood where she was, staring at Bai Qingning with a furious expression, her trembling hand lifting as if she wanted to berate Bai Qingning—but was so enraged she couldn't get a single word out.

Yet Bai Qingning only smiled with increasing gentleness. She lowered her eyes to look at Liu Matron on the bench, and even gave a rather mournful sigh.

"Alas, Liu Matron—look at what you've done, causing the Old Madam such distress. How has the Old Madam treated you all these years? How could you steal things? Isn't that a betrayal of the Old Madam's kind intentions and reputation?"

As she spoke, Bai Qingning picked the whip up from the ground and before the Old Madam's very eyes, dealt Liu Matron a fierce, hard lash. Then she turned back to smile at the Old Madam: "Old Madam, please don't be angry. Leave everything to your daughter-in-law. Your daughter-in-law will certainly discipline her properly and make her crimes known to all—letting everyone know that the Qin family does not tolerate this kind of unruly behavior."

Bai Qingning's words, contrasted with the sorry state of Liu Matron draped across the bench, were like a sharp sword plunging hard into the Old Madam's heart. The Old Madam felt a cloying sweetness surge up at her throat, and with a "heave," she vomited a mouthful of blood!

That blood was deep crimson verging on black. When it fell to the ground, the entire Qin household went still for a moment. Only when a maid cried out did Bai Qingning speak: "Escort the Old Madam back. Send for the physician."

——

No sooner had the Old Madam been carried back into her room than Qin Shanyue received word from a servant.

When Qin Shanyue had left that morning, he had been afraid that after his departure the two women in the Qin household would stir up trouble. He had deliberately called over a servant and given him a few instructions. He hadn't expected there would actually be an incident.

He hurried back on horseback, and as soon as he stepped through the door, he learned that the Old Madam had been so angered she fell ill—and it was Bai Qingning who had angered her. Even Liu Matron had been beaten to death.

Reportedly, while the Old Madam was being treated with needles and bloodletting, Bai Qingning had held Liu Matron down—no maid or matron had been able to stop her. Anyone who tried, Bai Qingning beat.

The physician was fighting to save the Old Madam's life inside while Bai Qingning was beating Liu Matron to death outside. In the meantime, when the Old Madam came around, her first question was about Liu Matron's condition. When told Bai Qingning had beaten her to death, the Old Madam vomited another mouthful of blood and fainted again.

When Qin Shanyue arrived at Warm Fragrance Pavilion, he was greeted by a scene of bloody carnage. Several servants were collecting a body with trembling hands, while Bai Qingning stood beneath a tree, quietly watching Liu Matron's corpse.

At the sight of this, Qin Shanyue was instantly consumed with fury. He strode to Bai Qingning, grabbed her arm in a fierce grip, and roared: "Bai Qingning, what exactly are you trying to do? You knew perfectly well that Liu Matron was my wet nurse, the woman who nursed me, my mother's personal maid. Why did you still beat her to death?"

"Your concubine doesn't understand the General's words." Bai Qingning's arm was wrenched painfully, but she showed no signs of yielding. She raised her head to look at Qin Shanyue and said in a composed voice: "Your concubine only acted according to household rules. She stole things—she naturally deserved to die. Otherwise, how would rules be maintained in the future?"

In her past life, her Qiuyue had died exactly like this. Now it was Liu Matron's turn. She would die the same way, and no one could save her.

"Bai Qingning! Just because I'm going to marry Zhao Hongzhu, you're going to make everyone's life miserable!" The veins at Qin Shanyue's temples throbbed with fury. He stared at Bai Qingning's gentle, dignified face, and for the first time found it ugly as a venomous scorpion. He shoved Bai Qingning hard by the shoulder and bellowed: "You're just taking revenge! Revenge on me, revenge on my mother, revenge on the Qin family! I never knew you were such a vicious woman! I truly regret being blind enough to have married you!"

Bai Qingning was shoved back several steps and nearly fell. Fortunately Qiuyue rushed forward to catch her. Only after she and Qiuyue had steadied themselves did she hear Qin Shanyue say through gritted teeth: "Bai Qingning, you will regret this."

Bai Qingning raised her eyes to look at him, and saw Qin Shanyue's expression contorted with fury as he enunciated each word: "I am repudiating you, Bai Qingning. I am repudiating you. From today onward, don't ever think—you can set so much as a single step inside my Qin household again!"

When Qin Shanyue's words fell, the entire Warm Fragrance Pavilion courtyard went quiet.

Countless pairs of eyes turned to look at Bai Qingning. Some maids gathered together in small clusters, whispering among themselves, unable to hold back.

"The General is going to repudiate Madam. Madam is surely going to beg for forgiveness."

"What kind of life can a repudiated woman have? When all is said and done, it's still Madam's fault. If Madam weren't so ruthless, how could she be repudiated?"

"Madam is in for real trouble this time. She beat Liu Matron to death with the rod—the Bai family will probably have to come in person to beg for clemency."

"Madam is sure to be punished! She might even be confined and made to kneel in the ancestral hall to reflect on her wrongs."

The broken fragments of discussion buzzed around like flies. Qin Shanyue found it grating on his nerves. His cold phoenix eyes bore down on Bai Qingning from above.

Today, he would not show Bai Qingning even a shred of mercy!

chapters.title: Twenty seven
chapters.content:
At that moment, Bai Qingli was being helped to her feet by Qiuyue. Her eyes were cold as a winter frost, and her voice was just as icy: "If that is how it is, then please, General, move to the Lotus Courtyard and draft the letter of dismissal."

The moment those words fell from Bai Qingli's lips, every maidservant in the courtyard froze.

The mistress actually refused to yield to the General!

Good heavens — had the mistress gone mad?

Qin Shanyue was equally enraged by Bai Qingli's unrepentant manner. Without even bothering to return to the Lotus Courtyard, he ripped a strip of white brocade from his own robe, drew the heavy blade he always carried at his side, and slashed open his palm. Blood welled up freely. With blood-soaked fingers, he wrote the two characters for "letter of dismissal" directly onto the fabric, then flung the brocade out toward Bai Qingli.

The brocade was light. Though Qin Shanyue had thrown it with great force, it lost its momentum the moment it caught air, drifting lazily toward Bai Qingli in slow, floating arcs.

The sky had already darkened by then, dusk settling over everything. Only a last sliver of fading sunlight touched the Warm Fragrance Pavilion. The world had blurred into silhouettes — Qin Shanyue and Bai Qingli standing face to face, each reflected only in the other's gaze. The wind stirred the hems of their robes, and it stirred that scrap of brocade drifting between them in midair.

The brocade looked like a piece of blood-stained snow. Like the snow that had fallen on the Qin family's old estate that day.

Bai Qingli reached out and caught it, her slender fingertips closing around the cloth. Her eyes swept over the two characters written there — "letter of dismissal" — and then she looked away without a trace of longing.

She had not the slightest desire to exchange even one more word with Qin Shanyue. She gave Qiuyue a slight lift of her chin and turned to leave.

Qiuyue had been so frightened she'd gone numb, and could only blindly support Bai Qingli as they walked. The maidservants of Warm Fragrance Pavilion didn't know whether to follow or not, and so they hesitated, exchanging uncertain glances.

By then, Bai Qingli had already brushed past Qin Shanyue.

Delicate gauze silk grazed heavy black brocade. The woman's hair, loosened from being shoved earlier, billowed up in the wind like spilled ink. Blood dripped steadily from the man's clenched fist — drip, drip — striking the ground, pooling into small dark hollows.

The autumn wind was wild. The white brocade inscribed with a dismissal written in blood tangled with the falling leaves scattered across the courtyard, weaving together into a desolate and merciless tableau. It was a grand, silent farewell — only Qin Shanyue had not yet understood it as such.

Qin Shanyue stood rooted to the spot, eyes burning red, jaw clenched tight. From the moment Bai Qingli took the letter and brushed past him, to the moment she walked out of Warm Fragrance Pavilion — he did not move.

He stood there like a statue, on the verge of being frozen to death in the cold autumn air.

He had never imagined that he and Bai Qingli could come to this.

When Bai Qingli had first married into the Qin household, she had smiled brightly and called him "General," and sometimes, coyly, "husband." He was a man of few words and a cold temperament, but Bai Qingli had always liked to be near him. She was never loud or intrusive — she might settle somewhere quiet with a book, or bring two cups of tea, and simply sit.

While he practiced swordsmanship and studied battle maps, she would sit silently beside him, reading or painting, and when the hour came she would go personally to the small kitchen to cook for him. After years of military life, he could eat almost anything — in dire straits, he'd gnawed bark. But Bai Qingli was different. Bai Qingli was the sort of woman who carved even a cucumber garnish into the shape of flowers and grass. When he was with her, he had felt a peace and refinement unlike anything he'd known before.

It had seemed, everywhere, like birdsong and blossoms, like unhurried elegance.

So how had they come to this? What had he done wrong?

Nothing. He had done nothing wrong.

Qin Shanyue lowered his gaze to his own hand and told himself: he had done nothing wrong. It was Bai Qingli who was ruthless and calculating, who had from the very beginning sealed off every possible path between them. She was to blame for where they now stood.

Their parting had been this savage and this final — even the letter of dismissal was stained with blood. They couldn't even manage the civil pleasantry of "may we each go our separate ways in peace."

It was all because Bai Qingli was too hard-hearted.

He would not waste another thought grieving over a woman like her.

"General." Just as Qin Shanyue stood staring blankly at his own hand, a maidservant approached. "The Old Madam has woken. She is asking for you."

Qin Shanyue came back to himself and gave a low sound of assent. The maidservant offered to bind his wound — it wouldn't do to appear before the Old Madam covered in blood — but Qin Shanyue waved her off. He simply drew a roll of gauze from inside his robe and wrapped the cut himself with practiced ease. He'd carried such things throughout his years commanding troops; it had become habit, even here in the capital. He'd thought he wouldn't need it. He had been wrong.

The Old Madam's courtyard was called Rosy Sunset Garden, and it was filled throughout with flowering plants. By autumn they were all bare, the beauty stripped away to something sparse and melancholy. As Qin Shanyue entered, a pang of sorrow struck him without warning. He walked quickly through the courtyard, past maidservants with frightened, anxious faces, through the outer room, and pushed aside the beaded curtain to enter the inner chamber.

Inside the bedchamber, the Old Madam lay in bed. Zhao Hongzhu attended her personally at her side. An experienced old physician had finished his needlework, put away his medicine case, and slowly shook his head. He rose, met Qin Shanyue's eyes, and withdrew to the outer room without a word.

The Old Madam was awake. The woman who had once sat upright and sharp-eyed at the head of a room now looked as though all the life had been drained from her, frail and withered against the pillows. When she saw Qin Shanyue enter, she lifted one age-spotted hand with a trembling effort. Qin Shanyue rushed to her side and knelt on the low stool by the bed, cradling her arm in his uninjured hand, his voice breaking: "Mother."

The Old Madam's eyes reddened at once.

Qin Shanyue was her youngest son. The Qin family had given so many loyal sons to the nation — and now only this one remained. And he had gone and brought home a brazen, low-born creature. A daughter-in-law, a girl of the younger generation, had dared humiliate her before everyone. She, who bore an imperially bestowed title!

"Shanyue." The Old Madam could barely speak: "Dismiss her. Dismiss her!"

Qin Shanyue closed his eyes and bowed his head: "Yes, Mother."

The Old Madam seemed to exhale some long-held bitterness, her eyelids drooping: "It is my fault as your mother, for choosing such a person for you. Shanyue, it is all my fault. If only I had listened to you from the start and refused — and waited for Hongzhu — none of this would have happened."

Zhao Hongzhu was standing right there at the head of the bed. She pressed her lips together and quickly called out in a soft voice, "Old Madam."

When the Old Madam's gaze fell on Zhao Hongzhu beside her, those clouded old eyes suddenly brightened. Her withered lips quivered as she pointed at Zhao Hongzhu and said, "Now that you have dismissed her, do not delay. Hongzhu is the one who should be your true wife."

Zhao Hongzhu lowered her eyes and stared at the tips of her own shoes, saying nothing.

Qin Shanyue held the Old Madam's hand. Under her urging, he nodded solemnly: "I will take Hongzhu as my lawful wife."

The Old Madam finally set her heart at rest and fell into an exhausted sleep.

Qin Shanyue and Zhao Hongzhu quietly withdrew from the inner room to discuss the Old Madam's condition.

"The Old Madam's constitution has always been fragile — she does not have much time left regardless," the physician said. "And today's fit of rage and grief has hastened the decline of her vital energy considerably. When I examined her last, I estimated she might last until the New Year in winter. But looking at her now — I would say perhaps half a month at most."

Half a month.

The grief in Qin Shanyue's chest deepened.

Whether from sorrow or something else, his head had begun to throb with wave after wave of dull pain, nearly enough to make him lose his footing. He swayed slightly, and Zhao Hongzhu hurried to his side to steady him, pressing her shoulder into his to support his tall frame.

Qin Shanyue was in no state to manage what came next. After Zhao Hongzhu arranged for the maidservants to see the physician out, she had Qin Shanyue settled in the nearby Warm Fragrance Pavilion — and with no small degree of calculation, installed him in her own bedchamber — before turning back to handle the rest of the affairs.

With the Old Madam gravely ill, Bai Qingli dismissed, and Qin Shanyue incapacitated with a splitting headache, Zhao Hongzhu was, for the moment, the only one present who could act as mistress of the household and direct the maidservants, manservants, and nurses. She managed everything in orderly succession, even instructing the small kitchen to prepare a porridge for Qin Shanyue. Only when all was settled did she ask, "What of the Lotus Courtyard? Has someone been sent to notify the Bai family?"

Being dismissed was too shameful a thing. Bai Qingli would never accept it willingly — she was most likely scheming at this very moment to find a way to stay in the Qin household, perhaps sending for family elders to apply pressure or plead on her behalf. Zhao Hongzhu maintained an outward air of calm, but inside she had already drawn herself taut. She had to press her advantage and drive Bai Qingli out in one decisive blow. Qin Shanyue still held a place in his heart for Bai Qingli — and no small one at that. If anything went wrong and Bai Qingli managed to stay, Zhao Hongzhu's position would become precarious.

Between her and Bai Qingli, it was now a matter of survival — there was no longer room for both.

She had not yet thought of a good approach. Her two previous failures — first the death of Lancao, then the death of Stewardess Liu, and then indirectly enraging her greatest support to the brink of death — meant she could not survive a third failure.

Because she so feared failure, a thread of cowardice had begun to creep into Zhao Hongzhu's heart — a feeling she had never known before. It was the first time in her life she had been so afraid of another person.

"The Lotus Courtyard sent no word to the Bai family. Only some laborers from the tenant farm below were summoned—"

Before the maidservant could finish, Zhao Hongzhu's expression turned to one of disbelief.

"She just... left?" The handkerchief in Zhao Hongzhu's grip was nearly wrung to shreds. She pressed further: "Did she do nothing else?"

Zhao Hongzhu now regarded Bai Qingli as she would a natural disaster. She was convinced that every move Bai Qingli made carried hidden meaning, that every word was a trap being laid for her. She couldn't help turning it over and over in her mind.

"She truly did nothing else," the maidservant replied. "The Second Miss Bai had people clearing out the storeroom. She went through the accounts directly with the steward and said that once the tally was complete, she would leave."

Zhao Hongzhu bit her lip and said nothing.

As things stood, both the Old Madam and Qin Shanyue were prepared to welcome her into the household — and as the primary wife, no less. The position had come abruptly, and it would certainly attract curiosity and gossip. But what great household didn't have secrets best kept hidden? Stories of noble daughters with untimely pregnancies, of official wives secretly doing away with concubines' children — such things were everywhere. She only had to endure the scrutiny, and she would become the first wife of the Qin family. In three or five years, once she had borne a legitimate heir and received an imperial title, who would dare bring any of this up again?

As long as Qin Shanyue stood behind her, she would never fall.

The more pressing matter now was marrying into the Qin household. Everything else could wait. Once she had secured her footing, why should she fear a cast-off divorcée?

Thoughts flashed through her mind in quick succession. Zhao Hongzhu made her decision swiftly. She shook her head, abandoned any further intention of making trouble for Bai Qingli, and said instead, "Tell the steward to cooperate with her. Have her dowry cleared out as soon as possible. Do not make things difficult for her."

Without Bai Qingli needing to say a word, no one in the entire Qin household would have dared give her trouble. Word had already spread throughout the estate that morning of Bai Qingli horsewhipping Stewardess Liu to death. No one was willing to provoke her. And Bai Qingli's dowry had been kept in its own dedicated storeroom from the moment it arrived at the Qin estate, so the inventory went unusually quickly — it was finished in just over an hour.

The tenant farmers from the estate below had been summoned by Bai Qingli's instruction and were waiting obediently to one side, hands at their sides. These were tenants from properties under Bai Qingli's name; Qiuyue accompanied them every year during the rent collection, and they were all mild-mannered, keeping their eyes lowered. When Qiuyue told them to lift the trunks and go, the whole group heaved them up immediately and filed out through the rear gate of the Qin estate.

Before leaving, Bai Qingli had also settled the affairs of the Lotus Courtyard.

Every maidservant who wished to leave had her bond of indenture released. Bai Qingli then drew a sum of money from the Qin household's accounts to give each of them a start — a safeguard, in case Zhao Hongzhu, once she took charge of the Qin household, decided to mistreat them for having once served Bai Qingli.

Among all the maidservants, only Chun Ri clenched her jaw and refused to go. She wanted to follow Bai Qingli.

Chun Ri had no parents; she had been sold into the Qin household when she was young. She had later helped Bai Qingli turn the tables on Stewardess Liu in a little scheme, and had since served closely at Bai Qingli's side — she was a favored senior maidservant. If she remained in the Qin household, she would surely face retribution sooner or later.

But to take a sum of money and simply leave — that didn't sit right with Chun Ri either. She was a clever girl. Before, when Bai Qingli had kept a low profile and quietly played the role of the Bai family's first wife, Chun Ri hadn't noticed anything unusual. But in the past few days, since the General had returned with Zhao Hongzhu, Bai Qingli's every action had opened Chun Ri's eyes wide.

She had never seen a woman who, after being betrayed by her husband, did not weep or rage, but instead remained sharp and formidable — a woman who could disregard her husband's affections and her mother-in-law's very life, and in just a few short days, turn the entire Qin household on its head.

While events were still unfolding, Chun Ri had not been able to guess what the mistress intended. But now that it was all over, she looked back and traced through what her mistress had done step by step — and could not help but exhale in quiet astonishment. The mistress had truly calculated everything precisely. From beginning to end, she had spared no one.

She couldn't quite say what it was she admired about her mistress — only that she loved that quality in her, the unyielding refusal to let anyone walk over her head. And the mistress was fiercely loyal to her own people. Qiuyue was such a dim-witted girl — always eating and sleeping, spending her days reading story books or imagining herself as the heroine in one, muttering to herself endlessly about goodness knows what — yet the mistress had always taken her side. When Qiuyue was called to account before the Old Madam's front courtyard, the mistress had declared without hesitation that she would bear the responsibility herself, not yielding an inch. She had never seen a mistress so good to her maidservants, nor one so entirely unlike any other. And so she wanted to follow her.

"Follow me?" Bai Qingli glanced briefly at Chun Ri.

Chun Ri and Qiuyue were the same age — a clear-featured girl with a delicate oval face, quiet in appearance but meticulous in her work, sharp-witted too. She was promising material. Having served this long, she had carried out every task without fault and with considerable merit.

"Following me is no guarantee of a comfortable life." Bai Qingli and Qiuyue had already reached the rear gate of the Qin estate by then. She waved her hand casually and said, "If you want to come, come. If the day comes when you no longer wish to stay, you're free to go. I won't keep you by force."

Chun Ri hoisted her small bundle and trotted cheerfully after them.

Her instincts had never led her astray. Even if life with Bai Qingli wasn't the finest of all fine lives, no one would ever dare bully her again.

The group of them left the Qin estate. Bai Qingli boarded the estate carriage directly, and it carried them to Fog Forest Courtyard.

Chun Ri and Qiuyue sat side by side on the driver's bench outside the carriage curtain. While Bai Qingli rested inside, Chun Ri asked Qiuyue in low tones where the mistress was going, and when she planned to return to the Bai family.

"The mistress hasn't said." Qiuyue had a packet of candied fruit in her hands and was stuffing her cheeks full on both sides. She held the packet out to Chun Ri as she spoke, arms outstretched: "We're headed to Fog Forest Courtyard. When we get there, keep your composure — don't go looking startled at everything."

Chun Ri's eyes went slightly wide. She hadn't expected to someday receive a warning about keeping her composure from Qiuyue. For a moment she wasn't sure what kind of place Fog Forest Courtyard could be. Surely it must house some important figure the mistress was going to seek out. But on its face, the dismissal wasn't legally sound — the mistress had committed none of the seven grounds for dismissal, and she was the daughter of an official, properly wed. She was not so easily put aside.

Still, anyone with the standing to overshadow the Qin family must be someone of particular rank — royalty, perhaps?

The more Chun Ri thought about it, the more it made sense. That explained it, she thought. When the mistress had been locked in conflict with the Qin family, she had seemed ready to drag them all down with her. Yet this time she had left so cleanly, so decisively — it didn't add up otherwise.

So the mistress had come to find someone to stand up for her!

Suppressing her excitement, Chun Ri accepted the candied fruit, popped a piece into her mouth, and followed Qiuyue's example in sitting quietly to wait.

The carriage moved slowly because of the large group carrying trunks behind it, barely faster than walking. After about an hour on the road, they finally arrived at Fog Forest Courtyard.

At the gate, Qiuyue directed the group to bring everything in through the rear courtyard and pile it in the back room. Bai Qingli entered through the front.

Chun Ri had meant to accompany Bai Qingli inside, but Qiuyue grabbed her arm. When Chun Ri turned back, Qiuyue's expression was entirely serious: "Don't cause trouble. Do you know who's in there?"

Chun Ri had never seen Qiuyue look so tense. She felt a flutter of excitement herself, and her voice rose slightly: "Who is it?"

Perhaps the First Princess, the one who had retired from court?

A knowing look spread across Qiuyue's face as she said, "You know why our mistress, the moment she left the Qin estate and came straight here—" and a faint expression of gritted teeth crossed her features.

Chun Ri grew even more excited: "Why — why is that?"

To pay respect to the First Princess, of course — and to lodge a formal complaint against the Qin family!

Qiuyue slapped her own knee: "Because there's a male fox-spirit in there! He has enchanted our mistress — bewitched her soul completely!"

Chun Ri: "Ah — ah?"

* * *

When Bai Qingli stepped into Fog Forest Courtyard, Shen Shizhuo had just walked out to the doorway of the study.

Shen Shizhuo was unaccustomed to being waited upon, so he lived alone in the courtyard — peaceful and unhurried. When noise broke out at the gate, he guessed it might be Bai Qingli arriving.

He had been sitting at the writing desk, but the moment he heard it, he found he could no longer concentrate on the book in his hands. He kept glancing toward the window.

Dusk had fallen, and through the window he could see only the dense green expanse of the fog forest. The sun had sunk to the far edge of the sky, leaving behind only a single thread of red among the trees — vermilion bleeding into deep emerald, one stroke of red amid ten thousand shades of green.

It was a view Shen Shizhuo had seen countless times. Yet today he could not seem to have his fill of it — his gaze kept drifting outward, and the book in his hands felt heavier by the moment, as though he could no longer hold it.

Until a flash of indigo appeared among the fog trees.

He had never watched anyone's hemline with such attention — the arc it traced as it swung, the way it caught on blades of grass as it fell, every thread of silk seeming to carry its own lingering grace.

He rose without thinking and walked out to the doorway.

Bai Qingli was coming toward him.

After an exhausting day of upheaval, Bai Qingli was so tired she couldn't lift a single finger: "Anu, in a moment."

She had now been dismissed by Qin Shanyue, but her revenge against the Qin family was not yet finished. Tomorrow she still needed to deliver a devastating blow to both the Qin and Bai families. After that, she would have to prepare to disappear — change her name, find a different place to live. She had planned to leave Fog Forest Courtyard to Shen Shizhuo and say a proper farewell to him.

In her past life, Anu had died with her in the snow mountains. In this life, she hoped Anu would find a good path.

With that, she turned and went back to her room.

Shen Shizhuo, left standing there, stiffened the moment he heard the words "her room." He glanced up at the sky.

Finally... was it time?

* * *

Once Bai Qingli had gone into her room, Shen Shizhuo stood alone in the courtyard, his thin lips pressed tightly together.

Chun Ri and Qiuyue finished settling the dowry, and when they looked up, they saw Shen Shizhuo standing near the study. The last of the day's light hovered above his head like a fading halo; a refined young gentleman stood beneath the tree. Chun Ri took one look at him and understood immediately what Qiuyue had meant by "male fox-spirit."

The man had strikingly fine features, a tall and upright bearing — like a crane amid the misty mountains. A chill emanated from him that seemed to say: do not approach. And yet, given his position—

"So this is... the kept man our mistress maintains?" Chun Ri asked in a daze. "She fell out with the General for his sake — dismissed and all, she didn't even go back to her family, only came here?"

Shen Shizhuo, standing beneath the tree, went rigid all over.

She had left her husband — for him?

So this woman harbored such devotion for him.

No wonder that, upon returning this time, she had called him to her room straightaway. She hadn't touched him before because she was still married. But now that the marriage was dissolved — she was already eager.

"Yes," Qiuyue sighed at length. "What can you do? The mistress is set on him."

Shen Shizhuo couldn't bear to hear another word. He snapped his head to one side and moved to leave — but was stopped by Qiuyue.

"Hey — you!" Qiuyue didn't know how to address him. The word "young master" rose to her lips and then felt wrong, so she skipped any form of address altogether and called out, "Where did the mistress go? What did she say to you just now?"

Shen Shizhuo had a pale complexion; in the moonlight, he seemed to gleam like jade. At Qiuyue's question, Chun Ri watched Shen Shizhuo's face flush crimson — the color crept upward from his neck, spreading slowly across his cheeks. His thin lips pressed tighter, his breathing grew heavier, as though he wanted to say something but couldn't bring himself to begin.

The crane of the mountain pines had suddenly become a puppy that would roll over at the slightest touch.

"Speak!" When he didn't answer, Qiuyue immediately assumed her best borrowed-authority posture, planted both hands on her hips, and announced: "You are the kept man our mistress purchased! Do you not understand what that means? You don't even rank as a concubine — at most you're a bed-warmer! I am the mistress's head maidservant. When I ask you a question, you answer!"

The red on Shen Shizhuo's face had nearly reached his ears. Under the combined scrutiny of Qiuyue and Chun Ri, he forced out one agonized sentence.

"The mistress has returned to her room," he said. "Tonight — she asks me to come."

Qiuyue and Chun Ri both stood frozen.

They were both unmarried young women. Hearing those words, they felt heat rush straight to their heads. Chun Ri spun around to leave — but Qiuyue grabbed her and held her in place.

"Being called to wait on the mistress is an honor for you," Qiuyue declared, face scarlet, maintaining her most dignified expression. "Go and bathe and change your clothes first. I'll instruct you in the proper conduct for attending one's mistress in the night. Our mistress paid a great deal for you — you had better serve her well."

Shen Shizhuo's back stiffened even further. He stood in complete silence.

Chun Ri, standing nearby, had been struck by a bolt from heaven, and was thoroughly dazed — words had left her entirely. She could only bow her head and stare at the tips of her own shoes, thinking: the mistress and the mistress's maidservants were, truly... unlike anyone she had ever known.

* * *

Meanwhile, on a different branch of the story: while Qiuyue and Chun Ri went to heat water and prepare Shen Shizhuo for the evening ahead, the Warm Fragrance Pavilion in the Qin estate was utterly silent.

Zhao Hongzhu fetched a bowl of porridge from the small kitchen, dismissed all the maidservants, and walked back to Warm Fragrance Pavilion alone.

When she returned to the bedchamber, Qin Shanyue had already sunk into sleep.

Qin Shanyue was having a very strange dream.

In the dream, he had become Bai Qingli.

Through her eyes, he stood at the gate of the manor to welcome his own return — watched himself walk through the doors of the Qin estate with Zhao Hongzhu on his arm, and felt, firsthand, the ache and bitterness of what Bai Qingli had endured that day. When he declared to her resolutely that there was nothing of a romantic nature between himself and Zhao Hongzhu, he could feel Bai Qingli's joy, her relief.

And then, at that very moment, he heard someone whispering gently at his ear — a soft, repeated calling of "Zijin" — drawing him back, pulling him out of the dream. Qin Shanyue slowly opened his eyes and found himself staring up at the canopy above the bed.

His soul still seemed to drift somewhere inside that dream. He was disoriented; the feelings had been too real, as though everything had truly happened once before. His body had been forced awake, and Zhao Hongzhu was already seated at the edge of his bed.

"You're awake? Do you feel better?" Zhao Hongzhu helped him sit up, asking gently beside him.

Qin Shanyue gradually gathered himself. He pressed two fingers to his brow, answered "awake" in a hoarse voice, and then couldn't help turning the dream over in his mind again.

Inexplicable — and yet it clung to him, circling his thoughts and refusing to leave.

"Have some porridge." Zhao Hongzhu handed him the bowl and began to massage his temples, her voice slowing further, taking on a note of careful hesitation: "The Old Madam woke a little while ago and told me she wants the wedding banquet arranged soon. But I — I don't know who to turn to for help. You know my situation — no parents, no brother, and even Lancao is gone. I don't know how to—"

Qin Shanyue's attention snapped fully back at once. A swell of tenderness rose in his chest, and he reached out to take her hand in his own.

The night had deepened by then. In the candlelight, Qin Shanyue looked at Zhao Hongzhu's luminous face. She had a sweet, round face — usually full of spirit and energy, but when she lowered her eyes, there was something distinctly soft and girlish about her.

A peach blossom face, glowing with a different kind of beauty.

"Don't worry. I'll ask some of the elder relatives of my comrades from the army to preside over your wedding." Qin Shanyue held her hand, lifted the porridge bowl, and felt a warmth spreading through him.

Zhao Hongzhu leaned her head against his shoulder and gave a soft sound of assent.

With Qin Shanyue handling the matter of finding a suitable elder to oversee things, she moved on to her own plans — the wedding banquet was being arranged in haste: whom to invite, whom to leave out, what style her bridal dress should be.

Qin Shanyue held Zhao Hongzhu and listened to her speak of these small details — and then, without warning, an image surfaced in his mind: Bai Qingli's wedding day, a thousand red candles burning, lanterns blazing the length of the street.

The moment it appeared, Qin Shanyue flinched as though he'd been burned, and immediately wrenched Bai Qingli from his thoughts, tightening his grip on his right hand.

The wound on that hand still ached. And he had not forgotten what Bai Qingli had done. Whatever had brought them to this point was the result of Bai Qingli's own cruelty and ruthlessness.

He would not let himself feel even the faintest warmth toward Bai Qingli again. The only person at his side now, the only one who needed his care, was Zhao Hongzhu.

"Whatever you wish." Qin Shanyue swallowed the porridge in one long gulp, his voice rough: "I'll give you the best."

The bedchamber glowed with warmth. Everything was moving in the direction Zhao Hongzhu had planned.

* * *

The people below lived out their separate dreams through the night, while the moon above remained unchanged from time immemorial.

A wash of pale light drifted with the evening breeze across the land, but it could not illuminate Fog Forest Courtyard. The trees there pressed in from every side, dark and dense, making the night feel especially black. So Chun Ri took up a small hammer and went about driving a row of lanterns into the trees, one by one, lighting a path.

Lanterns swaying in the wind, a thousand points of candlelight.

When she arrived at the door of Shen Shizhuo's room, she paused — but then she thought of Qiuyue, and steeled herself to go in. If Qiuyue could manage it, what reason had she to refuse?

She pushed open the door and walked in — only to find Qiuyue already in the middle of lecturing Shen Shizhuo.

"The Three Obediences and Four Virtues — I needn't teach you those, surely? However things are done in those establishments, you'll do them the same way here. If you attend the mistress well, you'll have a fine life ahead of you. If you fail her, the mistress will have you flogged! Our mistress is fierce when she punishes — just two days ago she flogged two maidservants to death."

Chun Ri crossed the threshold and looked over. From where she stood, she could see Shen Shizhuo standing in silence with his lips pressed tight, while Qiuyue lorded it over him beside him.
