As though in a dream from a distant lifetime, he followed the direction of the servant boy's gaze and looked across.

His eyesight was far better than the servant boy's. Through the gaps in the frame and the press of shoulders, past the thin veil of white gauze, he saw Bai Qingli's face clearly.

He had not seen Bai Qingli for some time.

His last memory of her was that absolute finality — her hand closing around the letter of divorce, her head never once turning back, her whole person like a cold stone carving, so rigid and sharp-edged that touching it might draw blood. It had sealed every warm thing that had ever passed between them under ice at the bottom of his heart; he could not bear to look.

And yet what he saw now was a Bai Qingli entirely unlike that one.

She was wearing an ordinary pale blue dress, with a simple white cape over it — the blue and white together giving her an air of quiet peace. She was looking toward the wooden frame in the distance, lit by warm candlelight, and she was smiling at someone Qin Shanyue couldn't quite see. Her eyes carried a tenderness he had not witnessed in a long time.

Qin Shanyue followed her gaze and saw Shen Shizhuo.

Shen Shizhuo was entirely unlike Qin Shanyue in type. Qin Shanyue carried the sharp, decisive air of a man who had lived among battles, and even without his armor he radiated a cold authority that kept people at a distance — street vendors never dared approach him. Shen Shizhuo was more like a tree growing in the mist of a thin mountain, his features wreathed in fine threads of cool quiet: upright and clean, with an unbending proud bearing and frost-cold eyes.

Shen Shizhuo had just answered a riddle correctly and was asking the stall owner how many correct answers he needed to redeem the hairpin. After getting his answer, he instinctively glanced back at Bai Qingli.

Bai Qingli was there watching him. Their eyes met — and between them, in that moment, there was something any onlooker could see plainly. Qin Shanyue could not put a name to what it was. It was only that he felt something like a heart being seized like a rag, soaked wet, wrung and twisted as hard as it could go — and what was wrung out was not water, but blood, drop by drop. Aching and suffocating.

He stared fixedly in that direction, the way a soldier stares at the enemy who has slaughtered his people.

For a long moment Qin Shanyue said nothing, only kept staring at those two figures.

He had not expected to encounter Bai Qingli here. He had even less expected to find her with a man.

A single man and woman, alone together at the lantern festival — by any reading, there was something intimate about it.

He ran through every eligible man in the capital in his mind, comparing each one to this stranger — but he could not place him. Every notable man in the city he recognized. This one he had never seen before.

When had Bai Qingli come to know this man?

She had barely been gone from the Qin household ten days — barely taken the letter of divorce and stepped out the door — and already she was out with someone else.

All at once it felt as though a hidden passage had been cleared in his mind. One perfectly logical explanation suddenly snapped all the previous strangeness into place.

Why, when he had returned from campaign, Bai Qingli had shown him no warmth.

Why, even though he had brought Zhao Hongzhu home and promised again and again that he had no such feelings for her, Bai Qingli had continued treating him with cold indifference — and had even moved against Zhao Hongzhu first.

Why Bai Qingli had been so utterly pitiless — taking the letter of divorce and walking out the door on the spot, not even going back to the Bai household, vanishing to somewhere no one could find.

Because Bai Qingli had already taken up with someone else!

His bringing Zhao Hongzhu home had simply given Bai Qingli the excuse she needed to leave!

Going through it item by item, the outrageous theory of "Bai Qingli transferring her affections to another" began to seem more and more fitting the longer he thought about it. There was simply no other explanation that could account for how completely and suddenly Bai Qingli had changed.

Fury blazed through Qin Shanyue's mind in an instant. He was experiencing the sensation of betrayal for the first time, and it was enough to shatter his reason and his pride. Without pausing for a single additional second of thought, he lunged toward Bai Qingli like a black panther springing from the mountain.

He came too fast — his old habit of moving through the darker corners of a crowd — and Bai Qingli never sensed him coming. Within seconds, the warm orange light before her was suddenly blocked, a cold wind swept against her, and when she looked up, she was looking directly into Qin Shanyue's face.

Qin Shanyue had grown thinner. The line of his jaw was sharper. His phoenix eyes pressed downward with an angular intensity, and his already strong features had taken on an additional edge of danger. His tall frame filled her entire field of vision.

She had put him entirely out of her mind in the past few days. Seeing that face now, she felt the strange double sensation of someone both familiar and foreign — a feeling of being across a great chasm of time.

The next second, Qin Shanyue raised his hand and knocked the wide-brimmed hat from Bai Qingli's head.

The hat was fastened to her chin with a tie. The force of Qin Shanyue's pull snapped the thin cord clean through. The jerk of it yanked Bai Qingli sideways, and she stumbled once before steadying herself, pressing one hand to the stinging skin of her jaw, looking at Qin Shanyue in bewilderment.

Qin Shanyue had been raised with the education of a gentleman. Though he had taken a military path rather than a scholarly one and wore a certain roughness that came with it, he still carried the cultivated propriety of a capital man of letters and the pride of a son of a great house deep in his bones. He had never raised a hand to a woman. Even on the day of the divorce, when he wrote the letter of divorce, the blade he held had only cut his own palm.

This was the first time Qin Shanyue had ever vented his displeasure in such a manner.

Bai Qingli looked up at him in genuine confusion.

They had not seen each other for a long time. Things between them had come close to a point of never meeting again in this life. In all likelihood they would never reach a place of peace with each other — even if they met, the natural response was to pretend not to know one another and give each other a wide berth. What was Qin Shanyue running up to yank off her hat for?

"Was it because of him?"

While Bai Qingli stood there bewildered, Qin Shanyue suddenly spoke. His voice was hoarse, his tone full of bitter fury — but she couldn't understand what he was saying.

"What?" Bai Qingli asked. "Who?"

"Him!" Qin Shanyue could no longer restrain himself. The low snarl that escaped him drew the attention of everyone nearby.

Just then, Shen Shizhuo had solved the final riddle and received the white lotus hairpin from the stall owner. The pin was fashioned from white jade and emerald, its upper half a large white lotus flower, the shaft below shading into translucent jade-green — a rare and unusual piece. The petals' edges were gilded. In the cold October wind it was ice-cold to the touch, but the jade itself was smooth and mellow beneath the fingers — clearly fine quality stone.

She would love it.

Shen Shizhuo had already pictured how Bai Qingli would look wearing it — but when he turned around, he saw a tall man standing directly in front of Bai Qingli. Bai Qingli had taken half a step back. The man had reached out and grabbed her wrist.

Shen Shizhuo's expression went cold. He walked forward quickly.

He had barely taken a few steps to reach the two of them — the word "let go" was barely to his throat, not yet out — when the man suddenly turned his head. A pair of phoenix eyes, shot through with blood, stared at him without blinking.

Shen Shizhuo felt a sharp inward alert. Every bit of his inner energy coursed through him at once.

The street was loud and chaotic, and he had deliberately softened his footsteps — yet this man had heard him coming from three steps away. Unusually sharp hearing. And looking at the flex of muscle along the man's arm, the calluses on his palm, the way the blade hung at his hip — this man was no ordinary fighter.

His thoughts had barely reached that conclusion when he heard the man grind out through his teeth: "Bai Qingli — you divorced me because of him, didn't you!"

A cold wind blew by. All the anger and alertness in Shen Shizhuo's chest froze in an instant. He stood rigid, staring at Qin Shanyue's face, and a string of thoughts rushed through his head.

In the pleasure house, he had never fit in — but no one had gone out of their way to make his life difficult either. He had occasionally overheard the other kept men swapping stories, including accounts of being caught in compromising situations.

Some women patrons could not come to the pleasure house directly, so they would invite a kept man they had taken a liking to out of the city — some for a day's outing, others to stay at a rented residence for a stretch. Once out of the capital, beyond authority's reach, a man and woman alone together would sometimes get up to things they shouldn't — and husbands who found out generally couldn't tolerate it. Having people come and catch the pair in the act was common practice, and most of the men in the house had dealt with it at some point.

[In moments like this, you absolutely cannot be aggressive. The moment you take an aggressive stance, you become the focus of attention — and that actually reduces the animosity between the patron and the husband. What's the point of the two of you quarreling? You need to make the patron and the husband quarrel with each other. That's how you get more of the patron's affection and protection. So you need to appear weak.]

[You must understand: what a patron likes about you is that you are compliant and easy to manage. You need to seem gentle enough, even aggrieved, so the patron will feel fond of you and sorry for you.]

[As for the husband — don't give him a second thought. The more furious he gets, the more composed you stay. By comparison, naturally you come out better.]

[We kept men all have to learn this. Otherwise, how do we hold a patron's heart?]

Those thoughts flashed through Shen Shizhuo's mind in an instant — and in the same instant he stole a glance at Bai Qingli beside him.

Bai Qingli's delicate brows had drawn together. At hearing those words, her jade-like face flushed slightly, and her voice dropped to something cold and sharp: "Qin Shanyue, what are you talking nonsense about? Let go! You and I have already divorced. Who I spend my time with is none of your business—"

Qin Shanyue did not let her finish. The moment the words were out of her mouth, he wheeled around and threw a punch at Shen Shizhuo.

His intention had been to knock the man out and drag him back to the estate for a thorough interrogation — to dig out every piece of this man's history with Bai Qingli. But the moment he moved, the man flowed sideways with an airy, liquid grace and simply wasn't there.

Qin Shanyue's expression sharpened.

A trained martial artist. But that footwork — it hadn't been learned in fewer than ten years.

Qin Shanyue went for the blade at his waist — but the moment his fingers touched the hilt, before he could draw it, the man suddenly stumbled backward three steps and went down, face twisted in apparent pain.

Qin Shanyue's hand stopped.

What was this? He hadn't touched him!

"Qin Shanyue!" At the same moment, a voice — sharp enough to border on indecorous — rang out from in front of him. Bai Qingli had thrown herself between the two of them, face bright with fury: "What gives you the right to hurt him?"

Qin Shanyue looked sharply down at Shen Shizhuo.

Shen Shizhuo lay on the ground with a convincing expression of agony — but he was looking at Bai Qingli's back, and at the corner of his mouth, the faintest smile had curved.

Useful.

The kept men of the pleasure house did, in fact, know a thing or two.

* * *

chapters.title: Chapter 34
chapters.content:
By the time Qin Shanyue understood what had just happened, he was furious in every possible direction.

He had never been subjected to such provocation.

He had been bested — by that kind of underhanded trick — and played for a fool.

A grown man, pulling that kind of coy, false-suffering maneuver! He could not argue his way out of it, had momentarily lost all reason, and with a sharp metallic ring he drew his blade.

Schemes and tricks be damned — he would cut the man down where he stood!

The heavy blade cleared its scabbard, and its bright, sharp face carved a fierce arc through the air. Bai Qingli had barely reacted before Shen Shizhuo's hand shot out from behind her, seized her arm, and yanked her backward. Her sleeve whipped out in a half-circle, grazing the edge of the blade.

When Bai Qingli collected herself, she saw that the sleeve had been sliced clean open. The wind caught the loose fabric and blew it back, exposing her arm to near the elbow — a length of pale, jade-smooth forearm, with a thin red line running along one side.

A hairline wound from the blade's force.

Shen Shizhuo had already put himself between her and Qin Shanyue. While she was retreating, the two men had exchanged several strikes — she could only hear the dull thud of bodies colliding. Her heart pounded in her chest and her palms were damp.

Once she had pulled back far enough to see clearly, she found the crowd had scattered on all sides. Shen Shizhuo and Qin Shanyue were locked in combat, sleeves and clothing flying in a blur. Shen Shizhuo used his knees and shins repeatedly to deflect the flat of the blade, but a body could not match steel, and he was being driven steadily backward. At the critical moment, a cold arrow came flying from behind Qin Shanyue — the angle was precise and nasty, and Qin Shanyue was forced back several steps. The arrow buried itself in the earth, cracking the smooth paving tiles and sending small fragments of brick spraying outward.

At the same moment, from the alley behind them, two horses came galloping out. Zhuifeng rode the first, bow in hand, using his arrows to hold Qin Shanyue at bay. Shen Shizhuo turned on his heel, gathered Bai Qingli with one arm around her back and the other under her, vaulted onto the second horse with perfect timing, seized the reins, and rode away from them down the long street with Bai Qingli in his arms.

Riding at full gallop was forbidden on public streets — only carriages were permitted to travel at speed — and with the lantern festival bringing crowds out in force, people scattered in panicked confusion at the sight of a horse bearing down on them. The street descended into chaos. Qin Shanyue dodged arrow after arrow as they came in rapid succession, and by the time he looked up, the horse's hooves had carried them from one end of the street to the other. The road on both sides was full of frightened people and scattered lanterns.

He could not catch up.

But there was nowhere Bai Qingli could hide from him. In this city, he had a hundred ways to find a person.

Meanwhile, the night patrol officers arrived quickly on the scene. They had assumed it was a gang brawl — that kind of thing was common at the lantern festival, with so many pickpockets and so many people. They usually arrested a few people around this time and sent them to the cells. But what the officers had not anticipated was that the person they found standing in the wreckage was General Qin Shanyue himself.

The second-rank General of Martial Valor! Trusted by the Son of Heaven! A family of undying loyalty!

The officers bowed hastily and asked with careful deference: "We pay our respects to the General. Might we ask, sir — the person who was fighting with you just now—"

According to the onlookers, it had been a fine young gentleman of some kind, the son of some noble house, who had dared to brawl with a great general in the middle of the street.

Qin Shanyue had not wanted this mentioned — but now that it had been: "No need to make a fuss of it. I will compensate everyone here for any losses."

The officers breathed a quiet sigh of relief. Best not to let it become a scene — they couldn't manage the children of officials anyway, and if it blew up it would have to be referred to the Court of Judicial Review. Men of their rank were better off staying out of it.

After the officers withdrew, Qin Shanyue summoned his servant boy — who had been watching the entire spectacle from the sidelines and was now trembling visibly — and told him to go and bring several soldiers.

"Find them." Qin Shanyue's voice had a cold that had never been in it before, carrying the low pressure of an approaching storm: "Arrest them. The man — dead or alive."

The servant boy flinched.

Dead or alive for the man — which meant the mistress was to be taken alive.

"Yes, sir." The servant boy hurried off.

Just then, Zhao Hongzhu appeared in the distance with her two maidservants. Qin Shanyue glanced at the servant boy, and the boy moved off to a respectful distance.

"Shanyue, what happened?" Zhao Hongzhu asked, her face full of surprise.

She had just been watching a street performer breathe fire nearby — very exciting — when she heard that a fight had broken out behind her. She came over and found Qin Shanyue standing there with the ferocious look of something that meant to destroy everything in its path, a blade still gleaming in his hand.

She had seen Qin Shanyue commanding troops on the battlefield before, and yes, he had always radiated a lethal intensity then — but this was the first time she had ever seen this particular look on him. It was as though he wanted to grind something to pieces.

The sound of Zhao Hongzhu's voice brought Qin Shanyue abruptly back to himself.

Bai Qingli had betrayed him — but Hongzhu had not. He still had Hongzhu.

The violent energy churning in his chest settled slightly. Out of some instinct rooted in his pride, he did not want to share this sordid business with Zhao Hongzhu — so he slowly sheathed the blade and said quietly: "Nothing. Just ran into a small thief."

Zhao Hongzhu was far too clever, and knew Qin Shanyue far too well. One gesture from him, and she knew something was off. He never concealed even official business from her — so why would he not tell her this? A premonitory unease rose in her chest. Her instinct told her this was important.

But she couldn't press him when he chose not to speak. She only quietly committed the face of the servant boy who had been at Qin Shanyue's side a moment ago — and then walked away — to memory.

Qin Shanyue might not tell her. But she could find out from that servant boy.

Those thoughts passed in an instant, and Zhao Hongzhu showed no sign of having noticed anything. She lifted her face with a bright smile: "Then let's go stroll over that way. I want to float a river lantern."

Qin Shanyue accompanied Zhao Hongzhu to the riverside and bought two river lanterns from a stall set up at a water pavilion. The vendor handed them paper and brush and asked them to write their wishes.

Zhao Hongzhu took the brush and wrote: [May the Zhao family's name be restored.] She folded it and placed it inside her chosen lantern, then looked over to find Qin Shanyue staring blankly at the slip of paper in his hand.

"Not done yet? Can't think of what to wish for?" she asked.

Qin Shanyue seemed to startle awake. He moved quickly, writing a few characters on the slip, folded it, and tucked it into his river lantern.

They walked together to the river's edge — a moat that ran the length of the entire capital from north to south. The surface was already dotted with floating lanterns, the tiny lights mingling with the threads of moonlight until the water shimmered and gleamed. They crouched at the edge; Zhao Hongzhu's vivid skirts spread across the pale green grass. She set her lantern on the water, then clasped her hands together and wished with quiet sincerity.

She believed heaven was just. She believed in the wheel of consequence. What belonged to the Zhao family — their innocence — would be returned to them, sooner or later.

While she made her wish, Qin Shanyue stared with a dark expression at the lantern in his hands. Only when Zhao Hongzhu lowered her hands did he quickly release his own lantern onto the water and rise to his feet.

Zhao Hongzhu sensed his distraction and lost any desire to continue wandering. She found a pretext about tired legs and returned with him to the Qin estate.

Once back, Qin Shanyue was gone before she could turn around. Zhao Hongzhu understood he had gone off to deal with the matter of the "small thief" — but she kept her expression neutral, as though she knew nothing, and after descending from the palanquin, walked with her two maidservants toward Burnt Book Court.

The moment they stepped inside the estate, both maidservants shrank their shoulders involuntarily.

The Qin estate was uncannily still. From the main gate all the way in, there was barely a maidservant to be seen. Only when they passed Rosy Sunset Garden could they hear the noise coming from inside.

These days, the atmosphere in the Qin estate was oppressive. The Old Madam had been in a state of madness since she learned that Qin Shanyue had petitioned the Emperor for a marriage decree — sleeping fitfully in the day and erupting at night, at first merely raging without striking, but lately completely disregarding who might be injured. Anyone who tried to stop her got a teapot or a hairpin hurled at them — whatever was at hand. A few days ago, a young maidservant who brought her congee was doused with it full in the face, and her previously pretty features were destroyed.

Yet this was the Old Madam, and the whole estate could only endure it. The longer they endured, the more suffocating the atmosphere became. It was as though a dark cloud had settled over the entire estate. The two young maidservants had arrived cheerfully enough with Zhao Hongzhu, but the moment they set foot inside the gates, their heads gradually began to droop. By the time they approached Rosy Sunset Garden, even their ears had flattened, and their arms stiffened.

They had only been in the Qin estate for a few days, but they had already learned something of the situation: the old woman in Rosy Sunset Garden and the young mistress they served were sworn enemies. The old woman had even taken the late General's blade and gone to the gates of Burnt Book Court intending to cut the young mistress down — only to be stopped by the soldiers on guard. Frightening enough, even from the outside.

When they had first been bought into the Qin estate, they had imagined they were stepping into a life of good fortune. Everyone knew how fine things were in a great house — even the maidservants were dressed as well as the daughters of modest families, with an education and good prospects; if a young mistress took a liking to you, you might even be matched to a good husband and rise in the world. Who could have known that what awaited them was this half-mad old woman, making their nights wretched with her howling? Every time they walked past Rosy Sunset Garden, every inch of their skin crawled.

But here was their young mistress, stopped at the very boundary of Rosy Sunset Garden's outer wall — pressing herself flat against it!

The wall was made of stacked bricks, and if you pressed yourself against it, you could hear through it.

Inside were two young maidservants, clearly just punished for something, crouching against the wall-base and weeping quietly, muttering through their sniffles.

"How is anyone supposed to survive this? The Old Madam has already slapped me four times today. Just because I look a little like that woman in Burnt Book Court, she takes it out on me every single day! She doesn't even treat us like people! Even a four-legged animal wouldn't be tormented like this! Keep going like this and I'm not going to survive it."

"I knew it would come to this — I should have walked out with the Mistress when she left! When the Mistress was here, did the Qin estate ever get like this? Everyone says the woman in Burnt Book Court comes from a good family, knows her manners, is a proper lady from a great house — but since she arrived, look at the state this place has fallen to! The Old Madam is being driven into the grave by her, and she spends every day pleasuring herself without a care. Proper lady? How does her character compare to our Mistress's? This is what a great lady looks like?"

The more the girl said, the more aggrieved she became. With the whole estate turned to ruin anyway, she stopped holding back — she let her resentment pour out through clenched teeth: "Everyone in Rosy Sunset Garden must have been blind before. Always flattering Zhao Hongzhu, singing her praises. Look at her now — how does she compare to the Mistress? When the Mistress was here, did she ever mistreat us servants?"

"That's right — the Mistress may have been born of a concubine-mother, but she was cultivated and gracious. When she was here, the Qin estate ran smoothly. She even gave us days off each month, and sent silver to any household with a wedding or a funeral. It was Zhao Hongzhu who spent every day stirring up trouble between the Mistress and the General! If not for her, how could the General have been so unfilial?"

Each sentence from the maidservants landed like a slap, cutting through the air to strike Zhao Hongzhu across the face. The two young maidservants following her were trembling harder with each word. And sure enough — at some point, Zhao Hongzhu could hear no more. She straightened abruptly, and at a swift, rigid pace, walked back to Burnt Book Court.

Under the moonlight, Zhao Hongzhu's full, finely drawn face was shadowed — but she forced it all back down.

She was not going to rush. She could not rush.

When she became Mistress of the Qin estate, these servants would answer to her. She only had to wait a little longer.

* * *

Back in Burnt Book Court, Zhao Hongzhu was so rattled by those two maidservants that she forgot entirely to find the servant boy and ask about Qin Shanyue's affairs. She went straight to her room, gritted her teeth, and counted the days.

Only a few days remained until the imperial-decree wedding. The bridal robes were already half-finished. The woman presiding over her marriage was the wife of the current Prime Minister — the greatest honor imaginable. She was about to leap to the very top in one step. Why should she trouble herself over a few lowly servants?

While Zhao Hongzhu was occupied with these thoughts, Qin Shanyue was still outside searching.

Tonight's events had been sudden, but they had occurred on a busy public street in full view of everyone — there were clues in every direction. It did not take long before the servant boy came to report: "General, we have located them. Near a small village on the outskirts of the capital."

At the time, Qin Shanyue was standing in the practice yard of the Qin estate, a silver spear in hand. When the servant boy came to report, he turned sharply, his arrogant, sharp-cut face full of cold killing intent.

"Call up the soldiers." The spear rang as Qin Shanyue rammed it back into the weapon rack, his expression vicious and dark: "Surround the courtyard. Take them alive."

* * *

By the time Qin Shanyue led his soldiers toward Fog Forest Courtyard, Bai Qingli was already tending to Shen Shizhuo's injuries.

Earlier, Shen Shizhuo had ridden them all the way back at full gallop. When they reached Fog Forest Courtyard, Shen Shizhuo had toppled from the horse, giving Bai Qingli such a fright that cold sweat broke out all over her. She had half-carried, half-dragged him with great effort back to the bedroom. When she pulled off Shen Shizhuo's outer robe, she found that his entire upper body was unmarked — not a patch of clean skin.

A vast spreading bruise of purple and dark blue covered his chest, the kind that came from someone striking with concentrated inner force. The sight made Bai Qingli go dizzy. She rushed to rummage through the boxes for safflower oil, poured some into her palm, and began applying it herself.

Shen Shizhuo's outer robe had been removed, leaving his upper half bare. He was not slight — his muscle tone was clearly defined and handsome — but he was fair-skinned, and that only made the marks on his chest look more ghastly. Bai Qingli pressed him firmly down onto his back, rubbed her palms together until they were warm, and laid both white, soft hands flat against his chest.

The moment her hands touched him, Shen Shizhuo's whole body gave an involuntary shudder. The truth was that his injuries were not severe — alarming to look at, but entirely superficial bruising. He had been performing a deliberate collapse, and hadn't expected to frighten Bai Qingli as badly as he had. She'd been circling around him anxiously, personally stripping off his clothes to treat him.

They had exchanged their vows, yes — but they had not so much as touched each other yet. Shen Shizhuo's body had been handled by a martial arts master teaching him, and by the wet nurse bathing him as a child — but never by a woman he loved. From the moment Bai Qingli picked up the medicine to the moment she rubbed her palms together, his head had been making a constant ringing noise. He had had the word "I'm fine, I can do it myself" ready to go — and then quietly swallowed it. He simply lay there, staring fixedly up at Bai Qingli.

Bai Qingli's face was tight with worry.

She rarely showed emotion this openly. The cool composure she normally wore had been discarded somewhere, and in its place her brows were tightly drawn, her eyes full of anguish, her lips pressed into a straight line. Shen Shizhuo shuddered — she seemed to be in more pain than he was. Her water-bright eyes looked directly at his face, one question following rapidly on another: "Am I pressing too hard? Does it hurt?"

Every organ in Shen Shizhuo's chest dissolved at her look. His heart hammered, and he said: "It hurts so much."

The moment those words left his mouth, Bai Qingli hadn't even reacted yet — but Shen Shizhuo's own face was blazing.

In the pleasure house, he had always looked down on those kept men who played helpless and performed for patrons — he had always thought that kind of behavior was too beneath dignity. But today he had genuinely tasted the reward for it.

He gave one small groan, and Bai Qingli grew more worried. He furrowed his brow, and she stared at him all the harder, as if she were the one in pain. His heart was divided: one half scorned himself from the bottom of his soul — every sage teaching he had ever read was scolding him right now — while the other half was drowning in Bai Qingli's soft words and tender attention, unable to surface.

While Bai Qingli pressed at his chest, his mind barely floated above the sweet water — most of it occupied by the question of how her hands could possibly be that soft. Only the very smallest fraction, in a moment when guilt surfaced, made him think: Bai Qingli had divorced that man in order to be with him — and he supposed he owed that man something of an apology.

As things stood, he had come up from the position of a kept man to something much better, while that man was now the discarded husband. He had taken a beating today, yes — but someone who had made their way by charm alone deserved as much. He would call it fair.

"Why did you bring this back with you?"

Shen Shizhuo's thoughts had barely gotten there when he saw Bai Qingli draw something from the folds of his robe: a white lotus hairpin.

Through all the riding and fighting and arrows, he had taken a considerable number of blows — but this hairpin had come through without a scratch. It lay in the cup of Bai Qingli's palm, and in the candlelight, it shimmered with a soft, pearlescent glow.

Shen Shizhuo had entirely forgotten about the hairpin. Through all the chasing and fighting, he had no idea how he had clutched it in his grip the whole way home. Bai Qingli's question caught him completely off guard, and without thinking he said: "I wanted to give it to you."

She would look beautiful wearing it.

Bai Qingli held the hairpin and went still for a moment.

She still had oil in her palm, warm and stinging from being rubbed together — which made the jade pin feel even cooler and more soothing in contrast. She had not expected Shen Shizhuo to say that. She was a woman who had lived and loved before; she was not naive about a man's intentions. Where Qiuyue might not have understood, she caught it the moment it reached her ears, and felt something in her chest tighten briefly.

She looked down at Shen Shizhuo.

His face was flushed red — even his neck was red — like an even wash of pink evening sky over ivory-smooth skin. The moment she looked at him, his gaze drifted away, unable to meet hers. It took considerable courage for him to look back at her for even an instant, and then his eyes moved away again at once. He had gone rigid all over, the tendons in his neck faintly visible.

"What's the matter?"

Shen Shizhuo's fingers had unconsciously crumpled the bedsheet: "You don't like the hairpin?"

He could not bear Bai Qingli looking at him like that — directly, openly, as though she wanted to open him up and read his heart, read his bones.

Bai Qingli pressed her lips together slightly.

The hairpin she liked — but his feelings she did not dare accept. After being betrayed by Qin Shanyue in her previous life, she had given up on romantic love entirely. In this life, she only wanted to live on her own terms. She had brought Shen Shizhuo back with her for no reason other than to repay the debt from her previous life — to let him live well in this one.

When she had brought him back, she had never thought of it in those terms. She had only thought of him as a lifelong companion — someone to look after each other and walk beside her all the way to the end. But if Shen Shizhuo had started to feel something for her, she wasn't quite sure what to do about it.

Her first instinct was to refuse, to put distance between them. But Shen Shizhuo was lying here covered in injuries, and she could not find it in herself to say anything harsh.

She turned it over and over, and finally set the hairpin on the pillow beside him. The words "I don't like these kinds of things — please don't send me anything else" were halfway up her throat — and then from outside the courtyard came a burst of noise, Qiuyue and Chun Ri rushing back in a panic.

"Mistress! Mistress!"

At the lantern festival, Qiuyue had not been that far away from Bai Qingli. From a distance, she and Chun Ri had both seen Shen Shizhuo and Qin Shanyue come to blows, and it had frightened the two maidservants badly — neither had dared show their heads. Once Bai Qingli and Shen Shizhuo had made their escape, they rushed to drive the carriage back. Their driving skills were questionable at best; a half-hour's journey had taken nearly a full hour. Both of them had barely landed when Qiuyue, with a wailing expression, came hurtling into the room without caring that Bai Qingli was tending to Shen Shizhuo's injuries, and flung herself directly at Bai Qingli, weeping.

"Your servant was terrified! Mistress, what are we going to do? The General found us!" She rubbed at her tears with one hand and pointed accusingly at Shen Shizhuo in the bed: "It's all your fault for provoking the General!"

Bai Qingli pacified Qiuyue for a while, then sent Chun Ri to take her out of the room. The two maidservants had barely stepped outside when another commotion broke out — the sound of people running somewhere in the night, boots striking the ground, the rhythm of steps coming through the darkness in a fast, precise beat.

That kind of footfall was not made by cloth-soled shoes. It was the sound of good leather boots fitted with iron soles — and at the speed of those trained in martial arts.

That cadence, Bai Qingli's brows drew together as she listened — she recognized it at once as potentially Qin Shanyue arriving with soldiers. She had heard that same sound when Qin Shanyue drilled his troops.

This location had never been particularly hidden. Secluded, yes — but if Qin Shanyue wanted to find it, he could. The thought of Qin Shanyue striking Shen Shizhuo earlier and now coming to bang on their gate with an army — that image made Bai Qingli feel like a cat whose tail had been stepped on, every hair standing on end. She set down the medicine oil, told Shen Shizhuo "stay there" in a firm voice, and walked out.

Shen Shizhuo had absolutely no intention of letting Bai Qingli face Qin Shanyue alone. He suppressed his unease and agitation, waited for Bai Qingli to step out, then immediately rolled off the bed, went to the window, and lifted the wooden frame.

He had intended to slip out quietly, reach the wall ahead of her, and get a look at the situation outside — but when he raised the window, he found himself looking directly into Zhuifeng's face on the other side.

Zhuifeng had been crouching out there for some time, looking at Shen Shizhuo with an expression of profound suffering.

Earlier, in order to cover Shen Shizhuo's escape, Zhuifeng had stayed behind and exchanged several arrows with Qin Shanyue, which was why he had arrived at the courtyard a little later — but he had been behind Shen Shizhuo the whole way. When he reached Fog Forest Courtyard, he had seen Shen Shizhuo tumble off the horse and act weak in front of Bai Qingli.

From the courtyard gate to the bedroom door was only a few steps, yet those two had taken a full quarter hour. Every time Bai Qingli steadied him, Shen Shizhuo practically floated off the ground; the moment he was on the bed, he grabbed her sleeve and called out in pain; the moment she leaned close, the pain vanished; the moment she drew back, his brow furrowed as though he were about to faint from the agony. He had kept Bai Qingli circling around him anxiously the entire time, and when she pulled off his clothes, his fingers had gone and gripped the bedsheets — from the look on his face, he was only one step away from asking her to take a blade to him so she could nurse him through the night.

A grown man, doing every undignified thing possible just to win a woman's attention — saying whatever nonsense came into his head to make it happen!

Such a small injury — barely a scratch on him, probably — and he had the nerve to lie there making noise! Groveling and performing like a stage player! Impossible to look at!

To think that the Prince Duan who had guarded the frontier, killed countless enemies, and never once bent his bones in a lifetime — had produced a son like this!

The family discipline had failed! The age had deteriorated! The people's hearts had grown corrupt! Morals had utterly collapsed!

What had their young master been learning in that pleasure house all this time?!

Those pleasure house boys deserved to be taken out and flogged, the lot of them!

Perhaps Zhuifeng's expression was a little too transparent — practically spelling out in plain characters [so this is the kind of person you are, Young Master] — and Shen Shizhuo was briefly arrested by it, at a loss for words. But Zhuifeng caught himself quickly and bowed with clasped hands: "Young Master, General Qin has come after us. He has brought soldiers and surrounded Fog Forest Courtyard. What do we do?"

Shen Shizhuo's brow tightened: "How many?"

"Two hundred infantry, fully armed, already in position. At this moment, escape is impossible." Zhuifeng bowed his head slightly, posture taut, his tone not especially urgent — in fact carrying a faintly self-congratulatory note: "But this subordinate has already informed Prince Duan's private guard. At the Young Master's word, the private guard will hold General Qin back. Even a second-rank general of the court cannot withstand the forces of Prince Duan's household."

When Shen Shizhuo heard the words "private guard," he frowned. Then he heard "second-rank general" — and his expression darkened further: "The man I fought tonight is a second-rank general?"

"That's right." Zhuifeng had already investigated every detail of Bai Qingli's situation thoroughly — it concerned the Young Master, and this was his first opportunity to lay it all out: "General Qin is the sole surviving son of the Qin family — and now the Qin household's only heir — deep in imperial favor. Before the divorce, Miss Bai was General Qin's wife. They separated only recently. From the General's behavior tonight, it looks as though he may regret it, and currently intends to take Miss Bai back by force."

The moment Shen Shizhuo heard that Qin Shanyue intended to take Bai Qingli back by force, his expression went cold and still, the cool-jade clarity of his eyes filling with a stark, hard edge.

Impossible.

He was not going to hand Bai Qingli over to anyone.

Zhuifeng watched Shen Shizhuo's face carefully and offered, with cautious delicacy: "In that case, there is only one way forward."

* * *

chapters.title: Chapter 35
chapters.content:
"What way?" Shen Shizhuo's brows drew together as he looked at Zhuifeng.

"With General Qin's power and standing, only Prince Duan's household can hold him back." Zhuifeng ventured this carefully, then immediately added: "Young Master — blocking General Qin is not something that can be solved by borrowing the private guard once. Qin Shanyue, if he intends to take Miss Bai, will come day after day, time after time. What the Young Master needs is a sufficient title and standing — only Prince Duan's household can keep a first-rank general of the court in check."

The implication of Zhuifeng's words was plain: if Shen Shizhuo wanted to hold Qin Shanyue back today, he would have to acknowledge his connection to Prince Duan's household — acknowledge his identity as Prince Duan's son.

But he had not yet come clean to Bai Qingli about any of this. What if she were angry with him?

Seeing Shen Shizhuo hesitate, Zhuifeng gritted his teeth and, with quiet ruthlessness, added a final nudge: "Young Master — are you really going to stand there and watch Miss Bai be carried off by that General Qin? From what the General was like tonight, if he truly takes Miss Bai away, do you think she would fare well? She'd likely be locked up and given a good beating for a few days — and some would even drown her in a pig cage."

Shen Shizhuo's back went rigid.

He could see it clearly — this was an open gambit. Every gain and loss was written out in front of him in plain terms. If he wanted to protect Bai Qingli, he needed to stand against Qin Shanyue. If he wanted to stand against Qin Shanyue, he needed commensurate power and status.

His expression was cold and dark. He turned it over in his mind, listening to the noise outside growing louder — and then closed his eyes briefly and said: "Go."

In this moment, it was as though Prince Duan's words had suddenly become clear to him.

Without power in your hands, you cannot even protect the person you love.

You cannot place the safety of the one dearest to you in another person's control and hope for their mercy.

What you want — you have to take it yourself.

* * *

When Bai Qingli walked out of Fog Forest Courtyard's gate, she found the entire perimeter ringed by two rows of soldiers. The rear rank held torches. The front rank had dropped to one knee, both hands drawing bows taut, arrows pointed directly toward Fog Forest Courtyard. At a single word from Qin Shanyue, those arrows would split the gate.

Qiuyue had heard the noise and was standing frozen against a tree, too frightened to move, half-reliving the dizzying shock of her first visit to the pleasure house. Chun Ri had summoned her courage and was standing just behind Bai Qingli, watching the gate.

Qin Shanyue sat astride a black horse in full military bearing. He turned his head as she stepped out, wheeling the horse to face her, looking down at her from above.

The horse's dark mane swept a curve through the air. In the distance the torches lit the night bright, and when Bai Qingli pushed open the wooden gate and saw those flames, the hand holding the door ring trembled. The ring slipped from her grip, and the wooden door swung back in the cold October wind and struck her lightly on the shoulder with a thud.

So familiar.

As though the events at the Qin family's old estate in the snowy mountains from her previous life were being replayed — except last time it had been a servant woman who surrounded the place; this time it was Qin Shanyue himself.

And at that moment, Qin Shanyue sat on his horse looking back at her.

The moonlight was cold and bleak. The lacquered wooden gate groaned open, and a slender figure emerged — fragile as a willow in the wind, her face like white lotus root pulled clean from still water, fresh and pale. The moonlight fell across her face, and as she raised her eyes, her expression calm and cool and composed, every torch flame around her went still for an instant.

Qin Shanyue felt as though he had crossed lifetimes.

He had not been back in the capital more than a month or so — and yet the world he had lived in for decades seemed to have been turned on its head. From some point he couldn't quite name, everything around him had become unrecognizable. The woman who had been his wife for three years was now living in the same courtyard with someone else. She had come out to meet him with nothing in her eyes but distance and cold, and when her gaze met his, he saw it clearly: contempt.

Qin Shanyue felt a chill to his teeth, followed immediately by a fury that rolled like lava.

In the time he had been waiting, he had already had the man's identity investigated.

A kept man.

A kept man whom Bai Qingli had purchased from the pleasure house on Qilin Street for five hundred taels of silver. To get that silver, Bai Qingli had even sold off some of her own dowry jewelry — and she had done this while they were not yet divorced.

The thought of Bai Qingli and this man inside this courtyard, carrying on in secret, exchanging whispered affections in the places he couldn't see — it made him feel as though fire had been lit inside his skull.

He and Bai Qingli had been married three years. Aside from bringing Zhao Hongzhu home, he had never in any way wronged her. Other men kept concubines, kept maids as companions — he had none. And even his bringing Zhao Hongzhu back had, at the start, been no insult to Bai Qingli in his own mind.

But Bai Qingli — she had been carrying on with some other man behind his back. And not just any man — a man of the lowest standing, a kept man with nothing but underhanded tricks!

Qin Shanyue stared at Bai Qingli as she came through the gate as though he wanted to tear through her skin and see the workings of her heart.

He had expected her to be afraid when she saw him. After all, he now knew about her shameless conduct, and her life was practically in his hands — she could have been on her knees begging him for mercy and it wouldn't have been too much to ask. But when Bai Qingli looked at him, there was not the slightest trace of fear.

"Qin Shanyue." Bai Qingli tilted her delicate jaw upward, her eyes holding his from below. In front of drawn arrows, under the light of torches, those eyes didn't flinch or retreat. She even stepped forward two paces, and with a composure utterly free of fear, said in a voice that rang clean and clear: "You and I have already divorced — we have no further ties to each other. As a current first-rank official, you have secretly mobilized troops and come to surround my estate. You have brought soldiers against a private citizen. Are you treating the laws of this court as nothing — bullying people with the power of your military authority? Are you not afraid I will bring a complaint before the Court of Judicial Review?"

Her words rang through the courtyard gate and out into the night, the kind that made one's spine go straight with something like awe. But she had underestimated what a man's possessiveness over a woman could do to his reason.

To Qin Shanyue, even though Bai Qingli had divorced him, she had once been his woman. Whatever grievances and entanglements there were between them, those were matters between the two of them — no one else had any right to touch her. He had a feeling toward Bai Qingli of [she's mine to discard but no one else can have her]. If she remarried he would feel unsettled, might even move to interfere — he didn't want her, but no one else should have her either; ideally, Bai Qingli would be ground down by the cruelties of life until she had no choice but to come crawling back to him.

But she had not merely remarried — she had been carrying on with some kept man while they were still married, treating him as though he were nothing, living her life free and easy outside, not giving him a moment's thought, only thinking of running away with someone else, even walking the lantern street hand in hand with the man — it enraged Qin Shanyue beyond all endurance. His chest felt as though a burning coal had been wedged inside it, both scorching and aching at once. He was humiliated, and he had been played, and at this moment he would not have stopped even if the Emperor himself were standing here.

"Take her."

Qin Shanyue's hands clenched the reins, the tendons on the back of his hand standing out sharply. His eyes were dark and vicious, his voice cold and hard: "Anyone else inside — kill them."

No exceptions.

"Qin Shanyue!"

Bai Qingli was struck through with alarm: "You are a first-rank general of this court! You are a general — how can you take lives at will? The Qin family's traditions are built on honor — how did your father raise you? Do not use military might to bully people! Do not abuse power against commoners! How can you do this?"

After so many years of knowing Qin Shanyue, this was the first time she had ever heard him speak like this. She had believed before that he had simply lost his head over Zhao Hongzhu — that it was a lapse of private virtue, nothing more. She had not imagined he could use his power to move against ordinary people.

This was a violation of the law.

"Taking lives at will? You dare speak of that — when you divorced me for that man's sake, did it ever occur to you that it might come to this! You refused to be the honored Mistress of the Qin household — you insisted on falling to this kind of place to be trampled on. This is your own doing!" Qin Shanyue's voice was low and ice-cold. Something seemed to cross his mind, and he gave a cold, contemptuous laugh, all fury and frost: "A kept man — a creature of the lowest station, who uses degraded tricks to seduce a respectable woman into divorcing her husband — you call that a person? Killing him would be no different from killing a dog."

The blood rushed to Bai Qingli's face — half outrage, half a burning sense of humiliation.

She had brought the mute man back for no reason other than to repay a debt from her previous life. From beginning to end, she had only ever thought of him as someone she could lean on and trust — important to her, but nothing with any ambiguous undertone. She had never thought of him in the way one thought of a kept man— She had been about to say "the mute man and I are completely innocent of any impropriety" — but then she remembered the way Shen Shizhuo had looked at her just now, and the words caught in her throat. She changed course midway and said instead: "When I divorced you, he and I were entirely innocent — there was not the slightest impropriety between us."

The expression on Qin Shanyue's face became near-contorted: "So now you are no longer innocent?"

The words stopped Bai Qingli cold for a moment — and in that moment, Qin Shanyue caught the flicker of her hesitation with absolute clarity. Jealousy blazed through him.

Bai Qingli was not someone who lied easily. Her nature ran cool and composed, and though she appeared delicate, she had always owned what she did. If she had declared with absolute certainty today that "nothing has ever happened between me and that kept man," Qin Shanyue might have let the man live for now and investigated afterward. But that moment's hesitation — it landed on Qin Shanyue like a slap directly across the face, burning away the last of his reason in an instant. He drew an arrow and set it to the bow. The bowstring hummed, a sharp whisper of sound, and the arrow drove hard into the wooden gate — catching the corner of Bai Qingli's skirt where the wind had billowed it outward, pinning the fabric to the wood.

Bai Qingli leapt back in fright. With a ripping sound, a patch of pale blue fabric was left behind, skewered to the gate by the arrowhead. She had just retreated back inside the gate when she heard Qin Shanyue give the command.

"Take Bai Qingli alive. Kill the rest."

On those words, the soldiers outside sharpened their eyes all at once. A unified shout of "Kill!" went up, one voice from two hundred throats, shaking the night sky, making the skin crawl.

Bai Qingli was already throwing the bolt on the gate. As she drew the bar across, she called out: "Run! Chun Ri, Qiuyue — you two go out the back gate. Don't worry about me."

Chun Ri had gone white with fear. She turned and grabbed Qiuyue and ran toward the back gate. Qiuyue clutched a tree trunk and wailed that she couldn't run and they should leave without her — while Bai Qingli was already sprinting toward the back of the courtyard.

She had never imagined Qin Shanyue could be this recklessly brutal — mobilizing military forces out of private interest, using them to crush a civilian household. The Qin Shanyue she remembered had never been like this.

The proud, upright young general she remembered had become something she could no longer recognize.

The battle cry was thundering at her back. Bai Qingli hoisted her skirt and was about to run — when from outside the gate, another wave of sound erupted, enormous and rising.

Bai Qingli stopped in her tracks. She looked sharply toward the gate.

A moment ago the gate had been under repeated assault — but the pounding had stopped. Instead she heard the clash of blades and the sounds of people fighting. Bai Qingli listened for a moment, brows furrowed, and then from beyond the gate came Qin Shanyue's voice, raised in a shout: "Prince Duan's private guard — why do you come here to obstruct me? Attacking a first-rank general without sanction — does Prince Duan intend to rebel?"

chapters.title: Bai Qingli held her skirts bunched in one hand, frozen mid-motion as though she had been about to run back to the bedroom. She stared hard at the gate.
chapters.content:
As the daughter of an official family who had also married a second-rank general, she naturally understood Prince Duan's position at court. In the past, when she still paid visits to some of the Qin family's collateral branches, she had heard quite a bit about Prince Duan from their mouths.

Prince Duan was now forty-five years old — in the very prime of maturity — and commanded tens of thousands of elite soldiers. To this day he had never married, had no wives or concubines, no children. Bai Qingli had even heard people discuss some scandalous speculation: that Prince Duan was impotent, which was why he never took a wife and remained stationed at the frontier year-round.

Da Feng had been founded through military strength — an empire won on horseback. Most of the old generals at court were Prince Duan's sworn brothers-in-arms. Even Qin Shanyue's father, the late General Qin, had grown up alongside Prince Duan. The two of them had trained in martial arts together from childhood and were inseparable confidants who would have died for each other. After they grew up, Prince Duan guarded Da Feng's eastern border against the coastal raiders, while General Qin guarded the western border against the barbarian tribes. They could only meet in the capital during the New Year, when they would drink themselves into oblivion and sleep side by side.

When old General Qin died on the battlefield, Qin Shanyue had not yet come of age — he was still just a slender youth. When the other generals at court could not hold back the barbarians, it was Prince Duan who crossed the entire breadth of Da Feng, wrested his friend's body from the barbarians' hands, and personally carried the coffin — walking eight thousand li through clouds and moonlight, thirty battles through dust and earth, mixed with the wind and sand of the frontier and the blood and tears of soldiers — all the way back to the capital.

But all of that was ancient history now. Once old General Qin was gone, Prince Duan's tea had gone cold. In the years since, Prince Duan had remained stationed at the western frontier battling the coastal raiders, rarely returning to the capital. The connection had faded. Only some of the old guard still remembered.

Qin Shanyue was younger and had some impression of Prince Duan, but his memories were hazy. With the passage of time and the entanglement of various interests — particularly the Zhao family affair — there was little kinship left to speak of between them. When Prince Duan's private guard arrived, Qin Shanyue's first reaction was that Prince Duan meant to kill him.

Recently he had been investigating the Zhao family case and had uncovered many secrets. He had been in frequent contact with the Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard. With Prince Duan's network of eyes and ears, he would naturally have detected the momentum Qin had been building over the years. Recently Qin had also been working with the Vice Minister of War to push for the Zhao family's rehabilitation. From Prince Duan's perspective, Qin Shanyue was a blade poised at his throat — one that could fall at any moment. It made perfect sense for Prince Duan to want to eliminate him.

But this was the outskirts of the capital — still within the capital itself, at the foot of the Son of Heaven. Even if Prince Duan truly wanted to kill him, he would never choose this location.

Yet from the distance, what had come charging in was indeed Prince Duan's private guard.

The kind of private soldiers kept by veteran generals were mostly battlefield veterans with a hundred or more kills to their names. In ordinary times they looked no different from the private guards kept by nobles and officials — but the moment they picked up bows and drew heavy blades, that piercing killing intent spread instantly, and even the night seemed to darken.

"General Qin jests." A hearty laugh rang out from the distance, wrapped in the sharp ring of blade tips, echoing through the night sky: "Clearly it is General Qin who has sent men to surround Prince Duan's territory. This humble one would like to ask the General — for what reason?"

Qin Shanyue's brow furrowed as he looked toward the speaker.

He recognized him. The man was called Zhuifeng, a child born into Prince Duan's household who had grown up on the eastern front fighting the coastal raiders. His father had been Prince Duan's personal guard and died saving the Prince, so Prince Duan had raised him personally from childhood, keeping him close as if he were half a son. Though only around twenty years old, he was already Prince Duan's right hand.

His presence here meant Prince Duan placed great importance on Fog Forest Courtyard.

Qin Shanyue's frown deepened.

He could not figure out what connection Bai Qingli could possibly have with Prince Duan. The Bai family were new nobles at court who knew well how to protect themselves and never dared involve themselves in Prince Duan's affairs. And Bai Qingli was merely a sheltered woman — what connection could she have with Prince Duan?

Various relationships and recent events flashed through Qin Shanyue's mind. The capital was like a great web woven by a spider — every thread connected to people and events — but he could find no point of intersection between Bai Qingli and Prince Duan.

At that moment, Zhuifeng had already ridden his fast horse through the battling guards and positioned himself directly before the gate of Fog Forest Courtyard.

He faced Qin Shanyue with his back to the courtyard, taking a protective stance. His tone was respectful, but the blade in his hand yielded not an inch. If Qin Shanyue dared advance one step, that blade would fall.

"This is Prince Duan's territory?" Qin Shanyue fixed his gaze on Zhuifeng, but his blade pointed at the gate: "The one living here is my household's divorced wife, Bai Qingli. What business is she of Prince Duan's?"

Zhuifeng was not foolish enough to reveal Shen Shizhuo's identity. He simply smiled and deflected, invoking Prince Duan's authority to intimidate Qin Shanyue: "Our master's orders — we lowly ones do not understand them. In any case, this is Prince Duan's territory. The General had best withdraw immediately. Otherwise, even if this reaches the Emperor's ears, Prince Duan's household would be in the right."

Naturally Qin Shanyue would not back down. He gave a cold laugh and swung his blade.

Zhuifeng met him head-on without evasion.

While the two of them fought, Bai Qingli had moved a ladder to the courtyard wall and climbed up to look outside.

Earlier, Chun Ri and Qiuyue had checked the back gate and found it also surrounded. Fog Forest Courtyard was now ringed on all sides — escape was impossible. But the people outside were divided into two groups: one was Qin Shanyue's private guard, the other Prince Duan's. The two factions were locked in fierce combat. Bai Qingli didn't dare open the gate, so she simply watched from the wall.

The night was deep and dark. In that dense blackness she could only see the wavering torchlight and the gleam of blade edges. Shouts of battle were everywhere. Only because she had died once before did she dare risk random arrows and look out at such a moment.

Qiuyue had long since gone weak in the knees. She sat by the ladder hugging her knees and sobbing. Chun Ri had somehow found a fire poker and gripped it with a deathly pale face.

The battle lasted about a quarter-hour. Both sides had reached the point of bloodshed and serious injury when the Imperial Guard finally arrived on horseback from the main road. The leader held up an iron tablet proving his identity and shouted as he rode: "Stop! The Emperor summons you both — stop at once!"

Prince Duan's household and General Qin — the two great powers at court — were in a precarious situation. Both were secretly exerting force over the matter of rehabilitating the Zhao family, using every underhanded tactic behind the scenes. But on the surface they had always maintained mutual respect, each afraid the other would catch them in a mistake. So when the Imperial Guard received word that Prince Duan's and the Qin household's private guards were fighting on the outskirts of the capital, they hastily requested an imperial decree and rushed over.

The Imperial Guard were the Emperor's personal attendants — the Emperor's hands, the Emperor's voice, the Emperor's will itself. Their arrival caused Prince Duan's and the Qin household's guards to separate instantly.

No one dared act recklessly before the Imperial Guard. They would report everything they witnessed truthfully to the current Emperor. The higher one's position and power, the more careful one had to be.

With the Imperial Guard's arrival, the battle was forcibly interrupted. Bai Qingli, perched on the wall, watched helplessly as everyone present was led away. She wanted to hear what the Imperial Guard asked them, but the distance was too great — she heard nothing. She only saw Qin Shanyue lead his men away first with the Imperial Guard, and then the remaining group also departed. For some reason, neither side seemed to care about her. The leader of the Imperial Guard merely glanced casually at her on the wall and made no mention of her.

The Imperial Guard who arrived later could certainly guess that something in this estate had provoked the dispute between Prince Duan and the Qin household. But since Qin Shanyue didn't mention it and Prince Duan didn't mention it either — both sides remaining tight-lipped — the Imperial Guard naturally wouldn't ask. He was only responsible for bringing them to the palace for the Emperor to judge. Whatever person could make these two great figures fight was beyond what a small Imperial Guard could afford to provoke. Better to pretend not to see.

Bai Qingli watched helplessly as they all left.

Her mind was unsettled. In this crisis she immediately decided to pack up and flee. She planned to run to West Street first, investigate Prince Duan's affairs, and check on her identity documents. If worst came to worst, she could pay for protection.

Today's events — both Qin Shanyue's actions and Prince Duan's inexplicable involvement — frightened her.

But when she packed her bundle, brought Chun Ri and Qiuyue, supported Shen Shizhuo, and opened the back gate to slip away — they were blocked.

The ones blocking them were Prince Duan's men, dressed in dark blue fitted clothing with iron wrist guards bearing carved tiger heads. Upon seeing Bai Qingli, they clasped their hands together with a sharp sound and bowed.

"Greetings, Miss Bai."

Bai Qingli stopped in her tracks. Behind her, Qiuyue gave a startled cry and grabbed Chun Ri. Only Shen Shizhuo, standing at the back, looked through the three women with a cold expression and warning intent at the men blocking the way.

The private guard blocking the gate bowed his head lower, his posture more cautious.

"How do you know me?" Bai Qingli's hand was hidden in her sleeve, palm gripping a cold dagger.

Prince Duan's protection and intervention had come inexplicably. This had never happened in her previous life. Bai Qingli couldn't understand it, so she was especially wary.

Prince Duan — that single character for "Prince" was enough to keep everyone in the Bai household from lifting their heads. The longer she spent in this world of fame and profit, the more she understood that such people could not be provoked. She could not recall ever drawing Prince Duan's attention. Had she done something after her rebirth to attract him?

But no matter how she thought about it, since her rebirth she had only acted in private household matters. As for other state affairs — like the Nanling floods — she had never leaked a single word. Everything had followed the trajectory of her previous life. Where could she have attracted Prince Duan's notice?

Could it be that her rebirth had been exposed?

She had heard that Prince Duan kept a group of gifted individuals who could divine fortunes, calculate fate, and even refine elixirs. Could they have discovered her differences?

The more Bai Qingli thought, the more alarmed she became. Cold sweat made the dagger in her palm slippery. She could only grip harder, her knuckles ice-cold and painfully tense.

"In answer to Miss Bai — it is our young master's wish." The man maintained his respectful posture, his voice resonant: "Our young master once received kindness from you. Seeing you in difficulty today, he hastily dispatched us to come to your aid."

He paused, then added: "Moreover, the Qin household's men have not gone far — they are watching from a distance. It seems they will not rest until they catch you. If you wish to leave, why not allow us to escort you?"

When Bai Qingli heard the private guard say "received kindness from you," she even suspected her ears were failing her and she could no longer understand speech.

Someone of such high position and power — what kindness could she possibly have given him?

Behind her, Chun Ri stood with her face tense, trying to look intimidating but actually unable to move. Qiuyue, on the other hand, had started muttering the moment she heard "received kindness from you": "Love at first sight..."

Bai Qingli had no time to deal with her foolish, stubborn maidservant and whatever she was mumbling. She ignored Qiuyue's mutterings, stared at the private guard for a moment, then asked: "Your young master — a young master of Prince Duan's household? Which one?"

There was only one Prince Duan in Prince Duan's household, and Prince Duan had never married. The Da Feng imperial family had few heirs — all were of imperial blood. Moreover, Prince Duan was clearly not the type to settle down peacefully. He might rebel any day. So even if other families had sons, they wouldn't bear to have them adopted into Prince Duan's line. Prince Duan's branch had always been a solitary stem, on the verge of extinction. How had a young master suddenly appeared?

"These matters — wait until Miss Bai meets the young master. He will explain everything." The private guard maintained his respectful stance, clearly having no intention of explaining further. He simply stepped aside briskly, assuming an open posture that showed he would not obstruct them.

Bai Qingli stood in place, her delicate face slightly cold.

She did not believe what Prince Duan's household said. But at present she was in an extremely passive position. Whether she believed or not made no difference to her current situation.

Her gaze traveled far in the direction the private guard had pointed — toward the village entrance, by two crooked trees. Indeed there were two shadowy figures loitering there. Those were the private guards Qin Shanyue had left behind.

Though both leaders had left, their watchers remained. Even if she really did leave Fog Forest Courtyard now, it would be useless. These people were watching her constantly. She couldn't escape at all.

Bai Qingli stood biting her lip for a moment.

October nights in the capital were bitterly cold. The bone-piercing north wind lifted the hem of Bai Qingli's robe. She looked at the oppressively dark sky in the distance and the shadowy figures. Finally, gritting her teeth, she turned and walked back into Fog Forest Courtyard.

In any case, she had already been caught. Fleeing anywhere would be useless. She didn't know why this young master of Prince Duan's household had rescued her, nor who he was. But since she was the one who had been rescued, whatever schemes the young master had would naturally lead him to seek her out.

Before she entered, she glanced back once more at the distant figures and the nearby private guards, then without another word returned to the courtyard.

Shen Shizhuo was the first to follow. Chun Ri came in worriedly clutching their bundle. Only Qiuyue stood alone at the gate, seeming to ponder something. After thinking for a while and still not figuring it out, she froze in place.

Chun Ri had to turn back and pull her: "What are you standing there for? Come in quickly!"

Only then did Qiuyue snap out of it. As they stepped through the gate, she whispered secretively to Chun Ri: "'Rakish Young Master Pursues Divorced Lady at Night, Coy Resistance Shakes Half the Bed' — I've read that story. That young master must have taken a fancy to our mistress, so he found an excuse to come help her."

The private guard had not expected to hear such audacious words. He looked up in shock.

Chun Ri didn't dare look at the private guard's face. She slammed the back gate shut with a bang, then turned her head: "When I get back, I'm definitely making the mistress burn all your storybooks!"

What on earth is barking around in that dog brain of yours!

Qiuyue paid no attention, immersed in the fantasy [so my mistress is the story heroine after all], unable to extricate herself.

According to the story's next development, the rakish young master and the faithless general would fight jealously over her! And then our mistress would have them both at her side, opening a full harem!

Qiuyue's shoulders trembled with delight.

Worthy of my mistress indeed!

Meanwhile, Bai Qingli had already returned to the bedroom. Her expression was too cold, making Shen Shizhuo somewhat uneasy. He followed behind her step by step, his voice tight as he asked: "Do you... do you dislike Prince Duan's household?"

* * *

chapters.title: Bai Qingli's mind was turning over the connection between Prince Duan's household and herself. The more she couldn't figure it out, the more she needed to think through it carefully. Her hands and feet were cold, but a fire burned in her chest, leaving her unable to rest for a moment.
chapters.content:
Hearing Shen Shizhuo's words, she forced the corners of her lips into a smile.

It wasn't that she disliked Prince Duan's household. She had no grievances with them, recent or old. Today she had even benefited from Prince Duan's help, for which she should be grateful. She simply didn't like this feeling of things spiraling beyond her control — of being fish on someone else's cutting board. Being trapped here, listening to two forces clash outside while she herself could do nothing — it reminded her of her previous life, of the fury and despair she felt when surrounded and burned to death.

Once a person was caught in the vortex of power, they would be swept along, constrained. When a tornado rose, the leaves caught inside had no power to choose.

"It's nothing. Don't be afraid. Prince Duan's household is fine. I don't dislike them." When Bai Qingli turned back, she saw Shen Shizhuo's beautiful phoenix eyes drooping slightly, making him look like a puppy whose fur had been drenched. She forced herself to spare some attention to comfort him, coaxing him to go rest: "You're injured too. Go rest. I will protect you. I'll handle these matters — don't worry."

Perhaps because she had been reborn once, though she was clearly not older than Shen Shizhuo, she always felt she had experienced more and knew more than him. So whenever she spoke with Shen Shizhuo, she carried an indulgent, older-sister tenderness that even she herself hadn't noticed. Especially today after Shen Shizhuo was injured — her gentleness toward him seemed inexhaustible. Even with a pile of worries unresolved, she tried hard to treat Shen Shizhuo well.

But Shen Shizhuo showed no sign of feeling reassured or comforted. He stood behind Bai Qingli and gave a muffled "mm," then stepped backward toward the door, one step at a time.

He kept backing up to the doorway. Bai Qingli never turned around.

His boots had already bumped against the wooden threshold. One more step back and he would leave the warm, candlelit bedroom and enter the cold moonlit courtyard of Fog Forest.

He lowered his eyes and slowly pulled the wooden door closed. When the door shut, the person inside thought he had left — but he hadn't. He simply stood quietly outside the door, listening to the sounds within.

The cold moonlight fell across his face, coating his ink-black hair with a pale gleam. His bone structure was refined, his features cool, his brows heroic — but his lips were cherry-pink, like a plum blossom emerging from snow in a winter courtyard. The colder his expression, the more striking that touch of pink became. The October wind billowed his sleeves as he stood in place like an abandoned crane about to die on a withered tree.

His goddess had not looked down on him with compassion. She was frowning as she pondered today's events, unable to spare him even half a glance.

Who was she thinking about?

Whether as Shen Shizhuo or as the young master of Prince Duan's household, neither seemed able to smooth the furrow between Bai Qingli's brows. She seemed to have many things weighing on her mind. She had her own path. No one could influence her. No one could change her.

Shen Shizhuo stood still for a moment, then finally walked back to his own room in silence.

From Bai Qingli's room to his required passing through a stretch of fog forest and the kitchen and Chun Ri and Qiuyue's room. As he walked, he heard the two maidservants whispering inside their room, probably discussing today's events. When he reached the fog forest, he saw a path of light — lanterns that Chun Ri had hung on the trees earlier. These lanterns dutifully lit the way, illuminating his path whenever he walked at night.

The candlelight was warm, deliberately positioned to avoid the wind. Occasionally a flame would flicker, and looking ahead he could see his room in the distance.

Shen Shizhuo stood before the forest, feeling his feet heavy as lead, his chest stuffed with a leaden weight that dragged painfully at his heart.

He didn't like seeing Bai Qingli unhappy, and he didn't like her thinking about others. But he had no way to make Bai Qingli happy, and no way to make her think only of him.

He began to miss the earlier moment when Bai Qingli had tended his wounds — when she lowered her head to gently apply medicine to his injury, her expression tender, a strand of ink-black hair falling softly against his waist. If only time could stop in that instant. Every time he looked up, he would see Bai Qingli's face.

But the wheels of fate rolled relentlessly forward, forcing everyone to scramble ahead whether they wished to or not. So many people would emerge to compete for Bai Qingli's attention. In her heart, he would never be the one who occupied everything.

Shen Shizhuo felt endless bitterness in his chest, as though a hole had been hollowed out. All joy leaked away, leaving only lingering sadness, loss, and grievance.

When he had first been left at the pleasure house, Bai Qingli hadn't existed in his world yet, so he hadn't cared. But now, somehow — though only a few days had passed — he couldn't withstand even the smallest ripple. He had tasted sweetness here, tasted what it was like to spend days and nights with Bai Qingli, and his heart had lost all sense of direction. Bai Qingli only stirred the water's surface a little, barely wetting her fingertips — but on his side, seas were already overturning. He was like a crane seeing the Milky Way for the first time, desperately flapping his wings to get closer, only to be thoroughly drenched, the feathers on his head hanging wet and limp, standing in the cold wind, chilled to the bone.

"Young Master! Young Master!"

Just as Shen Shizhuo stood before the fog forest, Zhuifeng came running from the distance, lowering his voice and carefully bowing: "This subordinate has just returned from the palace with news from the Master. Do you... do you wish to hear the latest situation?"

When he approached from afar, he had seen Shen Shizhuo standing before the fog forest, surrounded by a chill even colder than the moonlight. For a moment he hadn't dared approach. But this was a critical moment to summon the young master back to the estate — he couldn't hold back. He could only steel himself and approach.

"Speak." After a long moment, Zhuifeng heard Shen Shizhuo's voice — hard and cold as shattered ice.

"Just now, after this subordinate led the private guard in battle against General Qin, I entered the palace and was granted audience. I only told His Majesty it was the Master's order. But General Qin had already revealed the matter of Miss Bai." At this point, Zhuifeng cautiously glanced at Shen Shizhuo. Seeing his expressionless face, he added: "His Majesty's people have also been secretly searching for you. Finding you is now only a matter of days. With General Qin causing such a commotion today, His Majesty will certainly pay attention to Fog Forest Courtyard — and to you. Your identity cannot remain hidden, so the Master chose to be direct."
