Shen Shizhuo said nothing, but he could imagine what that confrontation in the palace must have been like.

Both His Majesty and Prince Duan carried buried wounds in their hearts — wounds that looked healed on the surface but concealed rotting flesh and foul white pus beneath. Both sides guarded their past love, hate, and grievances, pulling against each other. And Shen Shizhuo's existence was like a blade that, taking advantage of this lively lantern festival, emerged from nowhere and sliced through all that unbearable history, spilling filth across the palace's golden bricks and glazed tiles, suffocating everyone within.

The calamity buried twenty-some years ago had finally raised great waves today. Tonight not only would the Emperor on the dragon throne be sleepless — even the Empress in Kunning Palace, the Crown Prince in the Eastern Palace, and the Empress Dowager in Cining Palace would all lie awake. The moment they closed their eyes, they would remember: that woman from south of the Yangtze had once given birth to a child.

After a pause, Zhuifeng added: "His Majesty's intention is that the day after tomorrow at the palace banquet, he wishes you to attend. Your whereabouts have been exposed — naturally a day must be chosen to verify your identity."

The day after tomorrow happened to be the Empress Dowager's sixtieth birthday — what should have been a joyous occasion. But with Shen Shizhuo's sudden emergence, the Empress Dowager would likely find no joy in it.

Shen Shizhuo stood before the fog forest, staring at a wind-lantern. After a long while he asked: "What about him?"

Zhuifeng's mind turned quickly. He immediately understood: "He — General Qin knows nothing of your identity. He only thinks you're a kept man. The Master did not reveal your identity at court either. He only said that you once fell on hard times and received kindness from Bai Qingli, so he ordered us to protect this courtyard. General Qin has no idea that Prince Duan's heir and Shen Shizhuo are the same person."

He paused, then added: "From General Qin's manner, he seems still unable to forget Miss Bai. Before His Majesty, he once stated his intention to take Miss Bai back. It was only later, when the Master mentioned your existence — news weighty enough to shake the court's foundations — that General Qin was momentarily distracted and stopped mentioning Miss Bai. But in the future, he will undoubtedly come looking for trouble."

Shen Shizhuo thought of Qin Shanyue's appearance.

Qin Shanyue had a handsome face, excellent birth, and a record of battlefield achievements. Such a man must have been quite dazzling in the capital. He had once been Bai Qingli's husband. Why had Bai Qingli cast him aside?

Shen Shizhuo's silence went on too long, making Zhuifeng uneasy. He considered the young master's state of mind, thought for a moment, then ventured tentatively: "General Qin and Miss Bai have been divorced for some time. Earlier, he even petitioned His Majesty for an imperial marriage decree — he intends to marry the young lady of the Zhao family."

When Shen Shizhuo heard "the young lady of the Zhao family," he suddenly remembered the cup of tea Bai Qingli had purchased at that West Street teahouse — the information about two people.

One named Qin Shanyue. One named Zhao Hongzhu.

"The young lady of the Zhao family?" His voice when he spoke was hoarser than even he expected. He asked: "Who is the young lady of the Zhao family?"

He had a strange premonition that this person was very important.

"The young lady of the Zhao family—" Zhuifeng momentarily couldn't gauge whether Shen Shizhuo wanted to hear about the conspiracy entanglements between the Zhao family and Prince Duan's household, or about the romantic affairs between Zhao Hongzhu and Qin Shanyue. But he only paused for an instant before decisively choosing the latter.

"The young lady of the Zhao family was originally Qin Shanyue's betrothed." Zhuifeng quickly recounted the story of Zhao Hongzhu and Qin Shanyue: "The Zhao family was implicated in treason. All adult males were executed, but women and young children escaped with their lives. Zhao Hongzhu was exiled to the northern desert, and her engagement to Qin Shanyue was called off. But in recent years, the Zhao family case is being reopened. Qin Shanyue brought Zhao Hongzhu back from the northern desert. After he brought her back, he kept her at the Qin estate. According to our spies' intelligence, the two had already become intimate within the estate. Miss Bai and General Qin had many conflicts, with some chaos in the Bai family mixed in as well. In the end, Miss Bai divorced General Qin and moved out alone."

Shen Shizhuo's vision swam. The moonlight filled Fog Forest Courtyard, illuminating the desolation.

So it wasn't because she liked him that she divorced her husband. It was because her husband was entangled with someone else. He was nowhere near as important as he'd thought.

Then what was his purpose?

Had Bai Qingli seen his face, found him pleasing, and bought him back for temporary amusement — to relieve her loneliness after the divorce, someone to transfer her affections to?

Or perhaps he was just a tool for Bai Qingli's revenge against Qin Shanyue. Qin Shanyue was entangled with someone else, so she had to go find a kept man from a pleasure house too?

That was why, when she bought him back, she had allowed him to stay in the courtyard alone, not at all afraid he would escape.

Bai Qingli didn't like him that much at all. Even if she did, it was probably only a little — like keeping a small dog. When she remembered, she'd pat it a couple times. When she was annoyed, she'd toss it aside. Keeping him didn't cost much anyway. If she got tired of him, she could just go to the pleasure house and pick another one. She wasn't short of money — her back courtyard rooms were stacked with silver. Whenever she wanted, she could take anyone home.

Zhuifeng had barely finished speaking when he saw Shen Shizhuo move. He crossed the path lit by lanterns and walked straight back to his room, his manner cold and wordless. Zhuifeng couldn't quite read the young master's thoughts, but his report wasn't finished yet, so he could only continue following to report.

"The Master's intention is that you return to Prince Duan's estate tonight. Your current identity is no longer suitable for staying here. If you're worried Miss Bai will be harmed, why not simply bring her back to the estate? Prince Duan's household will absolutely not mistreat Miss Bai. Then General Qin will have no further excuse to obstruct her. Miss Bai will certainly be able to live freely in our Prince Duan estate."

Zhuifeng could see Shen Shizhuo's feelings for Bai Qingli clearly. When he said "absolutely not mistreat Miss Bai," he meant to keep her in comfort — fine clothes, jade ornaments, servants in abundance. Once this storm passed, if Shen Shizhuo still wished it, he could give Bai Qingli a proper status.

After all, Da Feng women could remarry. Though most women who remarried married down — not only bringing substantial dowries themselves but also facing some disdain from their husband's family. It was extremely rare for a remarriage to be a step up.

Prince Duan's household commanded immense power and stood even more noble and glorious than the Qin estate. Marrying in would let Bai Qingli leap to the very top in one step. She would have a status that all women in Da Feng envied.

After Zhuifeng finished, he waited confidently for Shen Shizhuo's response. But when he looked up, Shen Shizhuo was simply looking at him with cold, indifferent eyes.

Zhuifeng's heart tightened. He didn't dare continue.

After a moment, he heard Shen Shizhuo ask: "Would Prince Duan's heir be better than General Qin?"

The question came from nowhere, but thinking of the white lotus hairpin Shen Shizhuo had clutched all the way home, Zhuifeng understood what he was asking.

In Bai Qingli's heart, would Prince Duan's heir be better than General Qin?

He hastily said: "Naturally. The heir is of noble birth — the finest man in the world. Miss Bai must have suffered some indignities during her time divorced from General Qin. If she were with you now, wouldn't that be infinitely glorious? Miss Bai would surely be delighted."

Shen Shizhuo lowered his eyes and slowly shook his head.

He didn't think so. He and Bai Qingli hadn't spent much time together, but he knew: Bai Qingli didn't like power and glory. If she did, she never would have divorced Qin Shanyue in the first place. She wanted to leave the capital and find somewhere no one knew her to live quietly.

If not for Qin Shanyue interfering, they would have left in a few days. Bai Qingli didn't want to get involved in any of the capital's treacherous affairs. If he revealed his identity as heir to her now, she might feel he could live well here and leave him behind without a second thought.

Shen Shizhuo pressed his lips tighter. The lustrous pink took on a reddish tinge, bleeding into a rouge color. But his complexion grew paler. He stood in silence for a moment, then said with quiet certainty: "She wouldn't like it."

Zhuifeng was at a loss for words. He stood there with his mouth open, struggling for a long time before squeezing out from his throat: "No matter what, an heir is still better than a kept man."

Better in what way?

Shen Shizhuo couldn't see it. He only knew that when Bai Qingli saw Qin Shanyue come to surround the courtyard, she was merely angry. The matter seemed within her tolerance. But when she learned Prince Duan's household had come to surround the courtyard, she had been like a cat whose tail was stepped on — every hair standing on end.

"I can't let her know I'm Prince Duan's heir."

Zhuifeng could only nod: "Everything is as the heir wishes."

Shen Shizhuo's fingers lightly brushed the collar at his chest, then added: "In three days, when the banquet is held, send someone to ensure Bai Qingli doesn't enter the palace."

Zhuifeng immediately understood — not only could Miss Bai not know he was Prince Duan's heir, but once he turned around he had to ask Prince Duan's household to invite Miss Bai to the estate for a meeting.

But the master's thoughts were the subordinates' goals. Every word Shen Shizhuo spoke, Zhuifeng would remember and work desperately to fulfill. So he gave a crisp martial bow and immediately headed back.

After Zhuifeng left, Shen Shizhuo lay alone on his bed. He pulled the thin quilt over himself, folded his hands across his chest, and quietly closed his eyes.

It's all right, he thought.

Bai Qingli doesn't like Prince Duan's heir. He is Shen Shizhuo — the kept man who was bought back, who got injured and relies on her support, who would cough blood and die without her. He's the mute.

Bai Qingli doesn't like him that much right now — but at least she likes him a little. Otherwise why would she have bought him back specifically and not someone else?

As long as he stayed before Bai Qingli's eyes day and night, he would have more chances than anyone else. At the very least, when Bai Qingli was at leisure, she would reach out to touch him, invite him over to drink wine with her.

What Shen Shizhuo hadn't expected was that the very next morning at daybreak, Qin Shanyue came to Fog Forest Courtyard again.

* * *

chapters.title: The October capital's cold wind cut like knives. The gate of Fog Forest Courtyard was tightly shut. Qin Shanyue stood before it, watching his private guards knock.
chapters.content:
The arrow from last night still remained on the gate, its tip pinning a strip of white silk — making Qin Shanyue recall that moment yesterday when he'd turned on horseback and shot.

Bai Qingli had stood at the gate, facing the firelight, looking at him.

Qin Shanyue's hand gradually tightened around the heavy blade's hilt, his broad knuckles turning pale. His gaze swept inch by inch over this estate, his expression growing grimmer.

He remembered the earth-shaking news he had heard in the great hall yesterday.

The child born of Noble Consort Li — whose blood was either Prince Duan's or His Majesty's — had reemerged in the world. Prince Duan had found him. The day after tomorrow he would attend the palace banquet. Prince Duan had directly claimed the child as his own, while His Majesty, upon hearing news of the child, had set all other matters aside, clearly intent on meeting the child first before discussing anything else.

The reason Prince Duan's household was protecting this small Fog Forest Courtyard was that Bai Qingli had once inadvertently helped Prince Duan's heir when he was in difficulty. So when Qin came to demand her, Prince Duan's people had intervened.

He had merely wanted to bring back his dishonorable divorced wife. He hadn't expected to stumble into imperial family secrets. Now he couldn't touch anyone in this courtyard. Not only Prince Duan's household was watching — His Majesty's eyes were on it too.

But he had keenly sensed that Prince Duan's household's level of concern for Bai Qingli was too high. Even if Bai Qingli truly had helped Prince Duan's heir, there was no need to post guards day and night. Prince Duan's household must have some other designs on Bai Qingli — he just didn't know what.

Qin Shanyue's heart was like several taut strings.

As a man of the court, he naturally knew how dangerous this was. Bai Qingli was just an ignorant woman who had gotten tangled up in court affairs — she would likely be devoured without even bones remaining.

Though he resented Bai Qingli for her infidelity and dissolute days, he didn't want to see her die like this. So today he had come specifically to investigate the situation. At present, only he could extract Bai Qingli from this vortex and save her.

With this thought, Qin Shanyue withdrew his gaze from the arrow. The private guard knocking at the door increased his force, making the wooden gate boom loudly. The sound echoed in the cold morning wind and immediately drew Prince Duan's private guard.

"Stop!" Prince Duan's guards rushed over: "His Highness Prince Duan has ordered that General Qin is not permitted within three feet of this courtyard. If you harm our heir's lifesaving benefactor, Prince Duan's household will fight you to the death!"

Qin Shanyue looked coldly at Prince Duan's private guard, then kicked the man squarely in the chest, sending him flying three meters back to spit blood and collapse.

He commanded a million troops and held the rank of second-rank general. It wasn't for some lowly soldier to shout at him.

The rest of Prince Duan's guards rushed over, blocking Fog Forest Courtyard's gate — but none dared directly confront Qin Shanyue. Without Zhuifeng, they were leaderless and didn't dare fight.

At that moment, Fog Forest Courtyard's gate opened.

Qin Shanyue looked up, expecting to see a flash of blue — Bai Qingli emerging as she had last night. But he saw only white.

The one who stepped through the gate was a man as upright as the fog forest trees, wearing a robe of fine white cloth with a blue sash at his waist. His hair was casually pinned with a wooden hairpin. His features were as cool and clear as mountain mist. His eyes were steady. The moment he opened the door, the heavy scent of pine from Fog Forest Courtyard mixed with the morning's damp air and rushed out.

What immortal bone structure.

The bones in Qin Shanyue's hand that gripped the blade began to itch.

He had never wanted so badly to kill someone — to sever his bones, shatter his knees, carve away every piece of flesh, tie him behind a horse and drag him to death!

The man who opened the gate seemed unaware of this murderous intent. He stood properly behind the gate, raised his hands in a scholar's bow to those outside, and spoke in a modest, gentle tone as clear and steady as mountain streams.

"Gentlemen, Shen just now heard someone knocking. Is there urgent business?" Shen Shizhuo's gaze fell on Prince Duan's guards at the gate as though he didn't see Qin Shanyue at all, addressing only them: "My wife was exhausted yesterday and only just fell asleep this morning. Please keep your voices down."

How would Prince Duan's guards dare accept Shen Shizhuo's courtesy? Though their status was humble and they didn't know who this Shen Shizhuo was, Zhuifeng had ordered them three times over to treat everyone in the estate as their master. So they hurriedly stepped aside, bowing in return. For a moment the atmosphere was remarkably harmonious.

Only Qin Shanyue was left to one side, ignored.

Qin Shanyue had been born to high status and later became a second-rank court general — everywhere he went, people flocked to flatter him. When had he ever been treated so coldly? When Shen Shizhuo bowed to Prince Duan's guards and ignored him, his expression instantly turned iron-dark. And when he heard Shen Shizhuo's words, fury shot straight to the top of Qin Shanyue's head.

On the surface Shen Shizhuo was asking people outside to be quiet and not disturb his wife — but every word revealed his unusual relationship with Bai Qingli. That tone of familiarity and intimacy — as if she truly were his wife!

He was nothing but a kept man who traded on his looks — a man anyone could use, a degraded thing who lay in bed serving people. As a man, instead of seeking to build achievements and serve the nation, he relied on his flesh, surviving by bewitching women. Truly disgusting and base!

This filthy thing even dared to touch Bai Qingli!

Qin Shanyue's eyes flooded red with murderous intent.

Today, even if he had to apologize to Prince Duan's household afterward, he would cut down this kept man who had seduced Bai Qingli into divorce!

The blade flashed like sudden cold light; the figure pounced like a hawk. Qin Shanyue moved too fast — the Prince Duan guards who were still bowing couldn't react. In the blink of an eye, the black blade had reached Shen Shizhuo's throat.

Qin Shanyue was certain his blade wouldn't miss.

He was Da Feng's most valiant young general, a commander who had fought his way through seas of blood and mountains of corpses. This lowly slave might have some fighting skills, but he didn't believe he couldn't kill a mere kept man!

But just as his blade was about to strike, the kept man stumbled backward two steps. The blow that should have taken his life veered slightly off, only slicing through his chest garments and shallowly cutting the skin beneath.

At that moment, the Prince Duan guards at the gate finally reacted, drawing their blades to intercept Qin Shanyue. Instantly steel clashed and voices rose in chaos.

When Bai Qingli was startled awake, threw on her clothes, and rushed over, this was what she saw.

Yesterday's chaos was repeating itself. Qin's men and Prince Duan's men fought in a tangled mass. Qin Shanyue was surrounded but still dangerous, yet he pressed relentlessly toward the courtyard interior.

And Qin Shanyue's blade pointed at Shen Shizhuo, who had fallen to the ground.

Shen Shizhuo wore moon-white scholar's robes today, with a simple white jade crown in his hair. Morning sunlight filtered through the fog forest branches, broken into scattered fragments that fell across his eyes and brows, making his features luminous and dazzling. But his face was deathly pale, lips pressed tight, his sleeve pressed weakly to his chest. His normally upright back was trembling. When a breeze passed, he bent his head and coughed.

As Bai Qingli drew closer, she saw blood on his sleeve!

Great patches of blood soaking through the fabric, staining Shen Shizhuo's hand bones, dripping steadily to the ground and pooling into a small crater of crimson.

That bright red blood stabbed straight into Bai Qingli's eyes. Her heart clenched violently. The scene from her previous life — of the mute covered in blood, pinning her beneath him — suddenly surged up, making her legs go weak, nearly collapsing.

This was her nightmare, her fatal knot, the pain she could never forget in this lifetime. Whenever she thought of the mute being harmed because of her — stabbed multiple times, burned alive in the flames — her chest tightened and she couldn't breathe.

She stood frozen in place. In just a few seconds, her cool, clear face transformed from initial bewilderment to something cold and lethal. She raised her eyes. Through the fluttering hems of clothing and flashing blades, she looked toward the source of it all.

Twice now. Counting the lantern festival before, since her rebirth her mute had been injured twice at Qin Shanyue's hands!

For the first time, Bai Qingli hated being a woman — physically weak, unable to wield a blade, unable to cripple Qin Shanyue's hands!

"You—"

Bai Qingli boldly strode out through the courtyard gate, heading straight for Qin Shanyue. Both Qin Shanyue and the Prince Duan guards hurriedly withdrew, mindful of her presence and not daring to strike. The scene briefly froze into tense stillness.

This was Qin Shanyue's second time seeing Bai Qingli's fury.

The reason was obvious — because he had slashed that man who traded on looks, who could only seduce women.

When Bai Qingli saw that kept man injured, her face went whiter than rice paper on a writing desk. The heartache on her face was completely unconcealed. This reminded Qin Shanyue of their first year of marriage, when he had led troops out of the capital to battle and been wounded. Back then Bai Qingli had circled his bed just like this, her eyes full of distress, pulling at his hand without speaking, only crying.

He had asked her then if she regretted marrying him. He was a general — he might die on the battlefield any day, wrapped in a warhorse's hide, leaving only filthy blood that wouldn't wash clean. But Bai Qingli had held his hand and told him firmly: "I love exactly this kind of man — a general like you."

"The more people the General kills, the more peaceful Da Feng becomes. Most people are shallow — they only see the blood on the General's hands but cannot see the integrity in the General's bones."

"As a child I once thought of defending the nation, but unfortunately as a woman I cannot go to war. Fortunately, I married a man like the General. The General tends to the realm; I will tend to the General."

At the time, he had thought he'd found his soulmate.

The past was like passing smoke. The more he had loved then, the more he hated now. His soulmate had fallen into the mire in just a few years, letting all that filth and foulness stain her through!

Looking at that familiar face, Qin Shanyue couldn't help but laugh in rage.

"What am I doing here? Bai Qingli, do you really think that with Prince Duan's household protecting you, you can indulge yourself here?" Qin Shanyue pressed from outside toward the courtyard gate. His eyes bored into Bai Qingli as though he wanted to devour her whole: "Bai Qingli, I came today to kill someone. I want him dead. He will not live."

"As long as I draw breath, you will not have a moment's peace."

"Watch and see — how many days can Prince Duan's household hold me back."

* * *

chapters.title: It was early morning. Qin Shanyue's blade cut through the shallow mist and damp air of Fog Forest Courtyard, through the clear scent of pine. The killing intent in his words struck Bai Qingli's face, dousing her fury completely.
chapters.content:
In that instant, Bai Qingli experienced what it meant to be chilled to the bone.

Looking at Qin Shanyue's twisted expression, she seemed to see the great fire from before her death.

She had grown too complacent lately.

Successfully leaving the Qin household, successfully taking revenge on everyone, using her previous life's foreknowledge — it had made her think she could grasp fate in her own hands, that she had transcended worldly constraints, escaped confinement, and could handle any problem with ease. But when Qin Shanyue came at her in madness, she suddenly remembered: right now she was nothing but a village woman.

Under this vast imperial authority she was nothing — like a grain of sand. Qin Shanyue could crush her with one finger. So what if he had been unfaithful first with Zhao Hongzhu? So what if he wanted to kill the mute out of baseless jealousy? He was a second-rank general of the dynasty. His reach extended to the heavens. If he truly cast everything aside and relentlessly targeted her and the mute, how long could Prince Duan's household actually protect her? Moreover, she still didn't know what Prince Duan's household was scheming.

Once again she felt the same emotions as before her death in her previous life: fury, resentment, powerlessness.

Bai Qingli seemed to suddenly understand something.

As long as Qin Shanyue remained a general for one more day, as long as she remained a commoner for one more day, she would be the fish and he the knife. Status and position determined her helplessness. The only reason she had been able to leave the Qin household before was because Qin Shanyue no longer wanted to see her. Now that Qin Shanyue was running over in madness because of the mute, she had no recourse at all.

If she had known it would come to this, she shouldn't have waited for those identity documents. She should have fled the capital with everyone early on. Having provoked a madman of power and position, she couldn't even protect herself — let alone her mute.

No. No.

Bai Qingli reconsidered. She couldn't escape anywhere. Qin Shanyue was a second-rank general. If he truly wanted to track someone down, he could mobilize court resources. She, the mute, Qiuyue, and Chun Ri were just a few people — how could they withstand the vast Da Feng?

And she couldn't truly run for her entire life — not daring to see sunlight, not daring to speak her real name, hiding in darkness like a criminal.

Because she had done nothing wrong.

She had done nothing wrong!

A vicious energy coiled in her chest. Bai Qingli thought: why should she be the one to yield? Why should she be the one to avoid him? She and the mute and Qiuyue had never initiated harm! Why should she continue being trampled? Why should the people she cared about keep getting hurt because of her?

She needed to advance, not retreat.

Qin Shanyue wanted to kill the mute — she shouldn't run. She should kill Qin Shanyue first. She should return every wound on the mute's body tenfold, a hundredfold. She should eliminate the root of the problem. She should use Qin Shanyue's blood to settle the debt!

Bai Qingli stood in place with reddened eyes, looking at Qin Shanyue's face beyond Fog Forest Courtyard's gate.

Between them lay only a courtyard gate and a few Prince Duan guards — yet when Bai Qingli looked over, she felt an unbridgeable chasm separated them. Buried beneath that chasm were countless riches, endless power. If she wanted to climb across and stab Qin Shanyue, she needed something solid enough to support her.

What could that be?

Countless complicated thoughts flashed through her mind. Her head buzzed. She seemed to grasp a thread that flashed by, but couldn't quite untangle what it was.

At that moment, Shen Shizhuo's coughing rang out again, startling Bai Qingli back to awareness.

She turned her head and saw Shen Shizhuo cough up another mouthful of blood. The crimson stained his lips a vivid red — especially striking against Fog Forest Courtyard's muted greens and whites. Bai Qingli snapped back to herself. Ignoring Qin Shanyue, she rushed to Shen Shizhuo, helped him up, and brought him toward the bedroom.

"Bai Qingli!" Qin Shanyue's voice still pursued her like a plague: "Where can you run?"

Bai Qingli supported Shen Shizhuo and walked even faster.

At the gate, Prince Duan's guards and Qin Shanyue fought in a tangled mass. Steel clashed repeatedly. Several times Qin Shanyue nearly broke into the courtyard. By the end, Prince Duan's guards no longer dared hold back. The gate of Fog Forest Courtyard rang with the clash of blades and the flash of cold steel.

Bai Qingli's entire attention was captured by Shen Shizhuo's wound. She could spare no thought for anything else. She rushed him to the bedroom, settled him on the bed, then turned to find medicine and bandages, calling loudly for Qiuyue and Chun Ri.

Shen Shizhuo had been badly injured. He lay on the bed seemingly unconscious, making Bai Qingli's nose sting. She sent Chun Ri to fetch a physician, but Chun Ri soon returned to report — she couldn't get out. Bai Qingli had no choice but to send Chun Ri to boil water while she personally stripped Shen Shizhuo and bandaged his wound.

Shen Shizhuo's white robe was soaked through with blood. When she lifted it, it was heavy. Blood stuck to her fingertips — cold and fishy — making Bai Qingli tremble. She tossed the garment to Qiuyue to fetch a clean one, then lowered her head to examine Shen Shizhuo's wound.

Qin Shanyue often went to war and was covered in old scars, so Bai Qingli had some knowledge of treating external wounds. Her first look at Shen Shizhuo's injury brought a sigh of relief.

It wasn't as serious as she'd imagined. The blade had only cut about an inch below the skin — not a vital spot. Fortunately. But the wound was extremely long, slicing nearly across his entire chest parallel to his collarbone. Blood gushed out. Bai Qingli hurriedly applied golden wound medicine and hemostatic powder patch by patch, barely staunching the flow before wrapping it in bandages. Though it was late October, she worked up a sweat.

While she did all this, Shen Shizhuo lay unconscious on the bed. Only after she'd hurriedly finished the bandaging did he wake with difficulty. He seemed to be in extreme pain — even the corners of his eyes were tinged with red. He weakly raised one hand. The moment he moved, Bai Qingli quickly cupped it in both of hers.

Just then Chun Ri finished boiling water and brought it in. Bai Qingli dampened a cloth and wiped Shen Shizhuo's hands finger by finger.

His hand had been pressed to his chest earlier and was also soaked with blood. The blood had dried, sticky and highlighting every line on his fingers. Bai Qingli wiped with the warm cloth, asking as she worked: "Where else hurts? Are there other injuries? Next time you encounter something like this, don't rush forward. Just don't open the door. Qin Shanyue has spent years on the battlefield — you're no match for him. A gentleman doesn't court danger. Don't put yourself at risk again, understand?"

Shen Shizhuo looked at Bai Qingli quietly. Seeing her eyes rimmed with red, a warm current seemed to flow through his heart. The sweetness made him momentarily forget the pain in his chest.

He thought: she did care about him. She would be distressed for him. How wonderful.

Though the relationship might not be what he hoped for — just seeing her worry over him like this was enough to erase all his earlier unhappiness and grievance. At least he still mattered. At least in Bai Qingli's heart, he still held a place, however small.

He lay quietly on the bed as Bai Qingli tended to him, the two of them one above and one below, gazing at each other. For a moment Shen Shizhuo even wanted time to freeze here, wanted to keep being cared for by Bai Qingli forever.

But when Chun Ri finished boiling water and came back in — seeing this scene of deep affection — something felt oddly familiar.

Shen Shizhuo didn't notice anything strange in Chun Ri's expression. He was immersed in his own words, and by the end, a trace of difficult-to-voice shame crossed his face, as though he felt humiliated by having once fallen into the pleasure house.

Bai Qingli had only been worried about Shen Shizhuo's injury moments ago. Now learning that Qin Shanyue had insulted him, she was furious enough that her chest heaved violently. A fire burned there, flushing her normally cool face red.

"Qin Shanyue knows nothing of your character! You were forced into those circumstances — yet he dares insult you like this!"

"Don't belittle yourself. I know your integrity and pride. Don't take any of that nonsense to heart!"

Bai Qingli remembered the first time she'd seen the mute in this life — his face ruined, locked in a small room, beaten until covered in wounds. And in her previous life, the mute had endured having his voice poisoned mute and being beaten half to death and thrown out rather than submit to the pleasure house.

The mute had his own integrity. Though trapped in the swamp, he remained untainted by filth. For such a person to be publicly insulted by Qin Shanyue with such degrading words — how much must it hurt inside?

The more Bai Qingli thought, the angrier she grew at Qin Shanyue and the more her heart ached for Shen Shizhuo. Her movements became gentler still. After cleaning his hands, she even helped him under the thin quilt, then gently brushed her fingertips across his forehead.

"Don't think about those things. Rest first. I'll fetch a physician to examine you in a bit."

As Bai Qingli's hand touched Shen Shizhuo's forehead, he suddenly reached up and grasped her wrist.

The man's palm was broad and burning hot. Bai Qingli's fingers were ice-cold. When ice met fire at her wrist, it sent a jolt through her entire body. In that second, she suddenly remembered Shen Shizhuo winning that white lotus hairpin for her.

His hand was hot. She unconsciously tried to pull back, but Shen Shizhuo held fast. He looked at her intently, as though he wanted to ask something — but his lips moved without sound emerging.

Bai Qingli's heart tightened. She leaned closer: "What is it? What do you want to say? Does it hurt badly?"

"...It's fine." Shen Shizhuo finally managed to force out these words. His normally clear voice had gone hoarse: "As long as you know I'm not that kind of person — as long as you don't mind that I once lived in that place — then I still have somewhere to belong in this world. Let others insult and mock me — I don't care. I know there's still someone in this world who believes in me."

Bai Qingli froze in place, looking at Shen Shizhuo's face — pale from blood loss, his eyes full of hope and unease. She found herself unable to withdraw her hand.

At that moment Chun Ri quietly reminded: "Mistress, I'll watch him. You should go rest."

Bai Qingli tried to pull her hand back again, but the unconscious Shen Shizhuo gripped it like a rare treasure, a final thread of hope. No matter how she tried, she couldn't pry it free. When Chun Ri moved to help, Bai Qingli stopped her: "I'll watch. You go."

Chun Ri took the basin of bloody water and left. When she stepped out of the bedroom into the cold air outside, she suddenly remembered where she'd seen this before.

She felt like she'd read about this in a storybook — the hero getting the heroine to care for him by playing pitiful, saying things like "the general despises my humble status." His methods were quite skillful. He'd won the mistress's heartfelt sympathy.

Chun Ri's expression was complex.

Those who came out of the pleasure house were truly different.

* * *

chapters.title: While Bai Qingli tended to Shen Shizhuo inside the bedroom, Qin Shanyue was in a frenzy outside Fog Forest Courtyard.
chapters.content:
He had watched with his own eyes as Bai Qingli supported that degraded kept man and left. When she helped him up, the man leaned half his body against her shoulder in an intimate posture, then raised his head to look at Qin Shanyue.

The kept man had just been helped to his feet, his chest covered in flowing blood, looking utterly wretched — yet where Bai Qingli couldn't see, his eyes held a faint smile. Through the clash of blades and steel, his gaze met Qin Shanyue's from afar.

Like a victor.

Qin Shanyue went into a rage on the spot, nearly breaking through. The Prince Duan guards all bore some wounds. Both sides' eyes had gone red with fury. When Zhuifeng arrived with reinforcements to stop them, everyone was shocked by Qin Shanyue's injuries.

Several of Qin Shanyue's wounds were dangerously positioned — one more inch and they could have killed him. If Qin Shanyue truly died here, not even all their lives combined would be enough to atone!

"Stop!" After Zhuifeng brought men to intercede, he hurriedly spoke a few placating words and invoked Prince Duan's authority to control the situation. Normally, no matter how angry, Qin Shanyue would maintain surface civility and respond with a few perfunctory words. But today he didn't even glance at Zhuifeng — he simply stared fixedly at Fog Forest Courtyard's open gate.

Inside that gate lay territory he had never entered but deeply loathed.

One day he would stride in and kill everyone, burn every object inside!

Qin Shanyue suddenly wheeled around, mounted his horse, and rode away.

Zhuifeng watched Qin Shanyue depart covered in blood, feeling slightly relieved but increasingly puzzled. His impression of Qin Shanyue had been of someone steady and solemn — you could even say rigid and austere. But these past few days, Qin Shanyue's actions had been eye-opening.

For a woman — to act like a madman, hacking and slashing, covering himself in wounds, then leaving in a rage. Clearly gaining no advantage whatsoever, yet still coming to make a scene. This didn't seem like something a second-rank general would do. Where had that military genius General Qin gone?

He suddenly felt more curious about Bai Qingli.

What kind of woman could bewitch both Qin Shanyue and his own young master, enchanting them both until they were lovesick and heartsore?

With this thought, Zhuifeng gave a soft tsk, ordered the guards to disperse and continue protecting the courtyard, then silently vaulted the wall into the compound.

He had important matters to report to the young master.

* * *

When Zhuifeng entered the courtyard, Qin Shanyue's horse had already reached the street.

He was covered in blood. Entering the capital at dawn, he immediately frightened passersby into screaming. His horse's hooves pounded heavily on the road as vendors scrambled aside in panic.

Commoners were forbidden to gallop through the capital — violators were beaten and fined. Even court officials had to be mindful of those sharp-tongued censors who would submit memorials. Ordinarily, Qin Shanyue would have walked or taken a carriage. But today his chest burned with rage. His whip cracked against the horse's flanks as he charged recklessly through the streets without aim, until the steed found its own way to the Qin estate gates.

The guards at the Qin estate saw Qin Shanyue covered in blood and nearly lost their souls in fright. They rushed to help. Qin Shanyue meant to dismount himself, but when he turned, his arm suddenly gave out and he toppled from the horse.

Fortunately his guard lunged forward, using his own body to cushion the fall so Qin Shanyue didn't hit the ground directly. Another guard urgently called for help. They carried the blood-soaked Qin Shanyue back to the estate.

The Qin estate immediately exploded like oil in water, boiling over.

In earlier years, the Qin household had been prosperous with many sons — four courtyards, over a dozen young men. But later they all died on battlefields, dying until only Qin Shanyue's single branch remained. Their young master would stride out gloriously, then return covered in blood, eventually dying in the estate or vanishing on some distant battlefield. The Qin family had long been terrified.

Sleeping drunk on the battlefield, don't laugh at me — how many return from war since ancient times?

So when Qin Shanyue was carried into the estate covered in blood, everyone was alarmed. Even the Old Madam, who had been in a crazed state for over ten days, suddenly became lucid and urgently ordered people to fetch a physician.

Qin Shanyue was carried to Burnt Book Court — Zhao Hongzhu's territory. The Old Madam gritted her teeth and refused to set foot there. Zhao Hongzhu also kept her face rigid and wouldn't allow anyone in. So only servants ran back and forth, while guards at the gate relayed the medical condition sentence by sentence. The entire Qin estate was pervaded by an atmosphere of household discord and precarious instability.

The physician who had previously forced ginseng broth down the Old Madam's throat came to the Qin estate once more to apply needles, take pulses, and bandage wounds.

"All external injuries — no internal damage. Though it looks serious, the General has a strong constitution. Nothing major. Half a month's rest and he'll be fully recovered. He fainted just now only from excessive blood loss. This old one will prescribe a few tonics. Some nourishment and he'll be fine."

The physician stroked his beard with calm composure, wrote several prescriptions, and left. Zhao Hongzhu attended throughout, then after seeing the physician out, she summoned alone in the hall the servant boy who always stayed close to Qin Shanyue.

The men closest to Qin Shanyue were all battlefield veterans. To put it bluntly, they were inflexible. They respected Zhao Hongzhu as much as they did their own lives and would die for her safety — but they wouldn't listen to a single word she said. All their respect for Zhao Hongzhu stemmed from Qin Shanyue. So Zhao Hongzhu couldn't extract anything from them.

For instance: what Qin Shanyue had been busy with these past days, where he'd gone, where he'd been wounded so badly. No matter whether Zhao Hongzhu threatened or bribed, these men were like sealed gourds. When pressed hard, they would simply clasp their hands and bow, saying in muffled tones: "The General's business is of grave importance. This humble one cannot speak of it. Please ask the General yourself, Madam."

Zhao Hongzhu felt stifled listening to this. She waved them away, sitting alone in the hall while a maidservant came in to report: "The physician says the General will wake tomorrow." Seeing Zhao Hongzhu's apparent unease, the maid added cautiously: "Rosy Sunset Garden sent word — the Old Madam is worried and wishes to move the General there."

Zhao Hongzhu didn't even lift an eyelid: "Refuse them. Anyone from Rosy Sunset Garden need not be acknowledged."

Inside Burnt Book Court, Zhao Hongzhu's word was law. Once she gave the order, people from Rosy Sunset Garden couldn't even see the courtyard. Several guards with blades simply blocked the path. The servant woman who returned reported this to the Old Madam, who was so enraged she nearly toppled backward in her chair. She leapt up and went to fetch her late husband's precious blade to kill someone.

The servant women could only trail behind the Old Madam like a row of rat tails, following her around. When they reached the path to Burnt Book Court they were blocked again. The Old Madam flew into a tremendous rage before being barely coaxed back by several women.

"Tomorrow you must enter the palace."

One woman invoked the current Empress Dowager: "We mustn't keep the Empress Dowager waiting."

At the mention of the Empress Dowager, the old woman came back to herself.

Before marriage, she and the Empress Dowager had been close friends — intimate companions who spent every day together. It was only after they married, had children, and weathered life's storms that their meetings became less frequent.

Through these years of wind and rain, though both the Empress Dowager and she had changed considerably in their respective residences and estates, the affection from those early years remained in their hearts. They were sisters who could tell each other anything.

The old woman suddenly looked toward Burnt Book Court.

From where she stood, she couldn't even see the courtyard walls — but she seemed able to see Zhao Hongzhu's smug face.

The Qin Old Madam nearly died of rage.

Zhao Hongzhu had become a thorn in her eye and flesh. Thinking of how Zhao Hongzhu had done those disgusting, sordid things with other men and now came to harm her son — and that dog son of hers had his heart clouded by something and actually wanted to marry such damaged goods — didn't he find it nauseating!

The angrier she got, the more powerless she felt. That marriage was imperially decreed — she couldn't stop it.

The old woman's fire-hot brain turned twice, then thought of the Empress Dowager.

Tomorrow when she went to see the Empress Dowager, she would beg her to think of a solution.

She had no way to deal with Zhao Hongzhu — but the Empress Dowager surely could come up with good ideas. All these years she'd lived too comfortably in the General's household's inner quarters. The Qin men all had good bones — rarely was anyone lecherous or neglectful of proper wives. Her husband hadn't even kept bed-warmers. Her skills at inner-court intrigue weren't sufficient. Unlike her sworn sister, who had secured her footing in the man-eating palace and step by step ascended to the Empress's position. When it came to tormenting people, her sworn sister had a body full of excellent skills.

The Qin Old Madam immediately wrapped herself in cold fury and returned to her courtyard.

* * *

When the Qin Old Madam returned to Rosy Sunset Garden, it was already midday.

At that hour, Fog Forest Courtyard was utterly quiet.

Inside the bedroom, Shen Shizhuo lay sleeping on the bed while Bai Qingli had also dozed off leaning against him. Chun Ri slowly pushed the door open and quietly woke Bai Qingli.

"Mistress, today you're to meet that Prince Duan's heir."

Bai Qingli rubbed her stiff, aching neck and shoulders, first glancing at the still-sleeping Shen Shizhuo before responding and rising to leave with Chun Ri. There were only two maidservants in this courtyard — Qiuyue and Chun Ri. Going to Prince Duan's estate when she still didn't know what situation she faced, she naturally needed to bring the clever one. She could only take Chun Ri, leaving Qiuyue behind. Worried about Shen Shizhuo, she gave Qiuyue detailed instructions to care for him well, and if he coughed or developed a fever, to quickly fetch a physician.

Actually, after Qin Shanyue left earlier, Prince Duan's estate had already sent a physician to examine Shen Shizhuo. But Bai Qingli was uneasy and insisted on giving instructions.

Qiuyue just kept nodding. After Bai Qingli changed clothes and left, she pushed open the door and glanced at Shen Shizhuo. Seeing him sleeping soundly with a healthy flush to his face — clearly not dying — she didn't bother with him further.

The moment Qiuyue's front foot left, Shen Shizhuo on the bed suddenly opened his eyes, rolled off the bed, climbed out the window, exchanged a look with Zhuifeng who was expertly crouched outside, and the two of them slipped out of Fog Forest Courtyard together.

* * *

When Bai Qingli emerged from Fog Forest Courtyard, Qin Shanyue was just waking up in Burnt Book Court.
